Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Standardising TMS excitability protocols. - Applications: TMS biomarkers/targets for AD/MCI. - Methodologies: PRISMA systematic review + meta-analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: TMS-based diagnostic/therapeutic markers.

Method_Architecture: PRISMA systematic review with random-effects (Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman) meta-analysis of Hedges' g effect sizes across six neuroimaging features and three pairwise MCI-subtype contrasts.
Best_Metric: MTL atrophy aMCI vs NC Hedges' g=-0.84 (p<=0.001, 95% CI [-1.01, -0.68])
Dataset: Synthesis of 50 published neuroimaging studies (MRI/PET/SPECT) identified via PubMed and PsycINFO
Key_Novelty: First meta-analysis distinguishing aMCI vs naMCI neuroimaging via within-study comparisons
Primary_Limitation: 90% of included studies are cross-sectional with high heterogeneity and publication bias (Egger significant for aMCI MTL), limiting causal/longitudinal inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Neuropathological bases distinguishing aMCI from naMCI remain poorly understood, limiting clinical utility of MCI subtyping. - Applications: Early identification, differentiation, and targeted intervention/neurorehabilitation for prodromal dementia subtypes. - Methodologies: PRISMA systematic review with random-effects (HKSJ) meta-analysis of Hedges' g across six neuroimaging features and three pairwise contrasts. - Achievable Outcomes: Quantified subtype-specific effect sizes (e.g., MTL g=-0.84 aMCI vs NC) and identified amyloid burden as the only aMCI-specific abnormality.

Method_Architecture: Frequentist network meta-analysis of 19 RCTs ranking NIBS protocols (rTMS/tDCS/tACS) by SUCRA for cognitive outcomes in MCI.
Best_Metric: SMD 1.52 [95%CI 0.49-2.56] (rTMS-F3F4 global cognition vs sham)
Dataset: 19 RCTs (599 MCI participants) pooled from 7 databases
Key_Novelty: First MCI-only network meta-analysis of NIBS ranking protocols by brain-region target
Primary_Limitation: Few RCTs/patients and weak network geometry (few NIBS-vs-NIBS comparisons) may underpower the analysis.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Which NIBS protocol/target is optimal for MCI cognition; optimal dose-response unknown. - Applications: Non-pharmacological cognitive rehabilitation to delay MCI-to-dementia conversion. - Methodologies: Frequentist network meta-analysis with SUCRA ranking, GRADE, consistency testing. - Achievable Outcomes: Evidence that bilateral DLPFC rTMS most improves global cognition and language in MCI.

Method_Architecture: Multiscale lateralized sample and cross-sample entropy features from rs-fMRI AAL regions classified by a random forest with recursive feature elimination.
Best_Metric: Accuracy 97.47% (AUC 1.00)
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) rs-fMRI
Key_Novelty: Multiscale lateralized brain entropy (LSE/LCSE) functional-complexity biomarker for MCI-AD staging
Primary_Limitation: Single-dataset (ADNI) study with no external validation and near-perfect metrics suggesting possible overfitting.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Lateralization of brain functional complexity in MCI-AD had not been investigated; few fMRI studies of AD lateralization exist. - Applications: rs-fMRI biomarker for staging and diagnosing MCI-AD progression. - Methodologies: Multiscale lateralized sample/cross-sample entropy of AAL regions plus random forest with RFE and 10-fold CV. - Achievable Outcomes: Four-group discrimination at ~97.47% accuracy (AUC 1.00) and identification of 22 lateralized differential brain regions.

Method_Architecture: Connectivity-based Meta-Bands (CMB) algorithm with Louvain GJA community detection on source-level AEC MEG connectivity, plus novel meta-band metrics analysed with bootstrapping and FDR correction.
Best_Metric: DoD standard deviation: statistically significant for all three group comparisons (HC-MCI, HC-AD, MCI-AD), p<0.05 FDR-corrected
Dataset: Private resting-state MEG cohort from Hokuto Hospital and Kumagaya General Hospital (Japan), 161 participants
Key_Novelty: First to frame MCI/AD as a dilution of MEG frequency-dependent connectivity (meta-band) structure
Primary_Limitation: Purely group-difference/correlational analysis with no classifier or diagnostic performance metrics; cross-sectional, single-modality, two-site cohort.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Fixed canonical frequency bands ignore subject-specific oscillatory patterns and pathology-induced frequency restructuring; lack of consensus on network dynamics in AD. - Applications: Potential diagnostic-support biomarker for MCI and AD from resting-state MEG; scalable to new pathological groups without re-computation. - Methodologies: CMB algorithm with Louvain GJA community detection on AEC connectivity; novel metrics TA, AS, DoD, SR, BLZC; bootstrapping with FDR correction. - Achievable Outcomes: Quantification of subtle frequency-dependent connectivity alterations distinguishing HC, MCI, and AD; characterisation of progressive blurring of meta-band structure.

Method_Architecture: Jensen-Shannon Divergence differential-distribution (DDD) classifier with dynamic network biomarker channel selection on fused EEG and EGG signals.
Best_Metric: Sensitivity 96.67% (MCI, EEG-EGG multimodal fusion with DNB channels)
Dataset: In-house West China Hospital MCI dataset (Set A, n=190) and epilepsy dataset (Set B, n=171); registered at Chinese Clinical Trial Register
Key_Novelty: First joint EEG-EGG gut-brain DDD/JSD method for MCI detection with 40% DNB-channel selection
Primary_Limitation: Single-center case-control study with no external/multi-center validation
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No prior research combines EEG and EGG for MCI/epilepsy prediction; gut-brain electrophysiological coupling in disease states is unexplored. - Applications: Convenient community/primary-hospital screening for MCI and epilepsy using few channels (40%) and 5-minute recordings; wearable devices. - Methodologies: Jensen-Shannon Divergence differential distribution (DDD), dynamic network biomarker channel selection, multimodal EEG-EGG fusion, distribution correlation analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: High diagnostic sensitivity (96.67% MCI) with reduced electrode count; identification of prefrontal cortex as key gut-brain coupling region; rationale for modulating GI activity to regulate brain function.

Method_Architecture: Multicenter waiting-list-controlled RCT of manual acupuncture for aMCI with rs-fMRI functional connectivity analysis and GEE/Pearson correlation to clinical outcomes.
Best_Metric: Not reported in source (protocol; planned ADAS-Cog primary outcome, no results)
Dataset: Prospective multicenter aMCI cohort (Chengdu, China), four hospitals; ChiCTR2200062062 — no data yet generated
Key_Novelty: RCT protocol linking acupuncture effect to rs-fMRI functional connectivity changes in aMCI
Primary_Limitation: Protocol only with no results; waiting-list (non-sham) control precludes blinding and specificity inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: The cerebral mechanism of acupuncture for aMCI is incompletely understood; insufficient controlled evidence linking acupuncture effect to functional connectivity. - Applications: Early intervention for aMCI to slow conversion to Alzheimer's disease using integrative/TCM acupuncture therapy. - Methodologies: Multicenter waiting-list-controlled RCT with rs-fMRI functional connectivity analysis and GEE/Pearson correlation of imaging to clinical outcomes. - Achievable Outcomes: High-quality clinical evidence of acupuncture efficacy on cognition plus identification of brain modulation mechanism in aMCI.

Method_Architecture: Sham-controlled randomized tVNS during resting-state fMRI, analyzed with CONN toolbox ROI-to-ROI and whole-brain seed-to-voxel functional connectivity (FDR-corrected).
Best_Metric: ROI-to-ROI connectivity contrast t(48)=3.97, p-FDR=0.0082 (left aSMG to left pSTG)
Dataset: Single-site University of Florida MCI cohort (56 enrolled, 50 analyzed); resting-state fMRI on 3T Siemens Prisma
Key_Novelty: First study of tVNS effects on resting-state functional connectivity in MCI patients.
Primary_Limitation: Small sample, acute-only effects, and absence of AD pathology biomarkers and cognitive outcomes.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether acute tVNS connectivity changes translate to long-term cognitive benefit or disease modification in MCI/AD remains unknown. - Applications: Noninvasive, low-risk neuromodulation intervention for individuals at high risk of converting from MCI to dementia. - Methodologies: Sham-controlled randomized resting-state fMRI with CONN ROI-to-ROI and whole-brain seed-to-voxel functional connectivity analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: Demonstration of afferent target engagement of semantic and hippocampal networks, supporting development of longitudinal therapeutic tVNS trials.

Method_Architecture: Systematic review of 12 randomized controlled trials of rTMS in MCI across six databases (2000-2022).
Best_Metric: 10 of 12 RCTs reported improved cognitive measures vs control
Dataset: Six-database literature search (Medline, Embase, Cochrane, APA PsycINFO, Web of Science, Scopus), 2000-2022
Key_Novelty: Systematic review of 12 rTMS RCTs (345 MCI patients): left DLPFC, 10 sessions improve cognition
Primary_Limitation: Wide variability in rTMS parameters across trials and no quantitative meta-analytic pooling; conference abstract format.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No established treatments for MCI; rTMS parameters lack standardization. - Applications: Non-invasive brain stimulation (rTMS) for memory/cognition in MCI. - Methodologies: Systematic review of RCTs across six databases (2000-2022). - Achievable Outcomes: Evidence that rTMS, especially left DLPFC over 10 sessions, improves cognition in MCI.

Method_Architecture: Narrative mini-review of gamma (40 Hz) tACS studies in MCI/AD with a structured summary table of human and animal evidence.
Best_Metric: Per-study qualitative outcomes (e.g., Dhaynaut 2022: ~2% p-tau burden decrease in 3/4 patients; Benussi 2021: significant RAVL/long delayed recall improvement vs sham)
Dataset: Not reported in source (narrative review of published tACS/gamma-stimulation studies)
Key_Novelty: Mini-review synthesizing gamma (40 Hz) tACS evidence for memory/cognition in MCI/AD
Primary_Limitation: Cited evidence base is small, underpowered pilot/case-series studies with heterogeneous parameters; no quantitative synthesis.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Optimal tACS parameters (frequency, dose, duration, target region; standardized vs personalized) for MCI/AD remain undetermined; effects on pathophysiology not fully established. - Applications: Noninvasive cognitive remediation and memory enhancement in MCI/AD; potential prognostic tool to flag MCI patients at risk of converting to dementia. - Methodologies: 40 Hz gamma tACS (conventional and HD-tACS) targeting precuneus/Pz, temporal lobes, DLPFC, angular gyrus; outcomes via neuropsych testing, EEG gamma power, ASL MRI, PET (tau/amyloid). - Achievable Outcomes: Improved episodic/working/autobiographical memory, reduced tau burden, increased gamma spectral power, and maintained cognitive gains.

Method_Architecture: Whole-brain DTI tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) with voxel-wise GLM permutation/TFCE inference correlating FA to AES-C apathy scores.
Best_Metric: FA-apathy association p<.05 TFCE-corrected; AES-C vs GDS r=0.54 p=.003
Dataset: Single-site University Medical Center Groningen cohort (29 aMCI, 20 healthy controls)
Key_Novelty: First whole-brain TBSS DTI study linking apathy severity to widespread WM FA loss in aMCI
Primary_Limitation: Small cross-sectional sample (29 aMCI); apathy-FA association weakens to a trend when adjusting for Stroop I processing speed.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: WM correlates of apathy in aMCI were unclear with only one prior voxel-based study. - Applications: Identifying imaging biomarkers of apathy that may flag AD progression risk. - Methodologies: Whole-brain DTI with TBSS, GLM permutation testing, TFCE correction controlling for depression covariates. - Achievable Outcomes: Demonstrated widespread FA reductions correlate with apathy severity across commissural, association, and projection tracts.

Method_Architecture: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI with GLM fMRI analysis, ERP old/new RMANCOVA, fMRI-constrained ERP source localization (wMNE), and single-trial EEG-informed fMRI amplitude modulation.
Best_Metric: r/R2=0.14 (p=0.007) LPFC recollection correlate vs memory; late parietal group effect F(1,53)=4.411, p=0.041
Dataset: Single-site community cohort recruited at Affiliated ZhongDa Hospital / Henan Mental Hospital (Southeast University), China
Key_Novelty: First simultaneous EEG-fMRI in aMCI: preserved spatial but disturbed temporal retrieval dynamics
Primary_Limitation: Small, single-site cross-sectional sample without external validation, limiting statistical power and generalizability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Reconciling preserved fMRI retrieval-success patterns with behavioral EM deficits in aMCI; locating temporal sources of impairment. - Applications: Identifying individuals at high risk of cognitive deterioration; multimodal spatiotemporal biomarkers of episodic memory. - Methodologies: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI with fMRI-constrained ERP source localization and single-trial EEG-informed fMRI modeling. - Achievable Outcomes: Detecting disturbed recollection/post-retrieval-control dynamics underlying preserved retrieval patterns, correlating with memory performance.

Method_Architecture: Diffusion spectrum imaging with tract-based automatic analysis (mGFA) and classical ANCOVA/Spearman correlation to relate white matter integrity to memory awareness in MCI subgroups.
Best_Metric: CC-IPL group difference Cohen's d=0.76 (MCI-PA vs HC-NA, p=.001); IFOF correlation rs=-0.41, p=.002 in MCI
Dataset: Single-site sample from National Taiwan University Hospital memory clinics and local communities (87 older adults)
Sample_N_Approx: 87 — 46 MCI / 41 HC (analysis subgroups: 36 HC-NA, 24 MCI-NA, 22 MCI-PA)
Key_Novelty: First DSI white matter connectivity study of memory awareness (anosognosia) in MCI subgroups
Primary_Limitation: Small awareness subgroups and uncorrected significance thresholds in a cross-sectional correlational design limit generalizability and causal inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: White matter pathway correlates and cognitive basis of memory awareness deficits in MCI were unknown and inconsistent across studies. - Applications: Matrix reasoning test and frontal-parietal white matter integrity as potential markers of anosognosia in MCI; informing risk/decision-making management. - Methodologies: Diffusion spectrum imaging with tract-based automatic analysis (mGFA), awareness-based subgrouping via subjective-objective discrepancy scores, ANCOVA and Spearman correlations. - Achievable Outcomes: Demonstrated frontal-subcortical and callosal disconnection underlying poor memory awareness independent of gray matter, supporting a disconnection-syndrome model.

Method_Architecture: Tijms single-subject gray matter network construction from sMRI with graph-theory topological metrics, analyzed via ANCOVA, Rate-of-Change, and partial correlation with cognition and CSF biomarkers.
Best_Metric: r=0.259, p=0.0002 (clustering index vs ADNI-MEM, N=200)
Dataset: ADNI
Sample_N_Approx: 200 — 100 MCI non-converters / 100 MCI converters; each split 50 ApoE4 carriers / 50 non-carriers
Key_Novelty: First study of ApoE4 and progression effects on single-subject gray matter networks in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Only two MRI time points and a small CSF subsample; no classification/predictive model built, limiting risk-stratification claims.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: How ApoE4 and disease progression independently and interactively shape individual gray matter network topology in MCI, and link to CSF/cognition. - Applications: Network-based imaging biomarker to identify ApoE4 MCI carriers at high risk of AD progression and monitor therapy. - Methodologies: Tijms single-subject gray matter networks + graph theory + ANCOVA/Rate-of-Change/partial correlation on ADNI sMRI. - Achievable Outcomes: Topological metrics (clustering index, characteristic path length) that predict memory/cognition and track conversion-related decline.

Method_Architecture: Multimodal CCA with joint ICA (mCCA-jICA) fusing gray-matter volume (sMRI) and fractional anisotropy (DTI) to identify group-discriminative covariant components.
Best_Metric: r=-0.563, p=5.829x10-14 (GM_IC09 mixing coefficient vs MoCA, HC+MCI)
Dataset: Local cohort: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi University of Chinese Medicine and Renai Branch, plus Nanning aged-community centers
Key_Novelty: First sMRI-DTI mCCA-jICA fusion of covariant GM-WM abnormalities in SCD and MCI
Primary_Limitation: SCD/MCI groups not confirmed with AD pathology biomarkers, so groups may be pathologically heterogeneous
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Lack of cross-modal fusion analysis of sMRI and DTI in SCD/MCI; controversial and inconsistent single-modality results. - Applications: Identifying covariant GM-WM imaging biomarkers for early (pre-dementia) cognitive decline. - Methodologies: mCCA-jICA fusion of GMV and FA, group-discriminative IC analysis, correlation with neuropsychological scores. - Achievable Outcomes: More comprehensive understanding of joint GM-WM neuropathological mechanisms in SCD and MCI.

Method_Architecture: Single-voxel 1H-MRS neurometabolite ratios correlated with force-plate posturography using ANCOVA, FDR-corrected Pearson correlations, Fisher r-to-z, and stepwise linear regression.
Best_Metric: left SM1 mIns/tCr vs AP Vcop (TR-EO dual-task): rMCI=-0.569, z=2.56, p=0.005
Dataset: Locally recruited cohort (Lithuanian Sports University; same pool as Vints et al. 2022)
Key_Novelty: First to link regional brain 1H-MRS neurometabolites to posturographic balance in MCI vs HC.
Primary_Limitation: Small, heterogeneous sample with no significant group differences and many uncorrected exploratory correlations.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Neurometabolic mechanisms of impaired balance in MCI and how they differ from normal aging are unknown. - Applications: Identifying brain neurometabolite markers (mIns, tCho, tNAA) of fall risk and compensatory balance control in older adults with MCI. - Methodologies: Single-voxel 1H-MRS combined with force-plate posturography, correlation/Fisher r-to-z and stepwise regression. - Achievable Outcomes: Region-specific predictors of balance and a sensorimotor-compensation hypothesis in MCI.

Method_Architecture: Agnostic multi-modal partial least squares (mmPLS) applied to dual-tracer PET (5-HTT and amyloid) to derive a spatial covariance pattern and subject scores.
Best_Metric: Group difference t=-8.34, P=0.000001, Cohen's f=1.34; 5-HTT-Abeta correlation rs=0.81
Dataset: Johns Hopkins single-site MCI and healthy older adult PET cohort
Sample_N_Approx: 49 in analysis — 22 amyloid-positive MCI / 27 amyloid-negative HC (from 45 MCI and 35 HC studied)
Key_Novelty: mmPLS spatial covariance of 5-HTT loss and amyloid distinguishes MCI and tracks cognition
Primary_Limitation: Small single-site sample with no independent/external validation, precluding biomarker generalization and APOE4 dose analysis.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether serotonin degeneration precedes or follows amyloid deposition in preclinical AD remains unresolved. - Applications: Identifying neurochemical (serotonergic) targets for prevention/treatment and understanding MCI-to-AD progression. - Methodologies: Multi-modal partial least squares (mmPLS) on dual-tracer PET (5-HTT and amyloid) with voxel-wise covariance analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: A spatial covariance biomarker linking serotonin loss and amyloid to cognitive decline in MCI.

Method_Architecture: High-resolution MR elastography of hippocampal subfields with nonlinear inversion, combined with volumetry in linear mixed models and logistic regression / ROC analysis to discriminate aMCI from controls.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.85 (combined CA1-CA2 stiffness + volume)
Dataset: Single-site University of Delaware cohort (83 older adults recruited via flyers/social media; Siemens 3T Prisma)
Key_Novelty: First MRE of individual hippocampal subfields in aMCI; viscoelasticity adds value beyond volume
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional design with a small aMCI group (n=20) and no molecular/histopathological validation, limiting conversion and mechanistic inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Volumetric HCsf measures lack microstructural specificity to early aMCI/AD pathology. - Applications: MRE viscoelasticity as a potential clinical imaging biomarker for early neurodegeneration detection. - Methodologies: High-resolution MRE with NLI, ASHS subfield segmentation, ANCOVA/LMM, logistic regression and ROC analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: Combined stiffness+volume classification of aMCI reaching AUC 0.85, detecting tissue changes prior to atrophy.

Method_Architecture: Longitudinal surface-based morphometry (CTh, FD, GI, SD) on ADNI delta images with two-sample t-tests, regression against ADAS-Cog 11, and TFCE permutation inference.
Best_Metric: FD-ADAS11 association peak MNI x18 y-40 z67, cluster k=1693, pTFCE=0.004
Dataset: ADNI (ADNI1: Complete 2Yr 1.5T)
Key_Novelty: Whole-brain longitudinal FD/GI/SD vs cortical thickness for cognitive decline in aMCI/AD
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective single-dataset (ADNI) correlational design with only two timepoints and no predictive validation; many comparisons raise type I error risk.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Common sMRI biomarkers (cortical thickness, hippocampal volume) do not capture surface-folding complexity or its longitudinal link to cognition. - Applications: Improved neuroimaging-based diagnosis and progression tracking of aMCI/AD by combining volumetric and surface-based morphometry. - Methodologies: CAT12/SPM12 longitudinal surface-based morphometry (CTh, FD, GI, SD) with delta-image two-sample t-tests, regression, and TFCE permutation inference. - Achievable Outcomes: Cortical complexity measures (FD/GI/SD) correlate with cognitive decline in AD where CTh fails, supporting multi-measure neuroimaging biomarkers.

Method_Architecture: Resting-state EEG microstate, spectral, and source-connectivity analysis with group-difference statistics (Kruskal-Wallis/ANOVA, TANOVA) and CSF ATN stratification.
Best_Metric: Hurst exponent SCD vs MCI: p=0.0028, Cohen's d=0.87 (Kruskal-Wallis H=11.05, p=0.0040)
Dataset: PREVIEW prospective cohort (Careggi Hospital / IRCCS Don Gnocchi, Florence, Italy)
Key_Novelty: First use of LZ complexity and Hurst exponent on EEG microstate sequences in an SCD cohort
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional design with small HC (n=19) and CSF subgroup (carriers n=10), limiting power and precluding conversion prediction.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Neural correlates of prodromal AD (SCD/MCI) are unclear and existing biomarkers (PET/CSF) are invasive/costly for screening. - Applications: Non-invasive EEG screening of SCD/MCI populations and candidate biomarkers for progression to AD. - Methodologies: Resting-state EEG with spectral, source connectivity/graph, and microstate dynamics (LZ complexity, Hurst exponent) analyses, plus CSF ATN stratification. - Achievable Outcomes: Microstate temporal-structure degradation reliably separates MCI from SCD/HC and tracks AD-like CSF profile, supporting EEG biomarkers along the AD continuum.

Method_Architecture: VBM-based voxel-wise gray-matter Z-statistic atrophy maps computed against age-specific (and amyloid-stratified) cognitively-normal reference groups, classified via ROC.
Best_Metric: AUC 1.0 (ADNI, total GM, age-specific 10-year brackets); AUC 0.985 (independent validation, MTL)
Dataset: ADNI (ADNI-GO/ADNI-2) plus independent University of Cologne in-house validation sample
Sample_N_Approx: 260 — ADNI: 131 CN / 91 MCI (Table 1 totals); validation: 19 CN / 19 MCI
Key_Novelty: Fine-grained age-specific MRI references beat amyloid-negative references for CN-vs-MCI detection
Primary_Limitation: Reference and test data drawn from the same ADNI sample, likely inflating the perfect AUC=1.0; small (19/19) external validation cohort.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Distinguishing age-related from neurodegeneration-related GM atrophy at the MCI stage where signals overlap. - Applications: Clinical MRI-based atrophy quantification to support MCI diagnosis. - Methodologies: VBM Z-statistics with age-specific reference groups, amyloid stratification, ROC/DeLong analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: Near-perfect CN-vs-MCI discrimination (AUC up to 1.0 ADNI, 0.985 validation) using fine-grained age matching.

Method_Architecture: Random forest classifier with SHAP on FLAIR MRI volume/intensity/texture biomarkers and z-score composite indices, with statistical and Cox survival analysis.
Best_Metric: Accuracy 69.2% (sMCI-cMCI), AUC 69.0%; NC-AD Accuracy 86.2%, AUC 87.0%
Dataset: ADNI, CCNA, ONDRI (three multicentre dementia cohorts)
Sample_N_Approx: 1856 subjects (ADNI 978 / CCNA 369 / ONDRI 509); cross-sectional analysis N=1356, longitudinal analysis N=4707 scans
Key_Novelty: First FLAIR MRI biomarkers + composite indices for sMCI-cMCI conversion across 3 multicentre cohorts
Primary_Limitation: cMCI labeled by MoCA progression rather than confirmed AD diagnosis; modest sMCI-cMCI accuracy (69.2%) with small balanced MCI subgroups
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Reliably distinguishing converting MCI from stable MCI early, using routinely-acquired explainable imaging. - Applications: Patient stratification, clinical-trial cohort selection, early AD risk monitoring via routine FLAIR MRI. - Methodologies: CNN-based FLAIR biomarker extraction, z-score composite indices, random forest + SHAP, Kaplan-Meier/Cox survival analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: 86.2% NC-AD and 69.2% sMCI-cMCI accuracy, conversion signal detectable ~4 years pre-diagnosis, biomarkers validated against CSF p-tau/Aβ.

Method_Architecture: Semi-automated 3T hypothalamic volumetry combined with VBM, cortical thickness, and source-based morphometry structural covariance analysis.
Best_Metric: Cohen's d=1.12 (CN vs AD HV), d=0.58 (CN vs MCI); ANOVA p<0.0001
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative)
Key_Novelty: Semi-automated HTH volumetry shows early hypothalamic atrophy in MCI covarying with AD regions
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional ADNI sample with small amyloid subgroups and measurement uncertainty between segmentation methods, precluding causal/temporal inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Accurate volumetry of small subcortical structures like the hypothalamus; whether hypothalamic atrophy is primary or secondary in AD. - Applications: Early imaging biomarkers for the AD continuum including MCI; understanding metabolic/autonomic comorbidity in AD. - Methodologies: Semi-automated seed-growing HTH volumetry, VBM/CTH, source-based morphometry structural covariance networks. - Achievable Outcomes: Detection of early hypothalamic atrophy in MCI and mapping of its covariance with AD-vulnerable regions.

Method_Architecture: Random-effects (two-level mixed-effects) meta-analysis computing Hedge's g standardized mean differences of EEG microstate duration, occurrence, and coverage between MCI/AD patients and healthy older adults.
Best_Metric: SMD Hedge's g=0.462, p=0.002 (MCI microstate A coverage)
Dataset: Pooled data from 12 published resting-state EEG microstate studies (PubMed-sourced)
Sample_N_Approx: 1073 — 293 MCI / 346 AD / 434 HC (final pooled; abstract states 1347 across 448 MCI/514 AD/385 HC)
Key_Novelty: First meta-analysis pooling EEG microstate temporal parameters across MCI and AD vs controls.
Primary_Limitation: Small-to-medium effect sizes and substantial methodological heterogeneity across the 12 included studies, precluding direct biomarker use.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: EEG microstate findings in MCI/AD are inconsistent and not yet usable as reliable diagnostic biomarkers. - Applications: Early functional biomarkers of cognitive decline along the AD continuum from resting-state EEG. - Methodologies: Random-effects meta-analysis of standardized mean differences (Hedge's g) of microstate duration/occurrence/coverage. - Achievable Outcomes: Confirmed gradient-like increase in microstates A/B and decrease in C/D, suggesting compensatory verbalization/visualization in MCI/AD.

Method_Architecture: Group x electrode two-way ANOVA on visual oddball ERP components (N1/P2/N2/P3) under three emotional stimuli with sLORETA 3D source reconstruction.
Best_Metric: P3 latency under Happiness group effect F(2,133)=15.90, p<0.001, partial η2=0.19
Dataset: Primary single-site cohort from psychiatric clinics and communities in Zhejiang, China (150 participants)
Key_Novelty: Happiness-evoked P3 latency delay and right IFG hypoactivation as early ERP signs of MCI
Primary_Limitation: No diagnostic classifier/accuracy; cross-sectional, medication uncontrolled, education imbalance between groups
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Attentional mechanisms under external emotional stimuli in MCI/AD are poorly understood; no robust early electrophysiological MCI marker. - Applications: Early detection of MCI/AD via emotion-modulated visual oddball ERPs. - Methodologies: 32-channel ERP (N1/P2/N2/P3), group x electrode ANOVA, sLORETA source localization. - Achievable Outcomes: Happiness P3-latency delay and right-IFG hypoactivation as candidate early signs of MCI.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease (2024) 11(5):1325-1338

Method_Architecture: Cox and Laplace survival regression of DTI-ALPS glymphatic index against MCI incidence and MCI-to-AD progression, with VanderWeele mediation analysis of Abeta/tau and cognitive biomarkers.
Best_Metric: HR 0.501 (95% CI 0.356-0.706) for AD progression per 1 SD ALPS increase
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative)
Key_Novelty: First study linking DTI-ALPS glymphatic index to MCI onset and MCI-to-AD progression with mediators
Primary_Limitation: Single dataset (ADNI) with no external validation; multi-scanner DTI variability and manual ALPS measurement.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Lack of non-invasive glymphatic biomarkers and unknown role of glymphatic dysfunction across the CN-MCI-AD continuum. - Applications: ALPS index as a prognostic/prevention biomarker to identify individuals at risk of MCI and AD progression. - Methodologies: DTI-ALPS quantification, Cox and Laplace survival regression, restricted cubic splines, VanderWeele 2-stage mediation analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: Risk stratification showing higher ALPS delays MCI onset ~3.8y and AD onset ~3.5y, with quantified pathological mediation.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease (2025) 12:100156

Method_Architecture: Data-descriptor article releasing a preprocessed 4-channel (Fp1, Fz, Cz, Pz) olfactory-oddball EEG dataset with ICA-based cleaning and MMSE scores for HC/aMCI/AD groups.
Best_Metric: Not reported in source
Dataset: Olfactory EEG Dataset (Mendeley, DOI 10.17632/sgzbgwjfkr.5); recorded at Ziaeian Hospital, Tehran, Iran
Key_Novelty: Public 4-channel olfactory-oddball EEG dataset across HC, aMCI, and AD with MMSE scores
Primary_Limitation: Small per-group N (7 aMCI), only 4 EEG channels, and no analysis/classifier results (dataset descriptor only)
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Identifying early EEG/olfactory biomarkers distinguishing MCI/AD from healthy aging. - Applications: Brain connectivity, ERP, ERSP, phase coherence, and time-series analyses on olfactory EEG responses. - Methodologies: Olfactory oddball task with odorant delivery; 4-channel EEG; ICA preprocessing; MMSE-based diagnosis. - Achievable Outcomes: A shared benchmark dataset enabling comparative HC/aMCI/AD olfactory-response studies for early AD diagnosis.

Method_Architecture: Continuous Morlet-wavelet MEG spectral analysis with Riemannian-geometry covariance modelling, logistic regression, and a multimodal linear stacking classifier combining MEG, MRI and clinical features.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.84 (95% CI 0.78-0.92, logistic regression Model 4); multimodal stacking AUC=0.81 (SD=0.12)
Dataset: BioFIND (MEG + MRI, MRC CBU Cambridge and CTB Madrid sites)
Sample_N_Approx: 117 — 64 AD progression / 53 stable MCI (from BioFIND; multimodal classifier subset n=104)
Key_Novelty: MEG 16-38 Hz beta power + Riemannian covariance as non-invasive biomarker for MCI-to-AD progression
Primary_Limitation: Small single-cohort sample with site-progression collinearity and no external/EEG validation
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Need for non-invasive, affordable, synapse-sensitive biomarkers to predict MCI-to-AD progression; methods-related variance across EEG/MEG spectral studies. - Applications: Screening of large MCI populations; monitoring response to AD disease-modifying treatments. - Methodologies: Continuous Morlet-wavelet spectral analysis, Riemannian-geometry covariance modelling, logistic regression, multimodal stacking classifier with CPI variable importance. - Achievable Outcomes: Combined MEG+MRI+clinical model AUC=0.81 (stacking) / 0.84 (logistic regression) for predicting AD progression.

Method_Architecture: Statistical group-comparison and correlational analysis of auditory-task EEG/ERP components and iCOH functional connectivity in MCI, early AD, and HC.
Best_Metric: eta2=0.406 (SSW accuracy group difference, p<0.01)
Dataset: Primary cohort from First Affiliated Hospital and Mental Health Center, Zhejiang University School of Medicine (enrolled Feb 2021-Feb 2022)
Key_Novelty: First EEG/ERP + connectivity study of SSW and auditory n-back CAP tasks in MCI/early AD
Primary_Limitation: Small single-center cross-sectional sample (n=69) with no predictive model or validated diagnostic metric
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Distinguishing MCI from HC via auditory processing biomarkers; decoding the meaning of SSW-evoked ERPs and the apparent neural compensatory mechanism. - Applications: Early non-invasive recognition of MCI/early AD and identification of non-pharmacological intervention targets for central auditory processing. - Methodologies: EEG/ERP (P1-N1-P2, P3) plus iCOH functional connectivity (CPL, global efficiency) combined with SSW and auditory n-back behavioral tasks and correlational/ANCOVA statistics. - Achievable Outcomes: Group-level discrimination signals (eta2 up to 0.406) and significant connectivity-cognition correlations (p<0.01) that could feed a future MCI recognition model.

Method_Architecture: DCE-MRI with Patlak pharmacokinetic modelling to extract regional BBB permeability (PS) and B1-corrected T1, compared between MCI and SCI cohorts using non-parametric statistics.
Best_Metric: Hippocampus PS group difference: MCI 1.13 (0.99) vs SCI 0.42 (0.57) x10^-3 min^-1, p=0.019
Dataset: CANN trial UK-arm DCE-MRI sub-study (University of East Anglia; NCT02525198)
Key_Novelty: First DCE-MRI comparison of BBB leakage and T1 between MCI and SCI cohorts
Primary_Limitation: Very small, imbalanced sample (only 1 MCI-active subject) with no healthy controls, severely limiting statistical power.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Distinguishing subtle BBB leakage in SCI/MCI from healthy aging requires highly sensitive protocols; large literature variability in DCE-MRI metrics. - Applications: Early diagnosis and treatment monitoring of pre-dementia cognitive impairment via microvascular integrity imaging. - Methodologies: DCE-MRI with Patlak pharmacokinetic modelling, DESPOT1-HIFI B1-corrected T1 mapping, FastSurfer segmentation, signal-drift correction. - Achievable Outcomes: Regional BBB leakage (PS) and T1 can differentiate MCI from SCI in limbic memory regions, motivating larger confirmatory trials.
study_design_type: cross_sectional (nested sub-study of a randomized controlled trial)

Method_Architecture: Automated FLAIR-based WMH volumetry combined with NPI-Q assessment, analyzed using longitudinal mixed-effects models and correlation plots with FDR correction.
Best_Metric: r=0.169, p=0.008 (baseline whole-brain WMH load predicting change in future NPI total score)
Dataset: National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) Uniform Data Set
Key_Novelty: Quantified WMH load longitudinally predicts worsening neuropsychiatric symptoms in MCI-AD and AD
Primary_Limitation: Only baseline MRI available (no follow-up scans), small effect sizes, and null cross-sectional associations limit causal/clinical inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Inconsistent and inconclusive literature on whether WMH burden relates to neuropsychiatric symptom development and progression in MCI/AD. - Applications: Identifying vascular contributors to NPSs to justify aggressive vascular risk factor treatment in MCI-AD and AD. - Methodologies: Automated FLAIR WMH segmentation, NPI-Q symptom assessment, longitudinal mixed-effects models and correlation analyses with FDR correction. - Achievable Outcomes: Baseline WMH load predicts future worsening of total NPS, delusions, hallucinations, depression, irritability, and agitation in MCI-AD and AD.
Journal: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging (2021) 6:70-78

Method_Architecture: Quantitative spectral EEG (FFT) across wake and sleep states with a synthetic slowing index, compared by FDR-corrected ANOVAs and correlated with MMSE via Pearson's r.
Best_Metric: r=-0.53, p=8.00x10^-12 (T5 REM EEG slowing vs MMSE)
Dataset: Single-centre clinical cohort (Foundation Policlinico Universitario A. Gemelli IRCCS and University of Rome Sapienza), not a public dataset
Key_Novelty: First joint wake-and-sleep EEG analysis in one AD/MCI/HC cohort; REM slowing best tracks cognition
Primary_Limitation: No amyloid/tau biomarker or clinical follow-up to confirm AD pathology or identify MCI converters; cross-sectional correlational design.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether wake EEG slowing reflects neurodegeneration or homeostatic sleep drive, and whether it shares mechanisms with REM slowing. - Applications: Non-invasive EEG biomarker for AD/MCI staging and disease progression monitoring. - Methodologies: Topographic spectral EEG analysis across wake-sleep states with a synthetic slowing index and FDR-corrected ANOVAs/correlations. - Achievable Outcomes: REM-sleep slowing index as a sensitive, homeostasis-independent marker correlating with cognitive decline.

Method_Architecture: Narrative review qualitatively comparing reported sensitivity/specificity of biomarkers versus neurocognitive assessments for MCI-to-AD conversion prediction.
Best_Metric: Verbal episodic memory combined sensitivity 74.5% / specificity 77.1% (Belleville 2017, cited)
Dataset: No own dataset; reviews cited studies, many using the ADNI database
Sample_N_Approx: Not reported in source (narrative review; no own cohort)
Key_Novelty: Narrative review arguing cognitive tests match biomarkers' MCI-to-AD prediction at lower cost
Primary_Limitation: Non-systematic narrative methodology with no predefined search/inclusion criteria and no quantitative pooled analysis, risking selection bias.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No single biomarker or cognitive test reliably predicts MCI-to-AD conversion; standardized cutoffs and validated batteries are lacking. - Applications: Lower-cost MCI-to-AD conversion prediction in low/middle-income clinical settings using neurocognitive assessment. - Methodologies: Narrative literature review compiling sensitivity/specificity/accuracy/effect-size metrics from molecular, radiological, and neurocognitive studies. - Achievable Outcomes: Multi-domain cognitive batteries validated across diverse populations could match biomarker accuracy at lower cost and invasiveness.

Method_Architecture: Group-ICA and ROI-to-ROI resting-state fMRI functional connectivity analysis (CONN/SPM12) comparing MCI subgroups stratified by a composite small vessel disease burden score.
Best_Metric: TFCE=48.05, p-FDR=0.044 (vermis VIII - right cerebellum connectivity)
Dataset: Health-RI Parelsnoer Neurodegenerative Diseases Biobank (PND), a Dutch multicenter cohort
Sample_N_Approx: 68 — 34 MCI absent/low SVD burden / 34 MCI high SVD burden
Key_Novelty: First rs-fMRI study using a comprehensive SVD burden score within an MCI-only cohort
Primary_Limitation: Small, ethnically homogeneous, sex-imbalanced sample (N=68) with no cognitive/motor outcome linkage or longitudinal follow-up.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: The role of SVD in dementia development and which brain regions SVD affects at the MCI stage remain incompletely understood. - Applications: Identifying cerebellar/thalamic/caudate connectivity as potential targets/biomarkers for SVD in cognitively impaired individuals. - Methodologies: Group-ICA and ROI-to-ROI rs-fMRI connectivity (CONN/SPM12) with a comprehensive 0-4 SVD burden score and TFCE/FDR correction. - Achievable Outcomes: Demonstrated higher cerebellar and thalamo-caudate connectivity/activity in low-SVD vs high-SVD MCI individuals.

Method_Architecture: Linear regression, Pearson correlation, and ROC analysis relating the CAIDE vascular risk score to cognitive scores and volumetric MRI measures (gray/white matter, hippocampus, WMH) in amnestic MCI.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.70 (total brain gray matter volume predicting high CAIDE)
Dataset: ADNI
Sample_N_Approx: 226 amnestic MCI (final sample after removing outliers from initial 243)
Key_Novelty: First study to examine CAIDE risk score vs WMH and brain volumes specifically in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional, no controls, no longitudinal or molecular data; modest clinic-based sample limits causal inference and generalizability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether vascular risk scores reflect WMH versus gray matter changes in established MCI is unclear. - Applications: CAIDE-based risk stratification to identify MCI patients for targeted neuroimaging and therapy. - Methodologies: Linear regression, Pearson correlation, automated WMH segmentation, ROC with Youden's J, FDR correction. - Achievable Outcomes: Identification of gray matter and hippocampal volumes as stronger CAIDE correlates than WMH (AUC 0.70 vs 0.52).

Method_Architecture: Comparative interventional study of frequency-specific transcranial photobiomodulation (Alpha 10Hz vs Gamma 40Hz) plus cognitive training across four MCI phenotypes, assessed with MoCA/PSQI/BAI/IADL.
Best_Metric: MoCA significant improvement (no numeric value reported)
Dataset: Clinical cohort of MCI patients recruited at Istituto di Neuroscienze, Firenze, Italy (N not stated)
Key_Novelty: Phenotype-specific tPBM frequency: Alpha vs Gamma differs by MCI subtype; PSQI predicts Alpha
Primary_Limitation: No sample size, control arm, or quantitative statistics reported (conference abstract).
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No reliable clinical predictors of Gamma protocol response were identified; mechanisms of frequency-specific tPBM effects remain unclear. - Applications: Non-pharmacological neuromodulation for early intervention in MCI to delay or prevent cognitive decline. - Methodologies: Frequency-specific tPBM (10Hz/40Hz) plus cognitive training over 30 sessions, with phenotype stratification and multi-domain clinical assessment. - Achievable Outcomes: Personalized treatment matching stimulation frequency to MCI phenotype, using sleep quality as a response predictor.

Method_Architecture: Spectral dynamic causal modeling with parametric empirical Bayes on longitudinal resting-state fMRI, with VBM-driven ROI selection across 7 LC and cortical nodes.
Best_Metric: Effective connectivity (Hz): left rostral LC→parahippocampal cortex +0.08 (95% CI 0.03 to 0.13) in aMCI; left rostral→caudal left LC −0.14 (CI −0.05 to −0.20)
Dataset: Single-site Bellvitge University Hospital (Barcelona) cohort; resting-state fMRI, two timepoints 2 years apart
Key_Novelty: Longitudinal spDCM of locus coeruleus effective connectivity in aMCI and late-life MDD vs HC
Primary_Limitation: Small, partly overlapping groups (7 MDD also had aMCI) and uncorrected VBM threshold limit specificity and generalizability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: How LC noradrenergic dysfunction evolves and whether it compensates or degenerates across early neurodegenerative and depressive trajectories; reasons for left lateralization. - Applications: Non-invasive LC connectivity as a biomarker of noradrenergic dysfunction in aMCI and late-life MDD at risk of AD. - Methodologies: Spectral DCM with parametric empirical Bayes on longitudinal resting-state fMRI, combined with data-driven longitudinal VBM ROI selection. - Achievable Outcomes: Mapping group-by-time effective connectivity changes revealing both connectivity reductions and compensatory increases in LC networks.
Journal: Spanish Journal of Psychiatry and Mental Health (2025) 18:199-207

Method_Architecture: Letter to the Editor providing a narrative critical review of an spDCM resting-state fMRI effective-connectivity study of the locus coeruleus in late-life MDD and aMCI; no original analysis.
Best_Metric: Not reported in source
Dataset: Not reported in source (commentary, no dataset; references Maturana-Quijada et al. 2024 cohort)
Key_Novelty: Letter critiquing an LC spDCM connectivity study; urges DTI, plasticity, comorbidity foci
Primary_Limitation: It is a non-empirical Letter to the Editor with no original data, sample, or quantitative analysis of its own.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Compensatory neural mechanisms, impact of comorbid MDD+aMCI, and temporal progression of LC connectivity remain underexplored. - Applications: Early identification of cognitive decline / dementia onset via LC connectivity markers; targeting LC function for early intervention. - Methodologies: spectral dynamic causal modeling (spDCM); proposed integration of DTI white-matter imaging. - Achievable Outcomes: A more comprehensive picture of LC dysregulation trajectory and possible early interventions altering the neurodegenerative course.
Journal: Spanish Journal of Psychiatry and Mental Health (2025), in press (xxxx)

Method_Architecture: Resting-state EEG feature extraction (PSD, Hjorth, entropy, microstates) with LDA/SVM three-level classification and random-forest regression fusing EEG, CSF, APOE, and demographics.
Best_Metric: HC vs AD accuracy 85.8% (LDA); three-level HC/MCI/AD accuracy ~70%
Dataset: Xiangya Hospital cohort (Central South University, Changsha; enrolled March 2017-January 2022)
Sample_N_Approx: 890 — 189 MCI / 330 AD / 57 VCI / 47 FTD / 21 DLB / 246 HC
Key_Novelty: Largest-to-date EEG cohort (890) for HC/MCI/AD staging plus differentiation from other dementias
Primary_Limitation: Single-center, cross-sectional design with small non-AD dementia subgroups and limited CSF/APOE availability; no external validation.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: EEG-based MCI/AD classification historically limited by small samples and exclusion of other dementias; unclear which EEG biomarkers are reliable for early detection/progression. - Applications: Low-cost, non-invasive EEG screening tool for MCI/AD diagnosis and disease-progression monitoring in clinical practice. - Methodologies: Resting-state EEG feature engineering (PSD, Hjorth, entropy, microstates) with LDA/SVM classification and random-forest regression fusing EEG+CSF+APOE+demographics. - Achievable Outcomes: ~70% three-level HC/MCI/AD accuracy, ~80-86% binary accuracy, and hybrid-feature regression R2 up to 0.98 for cognitive/progression measures.

Method_Architecture: Narrative book chapter reviewing MRI biomarkers (structural MRI/VBM/cortical thickness, DTI, iron-quantification SWI/QSM/nigrosome swallow tail sign, and functional MRI connectivity) for distinguishing PD-MCI, PDD, and DLB from AD and healthy controls.
Best_Metric: Not reported
Dataset: Not reported (narrative review of published MRI studies in PD-MCI, PDD, and DLB)
Key_Novelty: Modality-organised MRI review distinguishing PD-MCI, PDD, and DLB
Primary_Limitation: Narrative (non-systematic) chapter with no original data; cited evidence is mostly small cross-sectional DLB studies.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Why striatal/occipital atrophy in DLB is absent in PDD is unclear; no distinct cortical atrophy profile separates DLB from PDD; direct DLB-vs-PDD imaging comparisons (e.g., swallow tail sign) are lacking; individual-level diagnostic prediction unproven. - Applications: MRI-based differential diagnosis of DLB, PDD, and PD-MCI versus AD and HCs, plus progression monitoring and therapeutic trials. - Methodologies: Structural MRI/VBM/cortical thickness, DTI, iron-quantification MRI (SWI/QSM, nigrosome swallow tail sign), and resting-state/task functional MRI connectivity. - Achievable Outcomes: Higher diagnostic accuracy for DLB via iron-sensitive and cortical-thickness markers, pending validation in larger longitudinal multimodal cohorts.
Journal: Neuroimaging in Parkinson's Disease and Related Disorders, Chapter 11 (Elsevier, 2023)

Method_Architecture: Multiscale time-varying functional-connectivity analysis (variable sliding windows + continuous wavelet transform) over 12 EEG ROIs, with t-test feature selection, regularized LDA, AdaBoost decision-tree classifiers, and weighted majority voting of 21 classifiers producing a soft connectivity-based discrimination score.
Best_Metric: Acc 91.97% (LOO CV HC vs MCI); 3-fold 91.17%; 84.61% 9-18mo progression-trend prediction (22/26)
Dataset: Wayne State University / Michigan ADRC (MADRC) resting-state EEG cohort (older Black Americans)
Key_Novelty: Multiscale EEG soft-score for MCI detection + pre-symptomatic prediction
Primary_Limitation: Small (137), class- and sex-unbalanced single-population cohort; progression prediction rests on only 26 follow-up subjects.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Mixed and non-reproducible EEG accuracy across studies; how to select sliding-window size; proactive prediction of MCI incidence before clinical symptoms remains very limited. - Applications: Low-cost non-invasive EEG screening and proactive risk stratification for early MCI detection in underserved older Black adults. - Methodologies: Multiscale time-varying functional connectivity, wavelet time-frequency features, regularized LDA + AdaBoost, weighted majority voting, soft connectivity-based scoring. - Achievable Outcomes: >91% cross-validated HC/MCI accuracy and 84.61% 9-18 month progression-trend prediction on a follow-up subset.

Method_Architecture: Longitudinal Cox proportional hazards survival modelling (age as time scale) with ANOVA/ANCOVA, Pearson correlation, and Kruskal-Wallis tests on individualized left frontal memory-related ERPs (Target/Nontarget/Diff at F7, F5, F3, F753) from a 64-channel EEG delayed match-to-sample working memory task.
Best_Metric: HR 1.47 (95% CI 1.03, 2.08) for F753 Diff predicting incident aMCI
Dataset: University of Kentucky Sanders-Brown / Alzheimer's Disease Center (UK-ADC) longitudinal aging cohort
Sample_N_Approx: 33 — 19 baseline normal cognition (7 converters / 12 non-converters) / 14 baseline aMCI
Key_Novelty: Baseline frontal memory ERP neuromarker predicts aMCI ~5 years before diagnosis
Primary_Limitation: Very small converter group (n=7) and non-random highly educated volunteer sample limit precision and generalizability, with no independent validation cohort.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: What the memory-related neuromarkers physiologically measure, and whether small-sample hazard estimates generalize to representative populations. - Applications: Noninvasive low-cost individualized prognostic EEG screening for aMCI risk in community clinics and future wearable/telehealth settings. - Methodologies: Bluegrass delayed match-to-sample working memory ERPs with Cox proportional hazards, ANOVA/ANCOVA, Pearson correlations, and Kruskal-Wallis tests. - Achievable Outcomes: Baseline left frontal Diff brainwaves predict incident aMCI ~5 years ahead with significant hazard ratios (F753 Diff HR=1.47).

Method_Architecture: Soft-voting ensemble (logistic regression, SVM, KNN, random forest, gradient boosting) trained on linear mixed-effects-derived trajectory features (r-slope, dev, d-slope) from RAVLT, ADAS13, and FreeSurfer entorhinal/hippocampus/ventricle MRI measures.
Best_Metric: F1 77% (HC vs cMCI, with MRI added, up from 60%); sMCI vs cAD F1 78% with MRI vs 77% without
Dataset: ADNI
Key_Novelty: Mixed-effects cognition+MRI trajectory features for conversion prediction
Primary_Limitation: High misclassification precludes individual-level prediction; ADNI-only with a limited set of cognitive/MRI measures and uncontrolled inter-visit timing.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Pinpointing when MRI adds predictive value over cognition and reducing misclassification to enable individual-level prediction amid MCI heterogeneity. - Applications: Early stratification of normal and MCI individuals at risk of converting to MCI/AD using combined cognitive and MRI trajectory features. - Methodologies: Linear mixed-effects trajectory features (r-slope, dev, d-slope) feeding a soft-voting ensemble with permutation (ELI5) feature importance and a leakage-controlled independent test set. - Achievable Outcomes: F1 60%->77% for HC vs cMCI and 77%->78% for sMCI vs cAD when MRI features are added to cognitive features.

Method_Architecture: Semi-automated 3D-slicer WMH volumetry (PVH/DWMH on T2 FLAIR, ICV-normalized) correlated with cognitive and blood-biochemistry changes via Pearson, multiple linear regression, and logistic regression in amnestic MCI over 2 years.
Best_Metric: r=-0.5, p=0.01 (change in DWMH volume ratio vs change in MMSE)
Dataset: Tokyo Medical University memory/outpatient clinic amnestic MCI cohort (2015-2018)
Sample_N_Approx: 38 amnestic MCI enrolled; 14 dropped out so 24 analysed for the full 2-year duration
Key_Novelty: DWMH (not PVH) progression correlates with MMSE/verbal fluency decline in aMCI
Primary_Limitation: Small sample (24 completers), short 2-year follow-up, and exclusion of severe-WMH (Fazekas grade 3) cases limit generalizability and causal inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Effects of WMH progression on MCI cognition were unclear; whether WMH progression and vascular risk factors drive AD conversion over 2 years; regional WMH versus cognition not assessed. - Applications: DWMH volume as an indicator of progressive cognitive dysfunction and PVH volume as a marker of cognitive dysfunction in MCI. - Methodologies: Semi-automated 3D-slicer FLAIR WMH volumetry, ICV-normalized ratios, Pearson and multiple linear regression, logistic regression for conversion. - Achievable Outcomes: DWMH progression correlates with declining MMSE and verbal fluency while PVH progression does not; vascular risk factors not associated with conversion under treated conditions.

Method_Architecture: Unsupervised Louvain graph-modularity clustering of MCI patients based on pairwise correlations of regional [18F]THK5351 (tau+astrogliosis) PET SUVR z-scores across 75 ROIs, with Kruskal-Wallis/Mann-Whitney group comparison, voxel-wise SPM, and Firth's logistic regression for dementia conversion.
Best_Metric: OR 88.95 (95% CI 3.224->999.9, p=0.008) for dementia conversion in AD type vs sparse type; AD-type conversion 90.9% (10/11)
Dataset: Gachon University Gil Medical Center cohort (Incheon, South Korea)
Sample_N_Approx: 97 — 60 MCI / 37 NC (62 also had flutemetamol PET); MCI subtypes: 17 limbic / 24 diffuse / 8 sparse / 11 AD type
Key_Novelty: First MCI subtyping by tau+astrogliosis THK5351 PET via Louvain clustering
Primary_Limitation: Small single-center sample without autopsy confirmation; very wide conversion-OR confidence intervals (upper bound >999.9) and MAO-B off-target THK5351 binding limit inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No established biomarker confirms MCI-to-dementia progression; MAO-B off-target binding limits THK5351 interpretation; whether limbic type reflects LATE/TDP-43 pathology is unresolved. - Applications: Prognostic stratification and differential diagnosis of MCI subtypes; flagging high-conversion-risk patients for early intervention. - Methodologies: THK5351 SUVR quantification with partial volume correction, Louvain graph-modularity clustering over 75 ROIs, Firth's logistic regression for rare-event conversion odds. - Achievable Outcomes: Four clinically distinct MCI subtypes with divergent conversion risk (AD type 90.9% vs sparse type 0%).

Method_Architecture: 1H NMR plasma metabolomics with univariate Mann-Whitney U (FDR-corrected) and six-model multivariate ROC machine learning using cross-validation and Monte-Carlo cross-validation, with VIP-based metabolite ranking to derive a lysine/glycine/glutamine diagnostic panel for MCI vs HC.
Best_Metric: MMSE 25.74±1.83 (MCI) vs 29±1 (HC); AUC reported in supplement ROC figures but no numeric value in available text
Dataset: Single-centre North Indian MCI/HC plasma cohort (Banaras Hindu University / CBMR SGPGIMS)
Sample_N_Approx: 50 MCI / 50 HC screened; NMR on 27 MCI / 20 HC (47 analysed)
Key_Novelty: NMR plasma panel (lysine/glycine/glutamine) for MCI in North Indian population
Primary_Limitation: Small NMR-analysed sample (27 MCI/20 HC), single-population cross-sectional design with no independent external validation; local file is supplement-only so main-text AUCs are unavailable.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Lack of validated, population-generalisable blood biomarkers for early MCI detection and conversion prediction. - Applications: Plasma NMR metabolite panel (lysine, glycine, glutamine) as a non-invasive MCI screening aid and basis for dietary/metabolic intervention. - Methodologies: 1H NMR plasma metabolomics with univariate Mann-Whitney U (FDR), six-model multivariate ROC, CV/MCCV, and VIP-based ranking. - Achievable Outcomes: Discrimination of MCI from HC and identification of an over-nutritional metabolic phenotype amenable to dietary intervention.

Method_Architecture: FreeSurfer hippocampal subfield segmentation with novel ratio-of-principal-curvatures (RPC) morphometry, univariate t-test and random-forest feature selection, and a two-hidden-layer MLP classifier of MCI-to-AD conversion.
Best_Metric: Acc 79.95% (random-forest top-20 features; sensitivity 74.44%, specificity 85.46%)
Dataset: ADNI
Key_Novelty: Novel RPC hippocampal curvature biomarker for MRI-only MCI-to-AD prediction
Primary_Limitation: Single ADNI cohort of only 178 subjects with no external validation and an ~80% accuracy ceiling.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Achieving high MCI-to-AD conversion accuracy from MRI alone without invasive PET/CSF data, and overcoming data insufficiency that limits deep models. - Applications: Non-invasive structural-MRI screening tool to flag suspected MCI-to-AD converters for preventive care. - Methodologies: Hippocampal subfield curvature/RPC analysis with univariate t-test and random-forest feature selection feeding a shallow MLP classifier. - Achievable Outcomes: 79.95% accuracy distinguishing MCI converters from non-converters using only structural MRI hippocampal biomarkers.

Method_Architecture: Group-comparison study of theory of mind (sarcasm comprehension via TASIT Part 2) across older adults with vascular risk factors, MCI patients, and healthy controls, using MANOVA/ANOVA with Scheffe post hoc and partial eta-squared.
Best_Metric: eta2=0.095, F(4,128.890)=2.638, p=0.038 (diagnostic-group effect on paradoxical sarcasm comprehension)
Dataset: Community-dwelling Greek older adults (VRF/MCI/HC), General Hospital of Katerini and Alzheimer Hellas centers, Thessaloniki
Sample_N_Approx: 109 — 41 VRF / 44 MCI / 24 HC (text; Table 1 lists HC n=22)
Key_Novelty: VRF older adults share MCI-like paradoxical sarcasm (ToM) deficit vs HC
Primary_Limitation: Single ToM test, unmatched younger/more-educated controls, no neuroimaging for VRF, and non-blinded single examiner limit inference.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether a vascular risk profile is an underlying ground for developing AD pathology and what brain substrate (e.g., white matter damage) produces the shared paradoxical sarcasm deficit. - Applications: Adding social inference tests to neuropsychological batteries to detect early social-cognition deficits before formal diagnosis. - Methodologies: TASIT Part 2 sarcasm-comprehension scoring with MANOVA/ANOVA, partial eta-squared, and Scheffe post hoc comparisons. - Achievable Outcomes: Paradoxical sarcasm comprehension identified as a specific ToM deficit shared by VRF and MCI groups but spared in healthy older adults.

Method_Architecture: Control-referenced MCI classification using linear mixed-effects models with interval-censored accelerated failure time (log-logistic and Weibull AFT) survival modelling on 12-year longitudinal PREDICT-HD data.
Best_Metric: Median time to HD onset 3.2 yr (95% CI 2.3-4.0) MCI vs 7.7 yr (6.2-9.2) intact; motor-planning MCI predictor p=0.014
Dataset: PREDICT-HD observational study (dbGaP phs000222.v6.p2)
Sample_N_Approx: 768 prodromal HD participants (analytic cohort; from 1,155 gene-expanded + 317 controls enrolled)
Key_Novelty: Validates MCI as a prognostic early landmark in prodromal HD via 12-year LMEM/AFT staging models
Primary_Limitation: Single genetically-tested PREDICT-HD cohort with unbalanced cognitive testing and no external validation, limiting generalisability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No consensus HD-specific MCI definition or accepted early cognitive endpoint for prodromal HD trials. - Applications: MCI enrichment/stratification and candidate endpoint for prodromal HD disease-modifying trials. - Methodologies: Control-referenced LMEM cut-offs with interval-censored log-logistic/Weibull AFT survival models. - Achievable Outcomes: 54% baseline MCI prevalence with prognostic validity for earlier HD motor onset.
prediction_horizon_years: 12 (12-year longitudinal follow-up; onset predictions reported in years)

Method_Architecture: Resting-state quantitative EEG (global field power and synchronization across four bands) and CSF neurogranin analyzed with multiple linear and logistic regression to predict MCI-to-AD progression over two years.
Best_Metric: Acc 81.4% (CSF Ng + GFP theta + GFS beta; logistic regression)
Dataset: Single-center Swedish cohort, Karolinska University Hospital-Huddinge (CSF + resting-state qEEG)
Sample_N_Approx: 99 MCI patients (72 with >=2y follow-up: 41 stable / 31 progressive)
Key_Novelty: CSF neurogranin and qEEG are independent, additive predictors of MCI-to-AD progression
Primary_Limitation: Small two-year follow-up sample precluded amyloid-stratified analyses and may misclassify late progressors as stable.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether qEEG alone can replace invasive CSF in MCI prognosis - Applications: Multimodal prognostic work-up to flag MCI likely to progress to AD - Methodologies: CSF neurogranin ELISA plus resting-state qEEG GFP/GFS with logistic-regression classification - Achievable Outcomes: 81.4% accuracy classifying progressive vs stable MCI

Method_Architecture: Whole-brain T1WI radiomics features (mRMR+LASSO reduced) form a logistic-regression signature combined with APOE4, CDR and ADAS in an SVM classifier to predict MCI-to-AD conversion.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.807 (test integrated model; sens 0.745, spec 0.738; 12-mo AUC 0.814)
Dataset: ADNI (357 MCI patients, baseline T1WI MRI, APOE4, neuropsychological scales)
Sample_N_Approx: 357 — 203 stable / 154 progressed to AD (training n=249, test n=108)
Key_Novelty: Whole-brain WM/GM/CSF radiomics fused with APOE4 + cognitive scales for MCI-to-AD prediction
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective single-database (ADNI) design with short follow-up and no external/prospective validation.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: non-invasive long-horizon MCI-to-AD prediction without PET/CSF - Applications: low-cost whole-brain MRI screening for high-risk MCI - Methodologies: WM/GM/CSF radiomics signature + APOE4/cognitive scales via SVM - Achievable Outcomes: test AUC 0.807, 12-month AUC 0.814

Method_Architecture: Coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis in GingerALE 2.3.6 pooling rs-fMRI FC, ALFF/fALFF, and ReHo peak coordinates with cluster-level FWE correction and jackknife sensitivity analysis.
Best_Metric: ALE z=4.21 (decreased ALFF/fALFF left STG BA22; cluster FWE p<0.05)
Dataset: 30 published rs-fMRI studies (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase)
Sample_N_Approx: 30 studies (7 FC, 13 ALFF/fALFF, 8 ReHo, 2 ALFF/fALFF&ReHo; 18 met aMCI criteria)
Key_Novelty: First ALE meta-analysis of rs-fMRI salience-network functional alterations in MCI and aMCI
Primary_Limitation: Substantial between-study heterogeneity and exclusion of naMCI/MCI-substage and non-English studies limit generalisability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Inconsistent SN imaging findings and lack of validated SN markers to predict healthy-to-MCI and MCI-to-AD progression. - Applications: Potential rs-fMRI imaging biomarkers and SN targets for non-invasive brain stimulation/follow-up. - Methodologies: Coordinate-based ALE meta-analysis pooling FC/ALFF/fALFF/ReHo coordinates with FWE correction and jackknife. - Achievable Outcomes: Convergent SN regions (decreased ALFF/fALFF in left STG/insula/PreCG/precuneus; increased FC in thalamus/caudate) replicable across studies.

Method_Architecture: Weighted Multiple Multiscale Entropy (WMMSE) algorithm applied to 16-channel EEG, with Lempel-Ziv complexity channel screening and MoCA corroboration, to evaluate pre- versus post-neurofeedback training brain-function changes in MCI.
Best_Metric: P<0.05 (WMMSE post>pre-NFT in F4/C3/C4/O1/T5; O1 P=0.011)
Dataset: Local 16-channel EEG from 60 MCI patients (First Hospital of Hebei Medical University)
Key_Novelty: Weighted Multiple Multiscale Entropy (WMMSE) EEG biomarker to evaluate neurofeedback effect in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small single-site sample with a short 10-day intervention and no healthy/AD comparison group, reporting only group-level significance.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Accurately quantifying NFT-induced brain-function change in MCI and overcoming information loss in multiscale EEG entropy. - Applications: EEG biomarker for monitoring neurofeedback rehabilitation effect in MCI. - Methodologies: Weighted/multiple multiscale entropy on EEG with LZC screening and MoCA corroboration. - Achievable Outcomes: Significant pre/post-NFT WMMSE increases (P<0.05) in F4, C3, C4, O1, T5 with improved MoCA scores.

Method_Architecture: Iteratively constructed higher-order (PCn) Pearson-correlation rs-fMRI brain functional networks, with t-test edge-feature selection and a linear SVM classified by subject-level 5-fold cross-validation, plus decision-level fusion of low- and high-order networks.
Best_Metric: Acc ~50% at convergence (ACC decreases as order n increases; exact values figure-only)
Dataset: ADNI rs-fMRI (MCI vs HC); HCP rs-fMRI (gender prediction)
Key_Novelty: Tests higher-order PCn rs-fMRI networks; finds higher order reduces, not improves, discrimination
Primary_Limitation: Exact classification metrics are reported only in figures, and the matrix-sequence convergence is not theoretically proved.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether higher-order functional-connectivity correlation adds discriminative information and proving/explaining its convergence and biology - Applications: rs-fMRI BFN biomarkers for MCI identification and individual-difference prediction - Methodologies: Iterative PCn BFN construction with t-test selection, linear SVM, 5-fold CV, decision fusion - Achievable Outcomes: Improved sensitivity for MCI by fusing higher- with low-order BFNs without accuracy gain

Method_Architecture: ALE coordinate-based meta-analysis (GingerALE) pooling MNI coordinates from rs-fMRI ALFF/fALFF, ReHo and FC studies comparing MCI patients with healthy controls.
Best_Metric: Group difference: 39 studies pooled; convergent decreased precuneus FC/ALFF (max ALE ~0.0156)
Dataset: 39 published resting-state fMRI studies (MCI vs healthy controls)
Key_Novelty: First ALE meta-analysis combining ALFF, ReHo and FC for the DMN in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Heterogeneity in demographics and analysis pipelines across included studies and operator-dependent seed selection limit convergence.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: whether early precuneus FC changes are a specific MCI-to-AD biomarker and the combined predictive relationship among ALFF/ReHo/FC remain unresolved - Applications: convergent DMN regions as rs-fMRI biomarkers for MCI diagnosis and TMS/drug targets - Methodologies: ALE coordinate-based meta-analysis integrating ALFF/fALFF, ReHo and FC - Achievable Outcomes: identification of consistent DMN regions showing coexisting damage and compensation in MCI

Method_Architecture: Resting-state fMRI ROI-to-ROI functional connectivity (CONN toolbox) and FreeSurfer hippocampal subfield/cortical-thickness analysis, compared across HC, mdaMCI and mAD with ANCOVA and connectivity-cognition correlation.
Best_Metric: group difference: significant fronto-temporal decoupling mdaMCI vs HC (FDR-corrected); neuropsych effect sizes up to f=.906
Dataset: Local cohort, University of the Sunshine Coast / Sunshine Coast University Hospital, Australia (3T Siemens Skyra)
Key_Novelty: Fronto-temporal functional decoupling precedes hippocampal atrophy in confirmed mdaMCI
Primary_Limitation: Small, cross-sectional sample (especially mAD n=6) without follow-up imaging, precluding conversion prediction.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether functional disconnection causally precedes structural atrophy and predicts conversion in larger longitudinal cohorts. - Applications: Resting-state fMRI fronto-temporal connectivity as a non-invasive upstream early-MCI biomarker. - Methodologies: Longitudinally confirmed mdaMCI diagnosis with FreeSurfer volumetry and CONN ROI-to-ROI connectivity. - Achievable Outcomes: Fronto-temporal decoupling distinguished mdaMCI from HC where structural measures could not; 11% single-timepoint false-positive rate.

Method_Architecture: PRISMA-registered systematic review and random/fixed-effects meta-analysis pooling standardised mean differences of proton-MRS metabolite ratios and concentrations across brain regions in MCI, AD, and healthy controls.
Best_Metric: SMD -0.94 (PC NAA/mI MCI vs AD; 95% CI -1.24 to -0.65, P<0.05)
Dataset: 63 published proton-MRS studies (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science)
Key_Novelty: Pooled MRS meta-analysis mapping NAA/mI changes in PC and hippocampus across MCI-to-AD
Primary_Limitation: Few longitudinal converter studies and high, unmoderated between-study heterogeneity with non-uniform MRS acquisition parameters.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: whether MRS ratios (mI/NAA) reliably predict MCI-to-AD conversion given few longitudinal studies and high heterogeneity - Applications: non-invasive MRS screening using NAA/mI in hippocampus/PC for AD progression monitoring - Methodologies: PRISMA-registered SMD meta-analysis with I2 heterogeneity and NOS quality assessment - Achievable Outcomes: consistent PC NAA/mI sustained decrease (SMD -0.94) and mI/Cr increase distinguishing AD from MCI/controls

Method_Architecture: PRISMA-guided random-effects meta-analysis of 12 sham-controlled rTMS RCTs in MCI, pooling standardized mean differences with subgroup and risk-of-bias analyses.
Dataset: 12 published sham-controlled rTMS RCTs in MCI (329 patients)
Key_Novelty: First MCI-only meta-analysis restricted to sham-controlled rTMS RCTs assessing cognition
Primary_Limitation: Few included studies and small total sample with substantial heterogeneity in stimulation parameters limit the strength of conclusions.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Optimal rTMS site, parameters, and duration of cognitive benefit in MCI remain unclear. - Applications: Non-invasive non-pharmacological rTMS therapy for cognition in MCI. - Methodologies: PRISMA random-effects meta-analysis of sham-controlled RCTs. - Achievable Outcomes: Significant pooled cognitive (SMD=0.83) and memory (SMD=0.73) improvement.

Method_Architecture: Seed-based resting-state fMRI functional connectivity of the nucleus basalis of Meynert analysed with propensity-matched 2x2 (condition x diagnosis) mixed-effect modelling and neuropsychological correlation.
Best_Metric: r=-0.321 p=0.041 (NBM-SMA rsFC vs WMS-LM immediate recall, smoking CN; uncorrected)
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) structural and resting-state fMRI
Sample_N_Approx: 224 — 86 non-smoking CN / 44 smoking CN / 62 non-smoking MCI / 32 smoking MCI (after PSM)
Key_Novelty: First rsFC study of smoking effects on NBM cholinergic connectivity in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small smoking subgroups, cross-sectional design, and a key correlation that did not survive multiple-comparison correction.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: How chronic smoking disrupts NBM cholinergic connectivity in MCI and links to AD progression. - Applications: Resting-state NBM connectivity as an early functional marker of smoking-related cognitive risk in MCI. - Methodologies: PSM-balanced 2x2 mixed-effect seed-based rsFC analysis of the NBM with neuropsychological correlation. - Achievable Outcomes: Decreased smoking MCI NBM-precuneus/MOG rsFC and distinct CN-vs-MCI smoker connectivity patterns.

Method_Architecture: Navigated single-pulse TMS over M1 with simultaneous 32-channel EEG; GMFP/ERSP/ITC and waveform metrics (sDA, peaks) analysed by rm-ANOVA and a leave-one-out cross-validated linear SVM classifier for aMCI-to-AD conversion.
Best_Metric: Acc 100% (sDA cutoff 0.86; sens 100%, spec 100%, accuracy 95% CI 77-100%)
Dataset: Local single-centre cohort of aMCI patients and healthy controls (TMS-EEG)
Sample_N_Approx: 32 — 17 aMCI / 15 controls (13 aMCI completed 6-yr follow-up: 7 pAD-MCI, 6 npAD-MCI)
Key_Novelty: TMS-EEG sDA/gamma-ITC waveform biomarkers predict aMCI-to-AD conversion over 6 years
Primary_Limitation: Very small sample (13 followed-up) makes the 100% accuracy estimates unreliable and only proof-of-concept.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Validating small-sample TMS-EEG conversion biomarkers in larger biomarker-confirmed cohorts. - Applications: Low-cost non-invasive TMS-EEG screening to flag high-risk aMCI converters. - Methodologies: Navigated TMS-EEG GMFP/ITC/sDA metrics feeding a leave-one-out cross-validated linear SVM. - Achievable Outcomes: sDA 100% and gamma ITC 85% accuracy distinguishing converters from non-converters.

Method_Architecture: Multi-kernel SVM (MCPC) fuses Pearson-correlation, sparse-representation, and Granger-causality fMRI connectivity patterns from a single modality to classify MCI vs NC, evaluated by nested LOOCV.
Best_Metric: Acc 87.40% (MCPC; sens 90.48%, spec 84.38%)
Dataset: ADNI resting-state fMRI (127 subjects: 63 MCI, 64 NC)
Key_Novelty: First to combine multiple connectivity patterns (PC/SR/GCM) from single-mode fMRI via MK-SVM for MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small single-cohort ADNI sample (127) with LOOCV and no independent external validation set.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Single-pattern connectivity is insufficient to capture MCI-vs-NC group differences - Applications: Non-invasive single-modality fMRI MCI screening - Methodologies: Combining PC/SR/GCM connectivity via multi-kernel SVM with nested LOOCV - Achievable Outcomes: 87.40% accuracy (AUC 0.922) for MCI vs NC
Journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology (2021) 9:782727

Method_Architecture: Whole-brain MRI radiomics (1198 FreeSurfer cortical/subcortical features) reduced by Mann-Whitney/Spearman/LASSO/AIC selection to 15 features feeding a logistic-regression model that defines a new N biomarker, combined with CSF A/T biomarkers and 5-year Kaplan-Meier/log-rank survival analysis of MCI progression.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.998 (radiomics N biomarker, AD vs HC; sens 0.969, spec 0.973)
Dataset: ADNI (ADNI-GO and ADNI-2): T1-weighted MRI + CSF biomarkers
Key_Novelty: First whole-brain MRI radiomics N biomarker improving the ATN system for MCI progression prediction
Primary_Limitation: Modest sample from strict inclusion with multicenter scanner heterogeneity, no PET biomarkers, and baseline-only (non-longitudinal) progression analysis.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Quantifying whole-brain neurodegeneration as a sensitive N biomarker and disentangling isolated A/T/N prognostic value in MCI. - Applications: MRI-based ATN risk stratification to flag high-risk MCI patients. - Methodologies: FreeSurfer radiomics with LASSO/AIC selection and logistic regression plus Kaplan-Meier/log-rank survival analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: AUC 0.998 N biomarker for AD vs HC and ATN-profile 5-year progression rates from 11.9% to 92.3%.

Method_Architecture: Simultaneous [18F]flutemetamol PET/3T-MRI with FreeSurfer/PETSurfer SUVR quantification, partial-volume correction, surface-based GLM, VBM, and univariate linear regression of cognitive domains against amyloid load.
Best_Metric: r=-0.57 p=0.005 (paracentral amyloid SUVR vs executive z-compound; executive group diff p=0.037)
Dataset: Single-center Padua PD-MCI cohort (University of Padua), [18F]flutemetamol PET/3T-MRI
Key_Novelty: Surface-based amyloid SUVR links frontal/parietal Abeta to executive deficits in PD-MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small subgroup sample sizes (8 Abeta+ vs 17 Abeta-) reduce statistical power and limit generalizability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Clinical relevance of sub-AD-threshold amyloid and amyloid's interaction with PD primary pathology in driving dementia. - Applications: Amyloid PET as a biomarker stratifying executive-dysfunction risk in PD-MCI. - Methodologies: Simultaneous [18F]flutemetamol PET/3T-MRI with surface-based SUVR quantification and VBM. - Achievable Outcomes: Abeta+ PD-MCI show worse executive performance (p=0.037) correlated with frontal/parietal amyloid load.

Method_Architecture: Perspective/evidence-synthesis describing an EEG small-world graph-theory feature-extraction pipeline (feature standardization, PCA dimensionality reduction, SVM classification) within a broader multimodal-biomarker machine-learning framework for MCI-to-dementia risk prediction.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.97 +/- 0.03 (EEG SVM AD vs. control; Acc 95% +/- 3%)
Dataset: Narrative literature scope: prior published EEG/MRI/PET/CSF biomarker studies; ongoing Interceptor and AI-Mind (~1000 MCI) projects
Key_Novelty: Perspective framing EEG small-world graph + PCA/SVM as a low-cost MCI-to-dementia screening tool
Primary_Limitation: A Perspective with no new primary cohort; quantitative performance figures are drawn from prior cited studies.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No validated affordable noninvasive individual-level MCI-to-AD biomarker at >95% accuracy with adequate follow-up. - Applications: Low-cost EEG-based large-population screening to triage high-risk MCI subjects. - Methodologies: EEG small-world graph features with PCA and SVM classification; multimodal biomarker integration. - Achievable Outcomes: Reported EEG SVM AD-vs-control AUC 0.97 with ~95% accuracy; stepwise biomarker-pyramid personalized risk evaluation.

Method_Architecture: GAN-augmented improved residual 1D-CNN combined with a three-layer LSTM applied to multi-time-point AAL90 resting-state fMRI 90x90 functional-connectivity matrices for AD diagnosis and MCI-conversion prediction.
Best_Metric: Acc 93.5% (AD vs. NC; sMCI vs. pMCI 75.5%, CNN+LSTM at 24 m)
Dataset: ADNI resting-state fMRI (baseline, 12 m, 24 m)
Key_Novelty: GAN-augmented residual-CNN + multilayer-LSTM on longitudinal rs-fMRI FC for AD/MCI
Primary_Limitation: Internal-only 5-fold cross-validation on a single ADNI cohort with GAN augmentation and no external test set or numeric AUCs.
