Open_Problems: - Open Problems: rs-fMRI sMCI-to-pMCI conversion prediction remains limited (~75%) due to heterogeneous MCI - Applications: non-invasive longitudinal rs-fMRI AD diagnosis and MCI-conversion monitoring - Methodologies: GAN-augmented residual 1D-CNN + three-layer LSTM on AAL90 FC matrices - Achievable Outcomes: 93.5% AD vs NC and 75.5% sMCI vs pMCI accuracy
Journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (2022) 19:4508

Method_Architecture: Coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis using GingerALE 2.3.6 on rs-fMRI ALFF/ReHo/FC foci with cluster-level FWE correction (p<0.05, 1,000 permutations).
Best_Metric: group difference (FWE-corrected ALE convergence, p<0.05, 1,000 permutations)
Dataset: 38 published rs-fMRI studies (ALFF/ReHo/FC coordinates in MCI vs HC)
Key_Novelty: First ALE meta-analysis combining ALFF, ReHo, and FC of the dorsal attention network in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Limited number of included studies and operator-dependent seed-point selection reduce reliability of the converged DAN markers.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Limited study count and operator-dependent seed selection limit DAN marker reliability. - Applications: DAN region targets (IPL, IFG, MFG, preCG) for early MCI intervention. - Methodologies: Coordinate-based ALE of ALFF/ReHo/FC foci with FWE correction. - Achievable Outcomes: Convergent abnormal DAN regions and inter-network interactions in MCI.

Method_Architecture: Resting-state fMRI ALFF (DPABI/SPM12) analysis comparing MCI vs HC at baseline and pre- vs post-moxibustion within MCI, with two-sample/paired t-tests and regression of ALFF change on MMSE change.
Best_Metric: MMSE/MoCA increase post-moxibustion p<0.0001 (Wilcoxon); ALFF-MMSE correlation p<0.05 FDR
Dataset: Locally collected 3.0T rs-fMRI cohort (Guangxi, China): 30 MCI + 30 HC
Key_Novelty: First rs-fMRI ALFF study of moxibustion's effect on spontaneous neural activity in MCI patients
Primary_Limitation: Small, cross-sectional sample with ALFF-only analysis and no sham/control intervention arm.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No validated treatment or clear central mechanism for moxibustion in MCI - Applications: Non-pharmacological intervention to improve cognition and modulate brain networks in MCI - Methodologies: rs-fMRI ALFF analysis with t-tests and regression against MMSE change - Achievable Outcomes: Significant post-treatment MMSE/MoCA increases with increased ALFF in DMN/VIN/subcortical regions correlated with cognitive improvement

Method_Architecture: Voxel-wise forward magnetization transfer rate (kfor) maps derived from inversion-recovery MTI with/without macromolecular saturation, analyzed with SPM12 general linear models across cross-sectional and longitudinal diagnostic groups.
Best_Metric: group difference: WM kfor AD 0.17±0.16/s vs MCI 0.36±0.17/s, p=0.00087
Dataset: Cardiovascular Health Study Cognition Study (CHS-CS), 1.5 T MTI at University of Pittsburgh MR Research Center
Key_Novelty: Voxel-wise forward magnetization-transfer-rate (kfor) maps for AD diagnosis and progression
Primary_Limitation: Small samples and a large-RF-offset 1.5 T protocol yielded only relative, underestimated kfor with ventral/temporal regions excluded.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: capturing kfor change in middle/late AD and ventral/temporal regions - Applications: non-invasive MRI microstructural biomarker for AD diagnosis/progression - Methodologies: voxel-wise kfor with SPM GLM group comparisons - Achievable Outcomes: significant kfor decreases (WM AD vs MCI p=0.00087) and progressive longitudinal declines

Method_Architecture: Longitudinal 3D pseudo-continuous ASL-MRI quantifying regional prefrontal CBF (FreeSurfer/Desikan-Killiany ROIs), compared with FDR-corrected t-tests/ANOVA and related to executive function via stepwise regression.
Best_Metric: Left lateral orbitofrontal CBF reduction 25.8% vs 7.8% (converters vs non-converters); interaction F(1,96)=4.66, p=0.036
Dataset: Single-center longitudinal cohort, Fudan University Zhongshan Hospital (49 PD + 37 HC, ASL-MRI)
Key_Novelty: First longitudinal ASL-MRI link of left lateral orbitofrontal hypoperfusion to PD-MCI conversion
Primary_Limitation: Small sample with only 10 converters and no time-matched HC follow-up limits power and generalizability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: How CBF reduction mechanistically drives cognitive decline and whether it precedes brain atrophy in early PD. - Applications: Non-invasive low-cost ASL-MRI perfusion marker to track PD-MCI conversion risk. - Methodologies: Longitudinal 3D pCASL ASL-MRI with FreeSurfer ROI CBF and stepwise regression against executive measures. - Achievable Outcomes: Detecting greater left lateral orbitofrontal hypoperfusion (25.8% vs 7.8%) in MCI converters over 2 years.

Method_Architecture: Radiomic features (430/ROI over 80 AAL ROIs) with Cronbach reliability and LASSO feature selection feeding L1-penalised Cox proportional-hazards survival models for single- and dual-modality MCI-to-AD conversion prediction.
Best_Metric: C-index 0.798 (dual-modality, Huashan external cohort; ADNI test 0.766)
Dataset: ADNI (355 MCI + 94 HC) plus Huashan Hospital external cohort (22 MCI)
Sample_N_Approx: 471 — 377 MCI (168 MCI-c/187 MCI-nc ADNI + 10 MCI-c/12 MCI-nc Huashan) + 94 HC
Key_Novelty: Dual-modality PET+MRI radiomic Cox model shows only modest gain over single-modality for MCI-to-AD
Primary_Limitation: The external test cohort (n=22) is very small, creating uncertainty in C-index estimates and overfitting risk.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether dual-modality PET+MRI meaningfully improves MCI-to-AD conversion prediction over single-modality radiomics. - Applications: Imaging-based prognostic risk stratification for MCI, including single-modality screening in resource-limited settings. - Methodologies: AAL-ROI radiomic LASSO feature selection feeding L1-penalised Cox survival models validated by C-index across two ethnic cohorts. - Achievable Outcomes: Dual-modality C-index 0.766 (ADNI test) / 0.798 (Huashan), only modestly above single-modality.

Method_Architecture: Multidomain event-related EEG analysis (LPP/ERP, ERSP time-frequency, wPLI functional connectivity, GRETNA graph-theory metrics) comparing MCI vs MCI-depressed groups during an IAPS emotion-regulation task with HAMD-17 correlations.
Best_Metric: Group difference: LPP win5 to negative stimuli 3.13±0.92 vs 0.69±0.49, p=0.015; depression vs clustering coefficient r=-0.66, p<0.001
Dataset: Local cohort — 43 MCI patients (Department of Neurology, Tongji Hospital, Shanghai); IAPS picture stimuli
Key_Novelty: First EEG study of neural mechanisms of impaired emotion regulation in depressed MCI individuals
Primary_Limitation: Small cross-sectional sample (43, only 17 depressed) precludes causal inference about depression and emotion regulation.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Causal mechanism linking depressive symptoms to impaired emotion regulation in MCI and whether EEG markers track treatment. - Applications: Objective EEG markers (alpha/gamma oscillations, alpha-band connectivity) for depression severity in MCI. - Methodologies: Combined LPP, ERSP, wPLI connectivity, and graph-theory analysis with HAMD-17 correlation. - Achievable Outcomes: Increased theta/alpha and decreased gamma oscillations and abnormal alpha-band network connectivity as candidate depressive-symptom markers.

Method_Architecture: Seed-to-voxel resting-state fMRI functional connectivity analysis using the CONN toolbox (Fisher-transformed hippocampal seed correlations) with GRF-corrected F-tests comparing MCI vs CN within each sex.
Best_Metric: Group difference: hippocampus-precuneus & hippocampus-brainstem connectivity stronger in males (cluster p<0.05 FDR, voxel p<0.001)
Dataset: ADNI (ADNI-1, ADNI-GO, ADNI-2, ADNI-3) resting-state fMRI and 3.0-T T2 MRI
Key_Novelty: First study of sex differences in hippocampal resting-state functional connectivity in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small sample size (n=80) and analysis restricted to the hippocampus as the only seed region.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: whether sex differences in hippocampal connectivity drive faster MCI-to-AD progression in females - Applications: sex-specific precision medicine and targeted brain stimulation/cognitive training - Methodologies: seed-to-voxel resting-state functional connectivity with GRF-corrected F-tests - Achievable Outcomes: identification of hippocampus-precuneus and hippocampus-brainstem connectivity as male-specific MCI-vs-CN markers

Method_Architecture: Linear-kernel SVM trained on baseline FDG-PET voxel intensities to classify PD-MCI patients as future PDD converters versus stable MCI, validated across independent test and PDD/DLB/PDNC/NC cohorts.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.73 (independent test; Acc 73.7%, sens 67%, spec 80%)
Dataset: Local clinical FDG-PET cohorts (Asan Medical Center, Seoul; Health Sciences Center/Crescentwood Memory Clinic, Winnipeg)
Sample_N_Approx: 165 — training 43 PD-MCI (23 PDD-converter/20 stable MCI) + 19 independent test (9 PDD-converter/10 MCI) + Asan validation 54 (18 NL/17 PDNC/19 PDD) + Winnipeg validation 39 (22 MCI/17 DLB) + 10 PD ON/OFF l-DOPA
Key_Novelty: FDG-PET SVM metabolic pattern (PDDCP) predicts PD-MCI to PDD conversion, robust to anti-PD meds
Primary_Limitation: Small training and validation samples (43 train; only 9 test converters) risk overfitting and unstable sensitivity.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Accurate individual-level PD-MCI to PDD prognosis remains unmet given small samples and heterogeneity. - Applications: FDG-PET SVM screening to enrich PDD trial cohorts and clinical prognosis. - Methodologies: Linear-kernel SVM on SPM-preprocessed FDG-PET with permutation-tested voxel weights. - Achievable Outcomes: ~74% test accuracy (AUC 0.73), medication-independent, also detecting PDD and DLB.

Method_Architecture: Logistic regression and tree-based ensemble ML (random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) applied to a J-ADNI structural tabular dataset with CVRS scores, evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.792 (LightGBM, clinical+CVRS; Acc 0.711, F1 0.655)
Dataset: J-ADNI (Japanese ADNI)
Key_Novelty: First ML application of CVRS to predict MCI-to-dementia progression in a Japanese (J-ADNI) cohort
Primary_Limitation: Small J-ADNI sample yields modest accuracy (max 71.1%) and an unusually high 2-year conversion rate (54.8%).
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Predicting MCI-to-dementia progression from a simple MRI visual rating scale in small non-ADNI Asian cohorts. - Applications: Cost-effective MRI-based clinical screening of MCI for dementia risk without PET/CSF. - Methodologies: Tree-based ML (RF, XGBoost, LightGBM) on CVRS structural tabular data with LOOCV and feature-importance analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: LightGBM AUC 0.792 / accuracy 0.711 for 2-year progression using clinical data + CVRS.

Method_Architecture: Single-author narrative review synthesising TSPO and non-TSPO PET radiotracers for imaging neuroinflammation in AD and MCI, with two tables of prior clinical-study regional uptake findings.
Best_Metric: Not reported (narrative review)
Dataset: Narrative review of ~26 published clinical PET radiotracer studies in AD/MCI (Tables 1-2)
Sample_N_Approx: Not reported in source (narrative review; ~26 studies tabulated)
Key_Novelty: Review of TSPO and non-TSPO PET tracers for imaging neuroinflammation in AD/MCI
Primary_Limitation: Narrative review with no quantitative meta-analysis; underlying studies are small and report conflicting neuroinflammation findings.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether neuroinflammation is protective or detrimental, and lack of standardised PET quantification. - Applications: Non-invasive PET imaging of microglial/astrocyte activation for early AD/MCI diagnosis and progression monitoring. - Methodologies: TSPO and non-TSPO radioligand PET with kinetic/uptake quantification. - Achievable Outcomes: Improved target-specific tracers enabling multi-tracer longitudinal staging.

Method_Architecture: Multinomial logistic regression combining qEEG/ERP cognitive-testing features and automated volumetric MRI measures to classify SCD, MCI, and dementia, with leave-one-out cross-validation and AUC evaluation.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.87 (combined qEEG/ERP+vMRI 3-class model; dementia vs SCD pairwise AUC 0.96)
Dataset: Local single-center retrospective cohort, Pacific Brain Health Center (Santa Monica, CA); eVox qEEG/ERP and Neuroreader volumetric MRI
Sample_N_Approx: 161 — 69 SCD / 53 MCI / 39 dementia (subset of 111 with vMRI)
Key_Novelty: Combines qEEG/ERP cognitive testing with volumetric MRI to differentiate SCD, MCI, and dementia
Primary_Limitation: Single-center retrospective convenience sample with no healthy control group and only leave-one-out cross-validation (no external test set).
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Distinguishing SCD from MCI and modeling cognition as a continuum rather than discrete categories. - Applications: Portable accessible adjunct screening for SCD/MCI/dementia in primary care, rural, and telehealth settings. - Methodologies: Multinomial logistic regression combining qEEG/ERP features with normalized regional MRI volumes; leave-one-out cross-validation. - Achievable Outcomes: Combined qEEG/ERP + left temporal lobe volume model differentiating SCD/MCI/dementia at AUC 0.87.

Method_Architecture: Group-ICA resting-state fMRI processed with sliding-window dynamic FC and an iterative ordinal Louvain multilayer-modularity algorithm to derive per-network switching rates, related to cognition via elastic net regression, Bayesian belief network, and a random-forest classifier.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.820 (IC15 random-forest sMCI vs pMCI; ±0.094)
Dataset: SIMPLE cohort resting-state fMRI (Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai)
Key_Novelty: First rs-fMRI multilayer-network switching-rate biomarker for MCI cognition and progression
Primary_Limitation: Moderate sample (118) with only 14 converters and short 1-year follow-up weaken the predictive model.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Reliable MCI-to-dementia conversion modelling with few converters and short follow-up - Applications: Non-invasive rs-fMRI switching-rate biomarker to stratify MCI progression - Methodologies: Louvain multilayer-modularity switching-rate analysis with elastic net and Bayesian belief network - Achievable Outcomes: AUC 0.820 for sMCI vs pMCI using DMN (IC15) switching rate

Method_Architecture: Localisation-based subject-specific neuromelanin locus-coeruleus seed-to-voxel resting-state functional connectivity analysis (CONN/SPM12) with Glasser-atlas ROI-to-ROI subnuclei analysis comparing MCI and control groups.
Best_Metric: group difference LC-ACC fc FDR p<.001 (LC-left insula FDR p=.012; LC-PCC FDR p=.021; LC-TPJ correlated to MMSE p=.017)
Dataset: Local single-centre cohort (Magdeburg memory clinic / DZNE; 28 MCI + 29 controls), 3 T MRI
Key_Novelty: Subject-specific neuromelanin-localised LC rs-fMRI links LC/salience-network fc to MCI and MMSE
Primary_Limitation: Modest single-site cross-sectional sample with no longitudinal follow-up, so conversion prediction is untested.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether LC rs-fc disturbances predict MCI-to-dementia conversion is untested without longitudinal follow-up. - Applications: Candidate fMRI/neuromelanin markers of attentional-network disturbance for early dementia diagnosis. - Methodologies: Subject-specific neuromelanin-localised LC seed-to-voxel and Glasser ROI-to-ROI connectivity analysis. - Achievable Outcomes: Group separation of MCI vs. controls on LC fc to ACC, insula, PCC and TPJ, with LC-TPJ fc tracking MMSE.

Method_Architecture: Pre/post dual-target rTMS intervention with resting-state EEG source-space functional connectivity (DICS source localisation on Brainnetome atlas, adaptive gedBounds alpha clustering, PLV) and neuropsychological testing.
Best_Metric: r=0.605 p=0.022 (MoCA improvement vs PCC-DC connectivity change)
Dataset: Local single-centre cohort, Shenzhen People's Hospital (resting-state EEG; ChiCTR1800019199)
Key_Novelty: Dual-target rTMS (DLPFC+PCu) restores PCC–DC EEG connectivity and improves memory in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small sample with no sham-control group and no follow-up on effect durability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Lack of sham-controlled, adequately powered, follow-up evidence and an optimal stimulation-site protocol for memory enhancement in MCI. - Applications: Non-invasive dual-target rTMS for cognitive/memory rehabilitation in MCI. - Methodologies: Resting-state EEG source connectivity (DICS, Brainnetome, gedBounds, PLV) with neuropsychological testing pre/post rTMS. - Achievable Outcomes: Significant MoCA and delayed-memory gains with restored right-PCC-to-right-DC connectivity correlated with cognitive improvement.

Method_Architecture: Dynamic Causal Modeling (DCM) with Parametric Empirical Bayes on resting-state fMRI over DMN/SAN/CEN ROIs, with ANOVA and step-wise linear regression against MMSE/CDR.
Best_Metric: L-dlPFC->L-PCC beta=-0.234 p=0.007 (MMSE model R2=0.115, F=5.434, p=0.002)
Dataset: ADNI-2 resting-state fMRI
Key_Novelty: First DCM/PEB effective-connectivity strength analysis across CN/EMCI/LMCI/AD stages
Primary_Limitation: Relatively small sample with resting-state-only data and modest cognitive-score variance explained.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: quantify connection-strength changes vs AD severity and the cingulate's role - Applications: EC biomarker for AD staging from rs-fMRI - Methodologies: DCM+PEB+BMR over DMN/SAN/CEN ROIs with regression - Achievable Outcomes: progressive EC loss (full in CN to none in AD); MMSE/CDR partially predicted

Method_Architecture: Source-reconstructed resting-state MEG power spectra (LCMV beamformer) compared between WMH-volume-defined vMCI and nvMCI groups using cluster-based permutation ANCOVA with Spearman correlations to cognition and hippocampal volume.
Best_Metric: group difference: theta higher in vMCI (CBPT p=0.036); beta lower (left p=0.0336, right p=0.0401); theta-MMSE rho=-0.306 p=0.001
Dataset: Local Madrid MCI cohort (three clinical centres; PSI2009/PSI2012 projects), MRI + resting-state MEG; WMH cut point from 346 cognitively intact controls
Sample_N_Approx: 117 — 61 vMCI / 56 nvMCI (129 recruited, 12 excluded for bad MEG data)
Key_Novelty: First MEG resting-state spectral comparison of vascular vs non-vascular MCI defined by WMH volume
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional, no AD biomarker confirmation, and no independent replication of the MEG markers.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: No robust quantitative WMH thresholds or MEG biomarkers ready for clinical VCI classification. - Applications: Non-invasive MEG differentiation of vascular vs non-vascular MCI in mixed dementia. - Methodologies: LST/SPM12 WMH segmentation with specificity-based cut point plus LCMV-beamformer MEG power spectra and cluster-based permutation testing. - Achievable Outcomes: Reproducible widespread theta increase and bilateral temporal beta decrease distinguishing vMCI from nvMCI independent of age and cognition.

Method_Architecture: fNIRS measurement of prefrontal oxy-hemoglobin (mHbO) during a verbal digit span task, compared against MoCA-K using independent t-tests and ROC/Youden discriminant analysis.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.952 (left PFC mHbO; sens 82.1%, spec 94.2%)
Dataset: Local South Korean senior-center cohort (84 healthy controls + 52 amnestic MCI), fNIRS PFC recordings
Key_Novelty: fNIRS left-PFC mHbO biomarker outperforms MoCA-K for MCI screening (AUC 0.952 vs 0.902)
Primary_Limitation: Single PFC-only mHbO feature with a small amnestic-only sample and no cross-validation, risking overfitting.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Optimizing an fNIRS neural biomarker for MCI beyond a single PFC feature without overfitting on small samples - Applications: Objective portable fNIRS screening/monitoring tool for MCI - Methodologies: PFC mHbO from a verbal digit span task analyzed with ROC/Youden discriminant statistics - Achievable Outcomes: Left-PFC mHbO discriminated MCI with AUC 0.952, exceeding MoCA-K (AUC 0.902)

Method_Architecture: Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of gray-matter volume combined with directed granger causality density (GCD) on resting-state fMRI, fused via ROC analysis to derive AD/MCI imaging biomarkers.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.938 (VBM+GCD PCUN.R, AD vs MCI; sens 81.3%, spec 100.0%)
Dataset: ADNI (ADNI1, ADNI2, ADNI-GO) rs-fMRI + structural MRI
Key_Novelty: First inflow/outflow granger causality density (GCD) fused with VBM for AD/MCI imaging biomarkers
Primary_Limitation: Very small sample (48 subjects, 16 per group) limits generalisability of the high reported AUCs.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Capturing directional information flow in AD/MCI with robust small-sample multimodal markers - Applications: Multimodal neuroimaging biomarkers for early MCI detection, progression prediction, and AD diagnosis - Methodologies: Voxel-based VBM plus directed inflow/outflow GCD with ROC fusion - Achievable Outcomes: Combined VBM+GCD reached AUC 0.926-0.938 across MCI detection, progression, and AD diagnosis

Method_Architecture: PRISMA/PICO systematic review of diffusion-MRI (DTI/DKI/DSI/NODDI) studies, classifying white matter fibers into limbic, projection, association, and commissural groups and tabulating their correlations with cognition and affection testing-scale scores in MCI.
Best_Metric: Group difference (qualitative: FA decreased, MD/DA/DR increased in cognition-related fibers)
Dataset: 69 published diffusion-MRI studies of MCI (2010-2022), PubMed and Web of Science
Key_Novelty: Fiber-level map linking WM disconnection to cognition vs affection in MCI via diffusion MRI
Primary_Limitation: Qualitative correlational synthesis of mostly small-sample, single-tract studies without meta-analytic pooling.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Identifying affection-specific fibers and quantifying global white matter network disconnection beyond single tracts. - Applications: Objective diffusion-MRI biomarker for early AD/MCI screening and targeted fiber-tract treatment. - Methodologies: PRISMA/PICO systematic review of DTI/DKI/DSI/NODDI metrics correlated with cognition and affection scales. - Achievable Outcomes: A fiber-level map linking hippocampus/temporal-lobe fibers to cognition and thalamic fibers to both cognition and affection.

Method_Architecture: PRISMA-guided systematic review synthesising 30 studies of EEG and ERP neurophysiological biomarkers in subjective cognitive decline, compared against MCI, AD, and controls and related to fluid, neuroimaging, and genetic biomarkers.
Best_Metric: Group difference: EEG slowing in SCD (increased delta/theta, decreased alpha/beta power); 30 studies synthesised
Dataset: 30 published EEG/ERP studies of SCD (PubMed and Web of Science, Jan 2011-Mar 2023)
Key_Novelty: First systematic review synthesising EEG/ERP biomarkers specifically in subjective cognitive decline
Primary_Limitation: Conflicting findings arise from small, heterogeneous SCD samples and varied SCD definitions, EEG systems, and analysis methods across studies.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Conflicting EEG/ERP results in SCD from small samples and heterogeneous SCD definitions/acquisition - Applications: Non-invasive low-cost EEG/ERP early-detection biomarker for SCD/AD - Methodologies: Resting-state spectral EEG, functional connectivity (PLI/EpEn/GFP/wSMI), and ERP components (P300/N170/N200/MMN) - Achievable Outcomes: Improved diagnostic accuracy combining EEG/ERP with MRI volume and prognostic SCD-to-MCI stratification

Method_Architecture: PCC seed-to-voxel resting-state fMRI functional connectivity analysis (CONN/SPM12) with FreeSurfer cortical thickness, comparing depression vs no-depression amyloid-positive MCI groups and correlating connectivity with amyloid SUVR and depression severity (HAMD-17).
Best_Metric: p<0.01 FDR (increased anterior DMN FC, depression vs no-depression); HAMD-17 positive correlation FDR p<0.05
Dataset: Catholic Aging Brain Imaging (CABI) database, Yeouido St. Mary's Hospital, Catholic University of Korea
Key_Novelty: First to isolate depression effect on anterior DMN connectivity in amyloid-positive MCI
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional single-center design yields only associations and cannot establish causal relationships.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Disentangling depression vs amyloid drivers of DMN connectivity change and establishing causality. - Applications: rs-fMRI DMN connectivity as marker of depression-related AD risk in amyloid-positive MCI. - Methodologies: PCC seed-based rs-fMRI connectivity with amyloid-PET stratification and HAMD-17 correlation. - Achievable Outcomes: Depression-associated anterior DMN connectivity increase correlating with HAMD-17 but not SUVR.

Method_Architecture: Single-blind, sham-controlled crossover pilot delivering active vs sham transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) via the NEMOS device, with safety assessed by adverse events and active-stand haemodynamics (beat-to-beat blood pressure, NIRS Tissue Saturation Index) plus exploratory cognitive/HRV/cytokine outcomes analysed with mixed-effects models and repeated ANOVA. Study protocol only; no results.
Best_Metric: Not reported (protocol)
Dataset: Local cohort: amnestic MCI patients at the Institute of Memory and Cognition, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin, Ireland (VINCI-AD trial; NCT05514756)
Key_Novelty: First safety/feasibility crossover trial of tVNS in amnestic MCI with NIRS haemodynamic monitoring
Primary_Limitation: Single-site pilot of only 40 participants with no efficacy endpoint, so therapeutic benefit cannot be established.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether tVNS is safe and tolerable in MCI given neuro-cardiovascular instability/orthostatic hypotension risk, and whether frontal tissue saturation can be augmented by tVNS. - Applications: Non-invasive home-usable neuromodulation as a dementia-prevention strategy in high-risk MCI. - Methodologies: Sham-controlled crossover device trial combining adverse-event tracking, Finapres beat-to-beat blood pressure, NIRS TSI, HRV and a cytokine panel. - Achievable Outcomes: Safety/feasibility data and effect-size estimates to power a definitive future tVNS trial in MCI.

Method_Architecture: Multi-site CSF-defined amyloid/tau (A/T) staging with GAAIN multi-repository consolidation and ComBat harmonization, FreeSurfer cortical thickness and hippocampal volumetry, vertex-wise GLM and linear mixed-effects longitudinal atrophy modelling (no machine-learning classifier).
Best_Metric: p=0.03 (longitudinal hippocampal atrophy A-T+ MCI vs NC); A+T+ vs NC p=0.005; cross-sectional hippocampal group difference p<0.001
Dataset: GAAIN-consolidated multi-repository: ADNI, ARWiBo, EDSD, PharmaCog (longitudinal data from ADNI and PharmaCog only)
Key_Novelty: First cortical-thickness/hippocampal atrophy study of amyloid-negative, p-tau-positive (A-T+) MCI
Primary_Limitation: Very small A-T- control group (20 baseline / 18 longitudinal), making normal-control comparisons secondary and underpowered.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether A-T+ is a distinct pathological state; no cortical signature identified even with larger samples; PART hypothesis requires histopathological confirmation. - Applications: Improved subtyping/prognosis of amyloid-negative MCI and harmonized multi-repository analysis of rare subgroups. - Methodologies: CSF A/T staging, GAAIN consolidation, ComBat harmonization, FreeSurfer cross-sectional/longitudinal pipelines, vertex-wise GLM and linear mixed-effects modelling. - Achievable Outcomes: Group-specific hippocampal atrophy rates and age-cortical-thickness associations adequately powered for a rare MCI subgroup.

Method_Architecture: Phase-amplitude cross-frequency coupling quantified by the entropy-based Modulation Index on 6-min closed-eye resting-state 64-channel EEG, analysed at global and eight-region levels with nonparametric statistics (Kruskal-Wallis/ANOVA, FDR) and Spearman correlation against cognitive scales (no classifier built).
Best_Metric: p<0.001 FDR (global alpha-gamma and beta-gamma coupling AD vs HC; no accuracy/AUC reported)
Dataset: Local cohort - Department of Neurology, Tongji Hospital, Tongji University, Shanghai, China (recruited Jan 2018-Dec 2021)
Key_Novelty: Concurrent rsEEG cross-frequency-coupling comparison of HC/MCI/AD; right-temporal theta-gamma tracks progression
Primary_Limitation: No amyloid/tau confirmation and no classification analysis, so coupling features' diagnostic/discriminative value is untested in a small single-centre sample.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether coupling alterations distinguish groups (no classifier built); whether couplings are caused by AD etiology vs other factors; inconsistent direction of global theta-gamma changes across studies; low discriminability between coupling features. - Applications: Non-invasive EEG marker for early detection and progression monitoring of MCI/AD; target for non-invasive brain stimulation. - Methodologies: Entropy-based Modulation Index phase-amplitude coupling on resting-state EEG, global and region-of-interest analysis, nonparametric statistics with FDR correction, Spearman correlation with cognitive scales. - Achievable Outcomes: Right-temporal theta-gamma coupling as a progression marker (HC<MCI<AD) and coupling-cognition associations dominated by the memory domain.

Method_Architecture: Eyes-closed resting-state EEG analysed with multitaper power spectral density, multiscale sample/permutation entropy, weighted phase lag index (wPLI) functional connectivity, and graph-theory network metrics (global/local/nodal efficiency, small-worldness) compared between MCI and HC using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with FDR correction (no classifier).
Best_Metric: p<0.05 FDR (C4 complexity p=0.0019, pFDR=0.037; Fp2 nodal efficiency p=0.002, pFDR=0.039)
Dataset: Local cohort - outpatient memory clinic, Department of Neurology, Hanyang University Hospital (Seoul and Guri, Korea)
Key_Novelty: wPLI plus variable-threshold graph metrics reveal MCI EEG network changes that spectral power misses
Primary_Limitation: Very small cross-sectional sample (12 MCI / 13 HC) limits statistical power and generalisability.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Lack of consensus on EEG connectivity/network changes in MCI; no standardised method for selecting a single graph sparsity threshold; small cross-sectional samples limit reliability. - Applications: Non-invasive low-cost EEG screening biomarker for early MCI/AD detection and monitoring. - Methodologies: wPLI functional connectivity robust to volume conduction, multiscale sample/permutation entropy, graph-theory metrics across variable thresholds, FDR correction and bootstrap CIs. - Achievable Outcomes: Theta-band global/nodal efficiency reductions, beta-band small-worldness loss, and reduced temporal-lobe complexity as candidate MCI biomarkers.

Method_Architecture: SVM classifiers (linear/non-linear) on FreeSurfer structural features and ICA/GIG-ICA-derived static and dynamic resting-state fMRI features, with stratified 10-fold cross-validation internally on the Shanghai Memory Study (SMS) cohort and external validation on ADNI using GIG-ICA-aligned components.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.91 internal (SMS sMRI+fMRI); AUC 0.86 external (ADNI)
Dataset: Shanghai Memory Study (SMS, Huashan Hospital, Fudan University) - internal; ADNI - external validation
Key_Novelty: Inter-cohort (Chinese SMS vs ADNI) validated sMRI plus static/dynamic fMRI MCI-conversion predictor
Primary_Limitation: Few converters (41 SMS, 25 ADNI) and only two cohorts, with no PET/CSF biomarkers and one-directional (non-swapped) external validation.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether brain dynamics change predictably before MCI conversion across populations; scarcity of longitudinal multi-cohort fMRI with conversion outcomes; whether inter-cohort clinical differences are population-driven. - Applications: Cross-cohort imaging biomarkers for MCI-to-AD conversion prediction and stratified early-intervention triage. - Methodologies: ROI-wise sMRI plus static/dynamic ICA-based fMRI features, GIG-ICA for cross-cohort IC correspondence, SVM with 10-fold CV, sliding-window dynamics. - Achievable Outcomes: Multi-modality MRI AUC > 0.85 generalizing across distinct cohorts.

Method_Architecture: Bibliometric and visualization analysis of 2,905 Web of Science Core Collection publications on EEG in MCI (2005-2022) using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and HistCite, covering co-authorship, co-citation, citation bursts, and keyword co-occurrence networks.
Best_Metric: Not reported (bibliometric review)
Dataset: Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC; SCI-Expanded and SSCI) - 2,905 EEG-for-MCI articles, 2005-2022
Key_Novelty: First bibliometric analysis of EEG research in MCI (2005-2022)
Primary_Limitation: Only the English-language WoSCC database was searched, so relevant studies in other databases or languages may have been missed.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Confirming diagnostic/prognostic value of EEG synchronization and rhythms with larger samples; clarifying common pathogenesis linking MCI with epilepsy, DLB and Parkinson's disease; underexplored advanced signal-processing and ML algorithms. - Applications: Early and differential diagnosis of MCI/AD; tracking amnesic MCI in large clinical trials via resting-state EEG markers; multimodal EEG-fMRI characterization. - Methodologies: Bibliometric analysis (CiteSpace, VOSviewer, HistCite); EEG functional connectivity and graph theory; machine learning and deep learning for EEG classification. - Achievable Outcomes: High classification accuracy for MCI-vs-HC distinction; objective non-invasive biomarkers; network-mechanism insights into cognitive impairment.

Method_Architecture: FreeSurfer (v7.2.0) atlas-based segmentation of 12 hippocampal subfields per hemisphere, with FDR-corrected regression comparing volumes across CN-NC/CN-C/MCI/AD groups and correlating subfield volumes with MoCA delayed-recall scores, controlling for age, gender, education, and eTIV (no machine-learning classifier).
Best_Metric: p<0.001 FDR (left presubiculum vs delayed recall, CN-NC); left HATA CN-NC vs CN-C p=0.036 FDR
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative)
Key_Novelty: Detects left HATA atrophy in cognitively normal pre-converters, before clinical AD/MCI symptoms
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional, single-modality structural MRI design with a small (n=28) CN converter subgroup and no MCI subtyping.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether subfield atrophy reliably precedes clinical decline across MCI subtypes; why CN-C and MCI groups did not differ; need to confirm the HATA finding. - Applications: Early/preclinical dementia detection and selection of sensitive hippocampal subfield biomarkers for AD progression. - Methodologies: FreeSurfer atlas-based subfield segmentation; regression with eTIV/demographic covariates; FDR-corrected group comparisons and volume-memory correlations. - Achievable Outcomes: Subfield-level (HATA, presubiculum) imaging markers of preclinical AD and memory decline that may outperform whole-hippocampus volume.

Method_Architecture: Topological data analysis (persistent homology) on 8-channel wearable EEG from an affective reminiscent oddball task, with UMAP/t-SNE clustering and random forest classification (MCI vs healthy cognitive aging) and regression (MoCA score) validated by leave-one-out-subject cross-validation.
Dataset: Local cohort, Nicolaus Copernicus University, Torun, Poland (elderly volunteers from Kamienica Inicjatyw; collected summer 2022)
Key_Novelty: TDA persistence-ratio EEG features from affective reminiscent oddball as MCI neuro-biomarker
Primary_Limitation: Very small (N=23), gender-imbalanced and class-imbalanced single-site pilot cohort with MoCA-only labelling and no external test set.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Whether the MCI-awareness link generalises beyond the oddball paradigm; small-N, class-imbalanced, single-cohort validity; modest regression accuracy. - Applications: Low-cost wearable-EEG neuro-biomarker for early MCI screening and remote monitoring of cognitive interventions and dementia care. - Methodologies: Topological data analysis (persistent homology) of multivariate EEG, EMD denoising, UMAP/t-SNE clustering, random forest classification/regression with LOOSCV. - Achievable Outcomes: Above-93% MCI-vs-healthy classification accuracy and MoCA-score estimation within ~+/-2.6 points in a pilot setting.

Method_Architecture: Qualitative PRISMA systematic review (PROSPERO CRD42023450811) of 22 concurrent TMS-EEG studies in the AD spectrum, synthesising single-pulse and repetitive TMS findings (TEP, GMFP, ITC, ERSP, plasticity metrics) by stimulation site and organising them into diagnostic, prognostic, and response biomarker categories (no pooled meta-analysis).
Best_Metric: Not reported (qualitative systematic review)
Dataset: Systematic review of 22 published TMS-EEG studies (databases: PubMed, ScienceDirect, PsychInfo); not a single cohort
Key_Novelty: Updated TMS-EEG systematic review reframing findings as AD diagnostic/prognostic/response biomarkers
Primary_Limitation: Heterogeneous, small, medication-confounded primary studies with non-standardised EEG methods, synthesised qualitatively without meta-analytic effect sizes.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Inconsistent diagnostic criteria, medication confounds, no standard plasticity definition/electrode naming, unreported cortex-to-coil distance, artifact handling, small samples. - Applications: Early detection and prognostication of AD; treatment-response monitoring for rTMS and conventional therapies; ML-based classification of AD-spectrum groups. - Methodologies: spTMS/rTMS/TBS/PAS combined with EEG; TEP/GMFP/ITC/ERSP/PCI metrics; sLORETA source localisation; SVM and other ML classifiers; phase-synchronised TMS-EEG. - Achievable Outcomes: Validated diagnostic/prognostic/response biomarkers, non-invasive prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion, and individualised neurophysiology-guided neuromodulation therapy.

Method_Architecture: Prospective 1-year longitudinal cohort with baseline serum ELISA synapse-related indices (BDNF, FGF2, FGF7, FGF22) and ERP (P300, MMN, N200) indices, modelled by forward logistic stepwise regression with ROC analysis and an independent external validation cohort, to predict 1-year MCI onset in depression.
Best_Metric: Acc 0.806 (validation); AUC 0.790 (derivation)
Dataset: Local clinical cohorts: Affiliated Hospital of Jiangsu University (derivation, Zhenjiang); People's Hospital of Yangzhong City (external validation)
Key_Novelty: First longitudinal serum-BDNF/FGF22 plus P300-latency model predicting MCI onset in depression
Primary_Limitation: Preliminary exploratory study with a modest, imbalanced sample requiring validation in larger cohorts.
Open_Problems: - Open Problems: Limited insight from the selected indices; need for larger validation and more precise multi-factor models; imbalanced groups. - Applications: Early clinical screening and risk stratification for MCI in depression; cost-tiered testing (FGF22+P300 latency as a cheaper option). - Methodologies: Longitudinal cohort follow-up; ELISA serum biomarkers; oddball-paradigm ERP; forward logistic stepwise regression; ROC and correlation analysis; external validation. - Achievable Outcomes: A validated low-cost predictive model (AUC ~0.79, accuracy ~0.81) to guide early intervention for cognitive decline in depression.

Modality: Structural MRI (high-resolution 3D T1-weighted, 1.5T) - sulcal morphometry and cortical thickness
Method_Architecture: Sulcal-based morphometry (surface, depth, length, width) from 106 sulci via BrainVISA/Morphologist with manual node-level relabelling, plus FreeSurfer cortical thickness; classification via logistic-model ROC, Leave-One-Out CV, and ISOMAP dimensionality reduction with a linear-kernel SVM.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.907 (best MCIc-vs-MCInc predictor; accuracy 0.892, Acc)
Dataset: Single-site retrospective cohort from S.Orsola-Malpighi / IRCCS Istituto delle Scienze Neurologiche di Bologna (Functional MR Unit, Bologna, Italy); HC from local Neuroimaging Laboratory database
Key_Novelty: First MCI-conversion sulcal study with manual node-level relabelling of all 106 sulci
Primary_Limitation: Small single-site cohort (esp. 12 MCInc) with in-sample/LOO validation, no independent test set
Open_Problems: Open Problems: reproducibility of sulcal-width predictors given high inter-subject variability across sites/scanners, and whether sulcal widening is independent of cortical thinning. Applications: prognostic stratification of MCI for AD conversion; imaging biomarker for prodromal AD. Methodologies: BrainVISA/Morphologist sulcal morphometry with manual relabelling, ROC/LOO validation, ISOMAP+SVM. Achievable Outcomes: AUC ~0.91 for MCIc vs MCInc with a single sulcal-width feature; multivariate accuracy ~0.865.
Journal: Journal of Alzheimer's Disease 99 (2024) 177-190, IOS Press

Modality: rs-fMRI (resting-state functional MRI); T1-weighted structural MRI used for cortical thickness covariates
Method_Architecture: Intrinsic neural timescale (INT) estimated from rs-fMRI autocorrelation AUC across cortical/subcortical hierarchies, then analysed with linear mixed-effect modeling of INT by hierarchical level (covariates age, sex, head motion, cortical thickness), ComBat site harmonization, and pairwise ROI comparisons with effect sizes.
Best_Metric: Cohen's d = -0.562 (largest reported effect size; inferior temporal, MCI-Converter)
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative); hierarchical levels derived from 100 unrelated HCP (Human Connectome Project) subjects
Sample_N_Approx: 904 analyzed (476 CN / 262 MCI / 57 Converter / 109 AD; from 945 baseline)
Key_Novelty: Altered hierarchical INT gradients distinguish stable MCI from AD/Converter via rs-fMRI
Primary_Limitation: Group classification depends on baseline/end-visit status; stable MCI may later convert, and sample is largely Caucasian.
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether stable MCI subjects later convert; INT relationship to amyloid-beta, phosphorylated tau, and symptom severity unexplored; generalizability beyond a largely Caucasian sample. Applications: INT as an additional measure for AD prediction and a stable diagnostic biomarker; disrupted E/I-balance regions as therapeutic targets. Methodologies: rs-fMRI INT via autocorrelation AUC, ComBat harmonization, LME of hierarchical gradients, future multivariate ML for conversion. Achievable Outcomes: early detection of pathological E/I imbalance before clinical conversion; INT-based conversion biomarker integrating cognitive panels.
Journal: The Journal of Neuroscience (Society for Neuroscience), Neurobiology of Disease section, June 19, 2024, 44(25):e2024232024

Modality: Multimodal neuroimaging - structural MRI, t-fMRI, rs-fMRI, MRS, ASL, DTI, PET (amyloid/tau/FDG), SPECT, and NIRF optical imaging
Method_Architecture: Systematic narrative literature review (PubMed, EMBASE; Jan 2000-April 2023) of nine neuroimaging modalities, organised within the NIA-AA AT(N) biomarker framework with summary tables of affected brain regions and biomarker categories in MCI vs AD.
Best_Metric: Not reported (qualitative review; no quantitative performance metric reported)
Dataset: Not reported in source (literature corpus from PubMed and EMBASE, English, January 2000-end of April 2023; no specific named cohort dataset)
Key_Novelty: Comparative review of 9 neuroimaging modalities for AD/MCI biomarkers within the AT(N) framework
Primary_Limitation: Reviewed studies are mostly cross-sectional with small cohorts (10-100); no pooled quantitative synthesis or study count
Open_Problems: Open Problems: reliance on cross-sectional, small-cohort (10-100 participant) studies; no single modality satisfies all biomarker criteria; lack of standardized large-scale multicentre longitudinal data. Applications: presymptomatic AD/MCI detection, MCI-to-AD conversion prediction, progression tracking, and differential diagnosis from VaD/DLB/FTD/PDD. Methodologies: multimodal/composite neuroimaging biomarker combination, high angular resolution diffusion imaging, multimodal NIRF probe design, DTI+AI integration. Achievable Outcomes: improved diagnostic accuracy, earlier non-invasive diagnosis, and potential inclusion of new modality biomarkers in the AT(N) classification system.
Journal: Psychoradiology, 2023, Vol. 3, 1-17 (Oxford University Press, on behalf of WCSM/WCH, Sichuan University)

Method_Architecture: Error-processing ERP component analysis (ERN, CRN, Pe, P300) recorded with 32-channel EEG during a modified Eriksen flanker task, with ICA artifact rejection and ERPLAB component extraction; statistical group comparison (ANOVA, post-hoc, paired t-test) and Pearson correlation with CANTAB cognitive subtests.
Best_Metric: Not reported (no classification accuracy/AUC; group differences reported as p-values, e.g., correct performance p=0.000; ERN peak amplitude Cz p=0.000)
Dataset: Primary data collected from participants recruited at the Memory Clinic of Tehran University of Medical Sciences; EEG recorded at the National Brain Mapping Laboratory (NBML)
Key_Novelty: First error-processing ERP comparison across AD, MCI, controls; links ERN to cognition.
Primary_Limitation: Small sample size (16 AD, 16 MCI, 15 controls) limiting robustness and generalizability.
Open_Problems: Open Problems: clinical/pathological heterogeneity of MCI and AD complicates reliable prediction of MCI-to-AD transition; small sample limits generalizability. Applications: ERN amplitude and accuracy of post-error responses as noninvasive neuromarkers for MCI and its progression to AD; P300 amplitude to detect MCI. Methodologies: modified Eriksen flanker task with EEG/ERP extraction (ERN, CRN, Pe, P300) plus CANTAB cognitive subtests and Pearson correlation. Achievable Outcomes: distinguishing AD, MCI, and controls via error-processing performance and ERN amplitude, correlating ERN with spatial working memory and new learning.
Journal: Journal of Alzheimer's Disease Reports 8 (2024) 681-696, IOS Press

Modality: Structural MRI (3D T1; VBM gray matter volume, SBM cortical thickness/sulcal depth/gyrification, subcortical shape); plus clinical/cognitive assessments.
Method_Architecture: Causal-inference epidemiology (propensity score matching 1:2 and IPTW) on longitudinal ADNI MCI patients stratified by diabetes status, combined with VBM/SBM and FSL-FIRST subcortical shape analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis to assess MCI-to-AD conversion and brain-cognition associations.
Best_Metric: Not reported (no classification accuracy/AUC; key result is AD proportion at 12 months: 8.82% vs 2.45%, P=0.026)
Dataset: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database (www.loni.ucla.edu/ADNI; downloaded June 12, 2023)
Key_Novelty: First to show DM accelerates MCI-to-AD within 1 year and drives nucleus accumbens atrophy.
Primary_Limitation: DM identified by self-reported medical history; small DM group sample size, especially after PSM.
Open_Problems: Open Problems: the impact of DM on MCI-to-AD conversion during later progression stages needs in-depth future investigation. Applications: the nucleus accumbens as a novel shared therapeutic target/link between DM and AD. Methodologies: combined PSM/IPTW with VBM, SBM, and FSL-FIRST subcortical shape analysis on longitudinal ADNI data. Achievable Outcomes: identifying the first year post-MCI diagnosis as the optimal therapeutic window for timely early intervention to delay MCI-to-AD conversion in DM patients.
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia (Alzheimer's Dement.) 2024;20:4583-4593; Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of Alzheimer's Association

Method_Architecture: Randomized controlled cross-over study of chiropractic spinal manipulation versus control in MCI patients using 62-channel resting-state EEG; per-band relative-power differences classified with an SVM (20 runs, 70/30 splits), assessed with a non-parametric cluster-based permutation test and inter-/intra-hemispheric coherence analysis.
Best_Metric: 99.74 Acc (SVM accuracy, beta2 band)
Dataset: Own/private EEG dataset collected at Railway General Hospital, Rawalpindi, Pakistan (26 MCI patients); available upon reasonable request
Key_Novelty: First study of chiropractic spinal manipulation effects on resting-state EEG in MCI patients.
Primary_Limitation: Small sample size (26), no control group, and no statistically significant permutation-test cluster.
Open_Problems: Open Problems: no permutation-test cluster reached significance; the exact cause of MCI remains unknown; small sample and lack of control group impede causal inference. Applications: chiropractic spinal manipulation as a non-pharmacological intervention that may augment cognitive function and potentially slow MCI-to-AD progression. Methodologies: combined cluster-based permutation testing, SVM classification of per-band relative-power differences, and inter-/intra-hemispheric coherence analysis on resting-state EEG. Achievable Outcomes: high SVM separation of chiropractic vs control changes (up to 99.74 in beta2); significant interhemispheric coherence increase across all regions post-intervention.

Modality: MRI / diffusion MRI - free-water diffusion tensor imaging (fw-DTI), with T1-weighted structural MRI for volumetrics
Method_Architecture: Single-shell free-water-corrected DTI (f-index, fw-FA) on ADNI with ComBat harmonization, voxel-based statistical modeling (ANCOVA with TFCE/FWE), ROC/AUC discrimination, voxel-based Spearman correlations with MMSE, whole-WM ROI analysis, and ANTs volumetric segmentation.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.84 (fw-FA, EMCI vs LMCI ROC discrimination)
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative); single-shell diffusion MRI subset
Key_Novelty: First fw-DTI study of white matter microstructure differences between EMCI and LMCI.
Primary_Limitation: Single-shell dMRI acquisition limits accuracy and precludes advanced multi-shell diffusion models.
Open_Problems: Open Problems: single-shell acquisition limits accuracy; A/T/N variability causes CN-EMCI overlap; ADNI MCI subtyping relies on a single episodic memory measure. Applications: discriminating MCI subtypes, monitoring disease progression, and guiding targeted interventions to preserve white matter integrity. Methodologies: multi-shell fw-DTI, DKI, and NODDI; ComBat harmonization; voxel-based correlation and ROC analyses. Achievable Outcomes: fw-FA as a reliable biomarker distinguishing EMCI, LMCI, and CN, integrable with cognitive/fluid biomarkers into diagnostic workflows.

Modality: Multimodal neuroimaging - volumetric/cortical-thickness MRI + amyloid-PET (florbetapir; PIB in AIBL), plus non-imaging clinical/genetic data
Method_Architecture: ADPacer, an ordinal learning model recasting MCI-to-AD conversion-pace prediction as a set of C-1 ordered binary SVM-style classifiers (RBF kernel with embedded feature weighting, dual QP via CPLEX) that uniquely leverages label-ambiguous training samples; integrates MRI, amyloid-PET, and non-imaging features with SHAP for modality interpretation.
Best_Metric: 0.95 Acc (binary task class 1-3 vs 4, ADNI CV); best ordinal overall accuracy 0.83 Acc
Dataset: ADNI (primary) and AIBL (secondary)
Key_Novelty: Ordinal pace-of-conversion model that uses label-ambiguous samples to augment training.
Primary_Limitation: Small sample size (amyloid-positive MCI only); weak AIBL external validation (tracer mismatch, small N).
Open_Problems: Open Problems: small, high-dimensional samples for amyloid-positive MCI; heterogeneity within the slow/non-converter class; lack of population-level pace distribution statistics. Applications: a deployable predictive tool usable at any visit when a patient is amyloid-positive MCI, informing future disease course. Methodologies: ordinal learning recast as ordered binary classifiers incorporating label-ambiguous samples, embedded feature-weighting within CV, SHAP for modality contribution. Achievable Outcomes: balanced 0.83 ordinal accuracy and up to 0.94-0.95 binary accuracy on ADNI, with preliminary cross-dataset transfer to AIBL.
Journal: IISE Transactions on Healthcare Systems Engineering, 2024; 14(2): 167-177

Modality: Neuroimaging - resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) functional connectivity; with supporting PET (amyloid-beta AV45/FBB, FDG, tau AV-1451) and T1-weighted MRI
Method_Architecture: Prognostic survival model using cortex-wide functional-connectivity gradients/manifolds from baseline rs-fMRI (diffusion map embedding) plus subcortical-weighted manifold degrees, fed into a penalized Cox proportional-hazards regression (elastic net) with clinical covariates and Weibull AFT imputation of interval-censored conversion times; evaluated by concordance index and externally validated on OASIS3.
Best_Metric: C-index 0.716 (concordance index; OASIS risk external validation, 0.716 +/- 0.015)
Dataset: ADNI (ADNI-GO/2/3) discovery dataset; OASIS3 (OASIS risk dataset and OASIS diagnosis dataset) external validation; HCP database used for gradient-template alignment
Sample_N_Approx: 116 unique (ADNI 68 unique / 115 samples; OASIS risk 33; OASIS diagnosis 803)
Key_Novelty: Survival Cox model of AD conversion using FC connectome manifolds and penalized regression.
Primary_Limitation: Small discovery sample with no left-truncation modeling; repeated within-subject scans treated as independent.
Open_Problems: Open Problems: explicitly accounting for left truncation and correlated repeated measurements within survival models for AD conversion remains unsolved. Applications: FC manifold-based risk scores as quantitative prognosis-prediction markers for early diagnosis and treatment planning. Methodologies: connectome-manifold (gradient) techniques combined with penalized Cox regression (elastic net) and Weibull AFT imputation of interval-censored conversion times. Achievable Outcomes: a prognostic risk score stratifying fast vs slow converters and correlating with PET pathology and clinical severity, validated externally (OASIS C-index 0.716 +/- 0.015).
population_specificity: CN/MCI at risk of AD conversion

Modality: FDG-PET (18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography); supporting structural T1-weighted MRI; Abeta-PET (18F-florbetapir) and tau-PET (18F-flortaucipir) where available
Method_Architecture: Voxel-wise statistical parametric mapping (SPM12) of cerebellum-normalized FDG-PET SUVr with bilateral retrosplenial-cortex seed ROIs and partial-volume correction; classical statistics (two-way/three-factor ANOVA, multiple logistic regression, bootstrap estimation of Cohen's d) comparing MCI converters versus non-converters in ADNI.
Best_Metric: Logistic regression predictor significance: RSC FDG-PET SUVr |Z|=3.181, p=0.0015 (no Acc/AUC/F1 reported)
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) - ADNI-1, ADNI-GO, ADNI-2 phases; data downloaded February 13, 2024
Sample_N_Approx: 399 (202 MCI non-converters [114 M/88 F] / 197 MCI-AD converters [121 M/76 F])
Key_Novelty: Large-cohort validation: RSC hypometabolism predicts MCI-to-AD conversion in Abeta/tau-negative cases
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective, ADNI-only observational design; Abeta-negative subgroup small and mechanisms unexamined
Open_Problems: Open Problems: the mechanisms through which RSC hypometabolism arises within early MCI remain unexamined. Applications: RSC metabolic activity as an early biomarker to identify MCI subjects most at risk of decline, including Abeta/tau-negative cases. Methodologies: FDG-PET SUVr analysis with bilateral RSC seed ROIs, SPM12 voxel-wise SPM, partial-volume correction, and multiple logistic regression combining RSC SUVr with sex and Abeta/tau-PET. Achievable Outcomes: incorporating RSC hypometabolism into multi-classifier predictive models to strengthen prediction of AD progression risk and conversion rate.
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia (Alzheimer's Dement.) 2024;20:8979-8986 - Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of the Alzheimer's Association

Modality: Structural MRI radiomics (cerebellar + hippocampal texture/shape) plus structural-connectome graph-theory network features
Method_Architecture: Cerebellar and hippocampal radiomics (first-order, GLCM, GLSZM, NGTDM, shape) + graph-theory connectome (degree centrality across 26 cerebellar lobules); LASSO/forward-stepwise feature selection; multi-classifier ML (AdaBoost, SVM, LR-LASSO, Gaussian process) chosen per task with DeLong comparison; SHAP interpretation; Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional-hazards conversion modelling. Trained on ADNI, tested on independent in-house cohort.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.864 (MCI vs NC, independent test); NC->MCI conversion AUC 0.818 (cerebellar) / 0.852 (combined clinical-radiomic); Cox HR 4.75
Dataset: ADNI (n=1319, training) + in-house Dalian Medical University cohort (n=308, testing)
Sample_N_Approx: 1627 (1319 ADNI train / 308 in-house test; conversion subset 371 NC: 137 progressed / 234 stable)
Key_Novelty: Cerebellar radiomic-network model outperforms hippocampal for MCI detection and NC-to-MCI conversion
Primary_Limitation: Cerebellar edge limited to MCI/conversion (hippocampus better for AD); modest external test set; retrospective
Open_Problems: Open Problems: which cerebellar radiomic/network signatures map to amyloid/tau stages and generalise across scanners. Applications: early clinical-trial enrichment and NC-to-MCI conversion risk stratification. Methodologies: cerebellar-lobule radiomics + graph-theory connectome, multi-classifier ML with DeLong comparison, SHAP, Cox/KM conversion modelling. Achievable Outcomes: a staged cerebellum-then-hippocampus model across the NC-MCI-AD continuum with calibrated conversion-risk categories.
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia (Alzheimer's Dement.) 2025;21:e14361 - Wiley on behalf of the Alzheimer's Association

Modality: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), resting-state prefrontal functional connectivity
Method_Architecture: Resting-state prefrontal fNIRS; channel-wise functional connectivity; network-based statistics (NBS) for subnetwork detection; Pearson correlation with MoCA; multiple linear regression (education duration + mean subnetwork FC predicting MoCA).
Best_Metric: Adjusted R2=0.257 (MoCA regression, F=24.723, p<0.001); MCI vs HC MoCA p<0.001 (no AUC)
Dataset: In-house single-centre cohort - Jiangbin Hospital, Guangxi, China
Key_Novelty: NBS on resting-state fNIRS reveals an enhanced, cognition-correlated right-PFC subnetwork in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional, single-centre; fNIRS cortical-only; compensatory interpretation unproven
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether the enhanced right-PFC subnetwork reflects compensation or early pathology, and whether it predicts conversion. Applications: low-cost fNIRS screening and neuromodulation target identification. Methodologies: resting-state fNIRS FC with network-based statistics and MoCA regression. Achievable Outcomes: a validated cognition-linked prefrontal fNIRS biomarker and intervention target.
Journal: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 2024;16:1416816 - Frontiers Media

Modality: Structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry of parietal subregions, Brainnetome Atlas BNA-246)
Method_Architecture: VBM with Human Brainnetome Atlas (BNA-246) parietal-subregion parcellation; ROC/AUC group discrimination; Cox proportional-hazards models for CN-to-MCI and MCI-to-AD conversion; volume-cognition correlation. ADNI cohort (CN/EMCI/LMCI/AD).
Best_Metric: AUC 0.688 (left IPL_6_5 rostroventral area 39, AD vs CN); best subregion combos for CN->MCI and MCI->AD conversion (Cox)
Dataset: ADNI - 662 participants (228 CN / 221 EMCI / 112 LMCI / 101 AD)
Key_Novelty: Parietal angular-gyrus subregion volumetry predicts CN-to-MCI and MCI-to-AD conversion (ADNI)
Primary_Limitation: Modest single-marker AUC (0.688); retrospective ADNI-only; no external validation
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether parietal-subregion atrophy is causally upstream and how it interacts with amyloid/tau spread. Applications: subregion-level early-detection markers for CN-to-MCI and MCI-to-AD conversion risk. Methodologies: BNA-246 VBM parcellation, ROC/AUC discrimination, Cox conversion modelling. Achievable Outcomes: a parietal-subregion signature integrated into multimodal AD risk models.
Journal: Journal of Integrative Neuroscience (J. Integr. Neurosci.) 2025;24(1):25991 - IMR Press

Modality: Neuromodulation - transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS); non-imaging intervention review
Method_Architecture: Narrative literature review; synthesis of tDCS mechanism (neuronal-excitability modulation), efficacy-influencing factors (neuroanatomy, current parameters, electrode montage), domain-specific cognitive outcomes (memory, attention, processing speed, executive, language), and safety.
Best_Metric: Qualitative synthesis: short-term memory/attention gains, moderate processing-speed gains; inconsistent executive/language; long-term uncertain (no pooled effect size)
Dataset: Not applicable (literature review)
Key_Novelty: Narrative review: tDCS gives short-term memory/attention gains in MCI; long-term efficacy uncertain
Primary_Limitation: Narrative (non-systematic) review; no pooled effect sizes; underlying evidence heterogeneous and short-term
Open_Problems: Open Problems: long-term efficacy, optimal individualised stimulation parameters, and predictors of response. Applications: portable/home-based cognitive enhancement and dementia-progression delay in MCI. Methodologies: narrative synthesis of tDCS mechanisms, efficacy factors, and cognitive outcomes. Achievable Outcomes: standardised, biomarker-guided tDCS protocols validated in large longitudinal trials.

Modality: EEG - event-related potentials (sensory P1/N1/P2 and cognitive P300/P600/P900) during a sustained visuo-attentive task
Method_Architecture: EEG ERPs during a sustained visual-attention task; extraction of sensory (P1, N1, P2) and cognitive (P300, P600, P900) components; cross-group comparison HS/SCD/MCI; ERP-performance relationship analysis.
Best_Metric: NA
Dataset: In-house cohort - University of Florence / AOU Careggi (CRIDEM) and IRCCS Don Carlo Gnocchi, Italy
Key_Novelty: ERP across SCD/MCI/HS shows non-monotonic pattern: MCI compensatory enhancement reverses SCD decline
Primary_Limitation: Small HS group; cross-sectional; single task; compensatory interpretation not longitudinally validated
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether MCI compensatory ERP enhancement predicts progression, and its neural/pathological basis. Applications: ERP-based early-stage stratification and prognosis for SCD/MCI. Methodologies: task-based sensory/cognitive ERP component analysis across the SCD-MCI continuum. Achievable Outcomes: a validated ERP marker set supporting prognosis in cognitive decline.

Modality: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) resting-state spectral power/covariance, combined with structural MRI and clinical variables
Method_Architecture: Resting-state MEG spectral analysis (band-limited power incl. 16-38 Hz) + covariance features; logistic-regression additive modelling of clinical/MEG/MRI variables; cross-validated high-dimensional multimodal classification (AUC mean+/-SD). BioFIND dataset.
Best_Metric: NA
Dataset: BioFIND (multisite resting-state MEG) - 117 MCI
Key_Novelty: MEG 16-38Hz power + MRI predict MCI-to-AD; multimodal AUC 0.81 > MEG 0.74 / MRI 0.77 (BioFIND)
Primary_Limitation: Single-cohort (BioFIND) cross-validation, no external test; MEG cost/availability; moderate combined AUC
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether MEG adds value over plasma biomarkers and generalises across MEG systems. Applications: non-invasive prodromal-AD progression prediction and treatment-response monitoring. Methodologies: resting-state MEG spectral/covariance features, additive logistic regression, cross-validated multimodal classification. Achievable Outcomes: an externally validated MEG+MRI+clinical panel for MCI-to-AD progression risk.

Method_Architecture: Amyloid-PET (A) and FDG-PET (N) with A/N positive-negative classification; longitudinal clinical follow-up to AD dementia; sensitivity/specificity/NPV/PPV by follow-up year; time-to-conversion (survival) analysis across amyloid and combined A/N groups.
Best_Metric: Amyloid-PET sens 100%(yr1)/94.67%(yr4), NPV 100%/88.24%; FDG-PET spec 85%, PPV 88%; A+/N+ conversion 27.79mo vs A+/N- 37.38mo (no AUC)
Dataset: In-house clinical cohort - Clinica Universidad de Navarra, Spain (2013-2021)
Key_Novelty: Combined Amyloid-PET + FDG-PET predicts earlier short-term MCI-to-AD conversion than amyloid alone
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre observational; modest N over 8-year window; no unified AUC; no external validation
Open_Problems: Open Problems: optimal biomarker sequencing/thresholds for short-term prognosis and integration with plasma biomarkers. Applications: memory-clinic prognostic workflow to identify near-term converters for early disease-modifying therapy. Methodologies: A/N PET classification, diagnostic-accuracy metrics over follow-up, survival/time-to-conversion analysis. Achievable Outcomes: a validated staged dual-PET protocol for short-term MCI-to-AD conversion prediction.
Journal: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging 2025;52:3567-3577 - Springer

Modality: Structural MRI (hippocampal-subfield volumetry) plus resting-state fMRI seed-based functional connectivity
Method_Architecture: Automated hippocampal-subfield volumetry (CA1, CA2/3, CA4, GC-DG, subiculum, presubiculum, HATA, fimbria, molecular layer); ANCOVA group comparison with TIV covariate; seed-based resting-state FC between subfields and cortical networks; FC-cognition correlation (naming, delayed recall). Two-centre PD-NC/PD-MCI/U-MCI/HC.
Best_Metric: Group subfield-volume differences (bilateral GC-DG/CA4/CA2-3 reduction in PD-MCI); GC-DG/CA4-posterior-DMN FC increased; FC-cognition correlations (no AUC)
Dataset: Two-centre in-house cohort (PD-NC/PD-MCI/U-MCI/HC); not ADNI
Key_Novelty: PD-MCI: bilateral GC-DG/CA4/CA2-3 subfield atrophy + increased GC-DG/CA4-posterior-DMN connectivity
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional, unbalanced groups; corpus PDF supplement-only (main text confirmed from published record); compensatory FC unproven
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether GC-DG/CA4-pDMN hyperconnectivity is compensatory or pathological and whether subfield markers predict progression. Applications: subfield/connectivity markers to distinguish PD-MCI from unspecified MCI. Methodologies: hippocampal-subfield segmentation + seed-based rs-fMRI FC with cognition correlation. Achievable Outcomes: a subfield-resolved structural-functional signature for Parkinsonian cognitive decline.

Modality: EEG - quantitative EEG (qEEG) review: power spectrum, functional/effective connectivity, microstates, non-linear/entropy
Method_Architecture: Narrative review of qEEG biomarker families (power-spectrum/oscillatory, functional and effective connectivity, microstates, non-linear/entropy) for AD/MCI diagnosis and monitoring; qualitative synthesis, no primary analysis.
Best_Metric: Qualitative synthesis: reduced alpha / increased slow-band power tracks AD severity; entropy/complexity reduced in AD/MCI (no pooled effect size, no AUC)
Dataset: Not applicable (literature review)
Key_Novelty: Review of qEEG biomarkers (power, connectivity, microstates, entropy) for AD/MCI diagnosis
Primary_Limitation: Narrative (non-systematic) review; heterogeneous underlying qEEG methods; no standardisation/specificity established
Open_Problems: Open Problems: standardisation, cross-study reproducibility, and cross-dementia specificity of qEEG markers. Applications: low-cost diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring of AD/MCI. Methodologies: power spectrum, functional/effective connectivity, microstates, non-linear/entropy EEG analyses. Achievable Outcomes: a standardised multimodal qEEG biomarker panel integrated with imaging and clinical data.
Journal: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 2025;17:1522552 - Frontiers Media

Modality: Diffusion MRI (cortical microstructure) - minicolumn-related cortical disarray diffusivity, with macrostructural MRI comparators
Method_Architecture: Minicolumn-related cortical diffusivity metrics (AngleR, PerpPD+, ParlPD) from diffusion MRI vs macrostructural measures (hippocampal/cortical volume, cortical thickness); Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with biomarker stratification; cognitive correlations. NACC cohort.
Best_Metric: Cortical diffusivity PerpPD+ outperforms hippocampal volume / cortical volume / cortical thickness in Kaplan-Meier survival (faster MCI->dementia conversion); cognitive associations p<0.001 (no AUC)
Dataset: NACC (National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center)
Key_Novelty: Cortical minicolumn diffusivity beats macrostructural markers for MCI-to-dementia prediction (NACC)
Primary_Limitation: Observational NACC-only; survival endpoints without AUC; proprietary pipeline needs external replication
Open_Problems: Open Problems: external validation of cortical-disarray metrics and their relation to amyloid/tau pathology. Applications: prognostic stratification of MCI for early intervention and trial enrichment. Methodologies: minicolumn-related cortical diffusivity (AngleR, PerpPD+, ParlPD) with Kaplan-Meier survival. Achievable Outcomes: a validated microstructural prognostic marker integrated with fluid/PET biomarkers.
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia (Alzheimer's Dement.) 2025;21:e70310 - Wiley on behalf of the Alzheimer's Association

Modality: Clinical/tabular - plasma/CSF allostatic-load index (neuroendocrine/immune/metabolic) plus AD biomarkers (plasma/CSF amyloid-tau, hippocampal volume)
Method_Architecture: Allostatic load index (ALI) from plasma neuroendocrine/immunological/metabolic markers with 12-month change; AD biomarkers (plasma Abeta42, CSF Abeta1-42, CSF tau, hippocampal volume); longitudinal association/logistic modeling of MCI-to-dementia conversion with moderation by age, APOE e4, and baseline tau. ADNI, 36 months.
Best_Metric: One-point ALI increase associated with 15% higher MCI-to-AD conversion odds (OR ~1.15); ALI linked to high CSF tau, plasma Abeta42, low CSF Abeta1-42 (no AUC)
Dataset: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative)
Key_Novelty: Rising allostatic load raises MCI-to-AD conversion odds 15%; interacts with CSF tau/Abeta (ADNI)
Primary_Limitation: Observational ADNI-only, associational; modest effect size; no interventional/external validation
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether allostatic load is causally upstream of amyloid/tau or a parallel modifier. Applications: stress-index monitoring and stress-reduction interventions as modifiable adjuncts to risk stratification. Methodologies: longitudinal allostatic-load index with biomarker and conversion modeling. Achievable Outcomes: a validated modifiable stress marker integrated into MCI progression-risk models.
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring 2025;17:e70140 - Wiley on behalf of the Alzheimer's Association

Modality: Multimodal - MEG (alpha power) + structural MRI (hippocampal volume) + plasma (Abeta42/40, p-tau217) + Abeta-PET and tau-PET
Method_Architecture: Multimodal biomarker Cox proportional-hazards regression with time-varying effects: MEG alpha power, MRI hippocampal volume, plasma Abeta42/40 and p-tau217, neocortical Abeta-PET and entorhinal tau-PET; compared against clinical/genetic baseline for CU-to-MCI progression. PREVENT-AD.
Best_Metric: Cox progression-risk (time-varying): MEG alpha short-term, neocortical Abeta long-term; plasma Abeta42/40, p-tau217, tau-PET each higher risk; hippocampal volume non-predictive (no AUC)
Dataset: PREVENT-AD (Pre-symptomatic Evaluation of Novel/Experimental Treatments for AD)
Key_Novelty: Time-varying multimodal markers predict CU-to-MCI: MEG alpha early, Abeta late; hippocampus null
Primary_Limitation: Preprint (not peer-reviewed); small enriched single cohort; MEG/PET cost; no external validation
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether MEG adds value over plasma markers at scale, and mechanism of time-shifting biomarker importance. Applications: individualized preclinical-AD risk prediction and prevention-trial enrichment. Methodologies: multimodal (MEG + MRI + plasma + Abeta/tau PET) Cox regression with time-varying effects. Achievable Outcomes: a validated time-sensitive multimodal risk model for CU-to-MCI progression.
Journal: medRxiv preprint (posted 22 September 2025) - not certified by peer review

Modality: EEG - resting-state EEG functional connectivity (Phase Lag Index) with minimum spanning tree network topology
Method_Architecture: Resting-state EEG; Phase Lag Index connectivity; minimum spanning tree metrics (diameter, eccentricity, maximum degree) across five frequency bands; Kruskal-Wallis group comparison; correlations with cognition, severity, and CSF biomarkers (t-Tau, p-Tau, Abeta1-42).
Best_Metric: Frequency-specific MST differences (AD theta+/beta-; MCI-AD delta max-degree); beta mean PLI and theta eccentricity discriminate AD/MCI-AD from HC; MST-CSF correlations (no AUC)
Dataset: In-house cohort - Nanjing Brain Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, China
Key_Novelty: rsEEG minimum-spanning-tree topology (theta+/beta-) tracks AD-spectrum severity and CSF biomarkers
Primary_Limitation: Small cross-sectional sample (MCI-AD n=14); statistical not classifier discrimination; single-centre
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether MST-EEG metrics predict conversion and generalise across sites. Applications: low-cost early-AD diagnosis and progression monitoring. Methodologies: PLI connectivity + MST metrics across frequency bands with CSF correlation. Achievable Outcomes: a validated, CSF-linked rsEEG network biomarker for AD staging.
Journal: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 2025;17:1604345 - Frontiers Media

Modality: Structural MRI (gray-matter atrophy patterns; cortical-to-hippocampal ratio; tau-related cortical-degeneration marker), anchored to histopathology
Method_Architecture: MRI gray-matter atrophy-pattern classification derived from histopathologically confirmed pure-AD vs AD+ (limbic TDP-43/AGD co-pathology) cases; cortical-to-hippocampal ratio; MRI tau-associated cortical-degeneration marker; applied to an independent clinical MCI/dementia cohort with cognitive and progression analyses.
Best_Metric: AD+-pattern classification of co-pathology; tau-related cortical degeneration is the primary progression predictor; hippocampal GM non-prognostic in mild dementia (no AUC)
Dataset: Histopathology-confirmed autopsy cohort (n=75) for pattern derivation; independent clinical cohort (MCI n=224, dementia n=221) via ADNI
Sample_N_Approx: 520 (36 pure-AD + 39 AD+ histopath; 224 MCI + 221 dementia clinical/ADNI)
Key_Novelty: MRI atrophy pattern detects limbic non-AD co-pathology in vivo; flags faster-declining MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small histopath training set; indirect pattern-based co-pathology inference; generalisability untested
Open_Problems: Open Problems: direct in-vivo confirmation of TDP-43/AGD co-pathology and stage-specific biomarker weighting. Applications: prognostic stratification and trial enrichment for MCI/AD with suspected co-pathology. Methodologies: histopath-derived MRI atrophy-pattern classification; cortical/hippocampal ratio; tau-degeneration marker. Achievable Outcomes: a validated in-vivo MRI co-pathology marker integrated with prognosis.
Journal: Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2025;17:236 - BMC / Springer Nature

Modality: Multimodal MRI (structural + functional gray-matter eigenmodes; structure-function coupling) with amyloid-PET
Method_Architecture: Gray-matter-eigenmode structure-function coupling; Shannon entropy (fMRI projected onto structural eigenmodes) and temperature (eigenmode-based FC reconstruction); multimodal MRI + amyloid-PET; diagnostic classification (ROC/AUC), amyloid-beta prediction, and MCI subtype (reversed/stable/progressed) stratification across BABRI and ADNI.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.901 (left-hemisphere entropy, CN vs MCI); amyloid-burden prediction error reduction 38.7-42.1% (p<0.01); AD-vs-CN/MCI entropy delta 8-21% (p<0.001)
Dataset: BABRI (Beijing Aging Brain Rejuvenation Initiative, N=135) + ADNI (N=275)
Key_Novelty: Gray-matter-eigenmode entropy: novel biomarker, CN-vs-MCI AUC 0.901, predicts Abeta (BABRI+ADNI)
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional (biphasic progression inferred); complex pipeline needing replication; temperature index uninformative
Open_Problems: Open Problems: longitudinal confirmation of biphasic progression and mechanism of hemispheric asymmetry. Applications: non-invasive early AD diagnosis, amyloid-burden estimation, and MCI subtype stratification. Methodologies: gray-matter-eigenmode structure-function coupling; entropy via fMRI projection onto structural eigenmodes; cross-cohort classification. Achievable Outcomes: a validated eigenmode-entropy biomarker for diagnosis, amyloid prediction, and trajectory stratification.

Modality: Clinical/tabular - modifiable behaviours (social/creative/physical activity) with structural MRI hippocampal volume and neuropsychological memory tests
Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional COMPASS-ND analysis; total hippocampal volume; verbal (RAVLT) and spatial (BVSM) delayed-recall memory; within-diagnostic-group regression with modifiable-risk-factor main effects and hippocampal-volume x activity interaction (moderation) terms; t-contrasts; collinearity checks.
Best_Metric: Moderation (interaction) effects: modifiable activities weaken hippocampal-volume-to-memory coupling in SCI (significant), absent in MCI (no AUC; two-tailed tests alpha<0.05)
Dataset: COMPASS-ND (Canadian Consortium on Neurodegeneration in Aging multi-site cohort)
Sample_N_Approx: 606 (CU/SCI/MCI/AD older adults; 103 no social engagement + 503 engaged)
Key_Novelty: Cognitive-reserve behaviours moderate hippocampus-memory link in SCI but not once MCI begins
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional; self-reported categorical activity measures; cohort/measure-specific
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether reserve's moderating effect can be prolonged into the MCI stage and its mechanism. Applications: timing lifestyle/prevention interventions before MCI onset; public-health policy. Methodologies: within-group moderation regression of hippocampal-volume x modifiable-activity interactions on memory. Achievable Outcomes: evidence-based intervention windows for modifiable-risk-factor programmes.
Journal: Canadian Journal on Aging / La Revue canadienne du vieillissement 2026;45(1):38-47 - Cambridge University Press

Modality: Vascular ultrasound (carotid intima-media thickness) + structural MRI (periventricular white matter hyperintensity volume)
Method_Architecture: Carotid ultrasound mean CIMT + 3T MRI PWMH volume; comprehensive neuropsychological PD-MCI diagnosis (10 tests/5 domains); multivariate logistic regression; ROC/AUC with DeLong Z-test comparing combined vs single markers.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.908 (combined CIMT+PWMH) vs PWMH 0.705 / CIMT 0.722 alone (both P<0.001); PWMH OR 2.114, CIMT OR 2.027
Dataset: In-house prospective cohort - Chongqing University Jiangjin Hospital, China
Key_Novelty: Carotid IMT + periventricular WMH combined (AUC 0.908) beats either alone for PD-MCI diagnosis
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional single-centre (concurrent diagnosis not conversion); internal AUC only; operator-dependent CIMT
Open_Problems: Open Problems: whether combined vascular markers predict conversion (PD-MCI to PDD). Applications: accessible vascular-imaging screening to flag high-risk PD patients.
