Primary_Limitation: Single-wave cross-sectional design prevents causal inference, and ASMI was estimated from an anthropometric equation rather than DXA or BIA
Open_Problems: Direct muscle-to-brain signalling mechanism unidentified; residual mediators (physical activity, basal metabolic rate, atherosclerosis) unexamined; direction of the sleep and leisure moderation unknown; leisure frequency only binary; sleep quality, efficiency and daytime dysfunction untested

Modality: Multimodal group intervention (exercise + cognitive training + social activity + nutrition), MoCA-J, physical function tests, mood scales
Method_Architecture: Single-arm feasibility study; paired t-tests, repeated-measures ANOVA, Cohen d
Best_Metric: Not reported - no classification metric; MoCA-J change +2.2 (d=0.91, p=0.002)
Dataset: Proprietary Japanese community sample (Kagoshima/NCGG)
Key_Novelty: First Japanese multimodal MCI community intervention - MoCA-J d=0.91 with 12-week follow-up
Primary_Limitation: No control group; MoCA-J gain cannot be separated from practice effects, Hawthorne effects, or regression to the mean (baseline near MCI cutoff); N=12 underpowered; single-site Japanese sample limits generalisability.
Open_Problems: RCT with active control (social activity only); factorial design to isolate component contributions; longer follow-up; blinded outcome assessment.

Method_Architecture: Two-arm controlled clinical observation (VR rehabilitation training plus scalp/eye acupuncture vs VR alone); MMSE/MoCA scoring with ANOVA, ANCOVA and pooled fixed-/random-effects estimates; FBCSP with MIBIF feature selection described as system design only
Best_Metric: OR 2.74 (pooled total effective rate; Z = 3.38, P less than 0.0001); MoCA WMD 2.42 (95% CI 1.98-3.06); total effective rate 86.96% treatment vs 65.22% control (MMSE)
Dataset: Single-centre Chinese hospital sample - 48 MCI patients from the neurology outpatient and inpatient departments of a tertiary hospital (Petersen criteria, MMSE 24-30, MoCA below 26, age over 50); no public dataset
Key_Novelty: Two-arm MCI trial adding scalp and eye acupuncture to VR rehabilitation training.
Primary_Limitation: Very small single-centre trial (46 analysed) with no sham control, blinding or registration, internally inconsistent tables, and pooled meta-analytic statistics presented without any systematic-review protocol
Open_Problems: Mechanism of acupuncture in MCI still under research; VR cognitive intervention described as in its infancy; durability of the combined effect untested; the FBCSP/EEG pipeline is never validated on the study's own data

Modality: Semi-quantitative 115-item FFQ (Dietary Inflammatory Index and RRR dietary patterns) plus MoCA cognitive screening and routine clinical bloods in a T2DM clinic cohort
Method_Architecture: Reduced-rank regression dietary patterns, quartile logistic regression (3 nested adjustment models), restricted cubic splines, bootstrap mediation analysis
Best_Metric: OR 6.84 (95% CI 3.58-13.10) for MCI, highest vs lowest quartile of the high-meat and low-vegetable pattern (Model 3)
Dataset: Single-centre T2DM clinic sample, Department of Endocrinology, First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University, Harbin, China (Feb-Nov 2022)
Key_Novelty: First RRR dietary patterns linked to MCI in T2DM, with DII partially mediating the association
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional single-centre design with MoCA-only outcome and self-reported FFQ intake; temporal order and causation cannot be established and MCI cases are not aetiologically characterised
Open_Problems: Prospective cohorts and dietary intervention trials in T2DM; generalisability beyond the Chinese population; biomarker-anchored rather than screening-only MCI ascertainment; whether the Mediterranean-style benefit holds without olive oil and red wine
Journal: Endocrinologia, Diabetes y Nutricion (Elsevier Espana, on behalf of SEEN y SED)

Modality: Clinical/Population - randomised clinical trials of non-pharmacological therapy in older adults with MCI, neuropsychological and functional outcomes (systematic review, no primary data)
Method_Architecture: PRISMA-guided systematic search of six databases; Mendeley 1.19.8 deduplication; Excel data extraction; Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions six-domain risk-of-bias appraisal (high/low/imprecise); narrative categorical synthesis into four treatment families; no meta-analysis
Best_Metric: Not reported (narrative synthesis; heterogeneity of methods, instruments and objectives precluded meta-analysis or statistical grouping; only summary figure is a mean study sample of 87.64 subjects)
Dataset: 50 published randomised clinical trials 2011-2021: PubMed (34), ScienceDirect (7), ProQuest (3), Lilacs (2), EBSCO (2), Taylor & Francis (2); searched February-June 2021
Sample_N_Approx: 50 studies; mean sample 87.64 subjects per study; pooled participant total not reported
Key_Novelty: Bilingual PRISMA review grouping 50 MCI trials into four non-pharmacological therapy categories.
Primary_Limitation: Heterogeneity of interventions, instruments and objectives made meta-analysis impossible, so conclusions rest on narrative benefit statements from small trials (mean 87.64 subjects) with risk of bias concentrated in masking of participants, staff and evaluators; search limited to English and Spanish; no protocol registration, certainty grading or publication-bias assessment.
Open_Problems: Durability of benefit after the intervention stops (six trials made no long-term evaluation); generalisability from largely female samples to older men; whether motor-only interventions confer any cognitive benefit; whether virtual-reality computerised cognitive training extends to dementia; adequately powered masked trials with harmonised cognitive outcomes to enable the pooled per-category effect estimate this review could not compute.
Journal: Revista Colombiana de Psiquiatria (Elsevier Espana, S.L.U. / Asociacion Colombiana de Psiquiatria), 2023;52(4):372-379

Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional two-group clinical comparison (PD-nMCI vs PD-MCI); Mann-Whitney U with Wilcoxon r effect sizes, chi-squared with phi, Spearman bivariate and partial correlations controlling UPDRS-III, FDR correction, Shannon S-values
Best_Metric: Spearman partial rho 0.728 (Cognition) and rho 0.76 (Communication) vs motor-adjusted PDQ-39 Summary Index, PD-MCI group only
Dataset: Proprietary single-centre Colombian PD outpatient sample (Grupo de Neurociencias de Antioquia, Universidad de Antioquia, Medellin; project PRG-2014-768), not publicly available
Key_Novelty: First study relating subjective cognitive and communicative complaints to HRQoL in PD-MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small convenience sample of 40 with only 11 PD-MCI patients, limiting power and external validity; cross-sectional and retrospective with no follow-up, so no causal inference; no instrument specific to subjective complaint, anosognosia or mood, and the NPI is not mood-specific; non-significant age difference as a potential bias.
Open_Problems: Reproduce the exploratory findings in larger and more heterogeneous samples; longitudinal follow-up to establish direction of effect; determine how education moderates the complaint-HRQoL relation; identify which PDQ-39 Cognition and Communication items form a defensible patient-reported cognitive endpoint; test whether cognitive and speech rehabilitation improves HRQoL in PD-MCI.
Journal: Revista Colombiana de Psiquiatria 2023;52(4):305-313 (Asociacion Colombiana de Psiquiatria / Elsevier Espana); DOI 10.1016/j.rcp.2021.07.005

Modality: Voice acoustic features (17 features: F0, jitter, shimmer, HNR, intensity) from /a/ and /pa-ta-ka/ phrases
Method_Architecture: LightGBM gradient-boosting multiclass classifier; SMOTE oversampling; Optuna hyperparameter optimisation; 5-fold group CV
Best_Metric: Accuracy 66.7% (3-class, chance 33.3%); binary acc 93.8% (HE vs MCI+AD)
Dataset: Proprietary 2-hospital Japanese sample (Takeyama + Honjo Kodama)
Key_Novelty: Simple-phrase acoustic features classify HC/MCI/dementia via LightGBM (OvR AUC 0.81)
Primary_Limitation: Severe HE class imbalance (n=13) makes the 0.95 HE-vs-others AUC unstable; MCI-specific discrimination not reported separately; single-language Japanese sample leaves language-independence claim untested; no external validation; cross-sectional.
Open_Problems: External validation in non-Japanese speakers; larger balanced HE group; per-class AUC reporting; dementia-subtype discrimination; longitudinal monitoring of acoustic features.
Journal: The Journal of Aging Research & Lifestyle (JARLife) 2023

Modality: HABIT programme (MSS, BrainHQ, yoga, support groups, wellness); MMSE, memory self-efficacy, CES-D, anxiety, ECog, partner burden, satisfaction
Method_Architecture: Quasi-experimental pre-post comparison of two non-randomised cohorts; t-tests, Mann-Whitney U, Cohen d
Best_Metric: Not reported - no classification metric; satisfaction 5.8/7 virtual vs 6.5/7 in-person; anxiety d=0.39 virtual
Dataset: Proprietary Mayo Clinic sample (3 sites: Phoenix, La Crosse, Jacksonville)
Key_Novelty: Mayo HABIT virtual vs in-person MCI programme - comparable outcomes, high satisfaction (5.8/7)
Primary_Limitation: Quasi-experimental: cohorts time-separated (pre-COVID vs COVID), not randomised; in-person group had longer MCI duration (2.0 vs 0.7y) confounding format attribution; 95% White, 88% spousal partners; virtual group selected for tech capability; no longer-term outcomes.
Open_Problems: Prospective randomised or matched equivalence trial; duration-stratified analyses formalised; 6-12 month follow-up; digital-divide mitigation; diverse-population validation.
Journal: Mayo Clinic Proceedings: Innovations, Quality & Outcomes 2021

Modality: Telerehabilitation (Brunnstrom video exercises) with/without anodal tDCS 2mA dlPFC; NPRS/FPS, BRS, Ashworth, TUG, sfBBS, MMSE, IQCODE
Method_Architecture: Multi-arm parallel-group RCT protocol (CONSORT 2010 multi-arm, SPIRIT 2013); planned two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, ITT
Best_Metric: Not reported - protocol only; no data reported
Dataset: Planned at UNIOSUN Teaching Hospital, Osogbo, Nigeria; PACTR202208571972367
Sample_N_Approx: 87 planned (29 per group, 80% power, effect size 0.80)
Key_Novelty: First RCT protocol for telerehab +/- tDCS in post-stroke MCI in sub-Saharan Africa (n=87)
Primary_Limitation: Protocol only, no results; feasibility in Nigerian older adult population unproven; double-blind claim questionable for active tDCS vs no-tDCS and in-person vs video; digital divide (device/internet) unaddressed; 29/group modest for 3-arm multiple outcomes.
Open_Problems: Trial completion will answer whether tDCS adds value to telerehab and whether telerehab is non-inferior to conventional physiotherapy; sham-tDCS design for placebo control; process evaluation embedded.

Modality: Auditory duration discrimination psychophysics (sub-second 640-1950ms vs supra-second 2440-7440ms); PSE, DL, RT; CERAD word list
Method_Architecture: Linear mixed-effects models (R lme4/lmerTest); psychometric function fitting (quickpsy); Pearson correlations
Best_Metric: Not reported - no classification metric; PSE bias interaction p=0.010; r=-0.52 memory vs sub-second PSE
Dataset: Proprietary DZNE Magdeburg sample; data on OSF (osf.io/fseh4)
Key_Novelty: Sub-second PSE bias in aMCI correlates with memory (r=-0.52) - first sub/supra-second test
Primary_Limitation: Small aMCI sample (n=10) limits precision and generalisability; cross-sectional design precludes predictive inference; PSE-memory correlation (r=-0.52) leaves ~73% variance unexplained and the memory-decay interpretation is one of several compatible explanations; no neuroimaging to test mechanism.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal follow-up to test whether sub-second timing predicts aMCI-to-AD conversion; neuroimaging correlates (MTL volumetry, cerebellar/basal ganglia circuits); replication in non-amnestic MCI and AD; clinical diagnostic utility vs standard tests.

Modality: Clinical cohort (SPRINT); adjudicated AKI (modified KDIGO) as time-varying predictor; adjudicated MCI/probable dementia/composite outcomes
Method_Architecture: Counting-process Cox proportional hazard models; Fine-Gray competing-risk sensitivity analysis
Best_Metric: HR 1.72 (95% CI 1.07-2.75) probable dementia; 1.43 (1.01-2.04) composite; MCI alone n.s. in fully adjusted model
Dataset: SPRINT / SPRINT MIND trial cohort (US, high cardiovascular risk, no diabetes/stroke)
Key_Novelty: Adjudicated mild/reversible AKI independently linked to probable dementia (HR 1.72) and MCI/dementia composite in SPRINT - first adjudicated-endpoint AKI cohort
Primary_Limitation: Pre-baseline AKI history not captured; retrospective/associative secondary analysis; AKI event group small (n=270) with modest event counts and wide CIs; MCI-alone association not significant; SPRINT excluded diabetes and stroke; no imaging/biomarker mechanism data.
Open_Problems: Whether AKI is causal vs a frailty/vascular marker; which AKI characteristics matter (severity, recurrence, recovery); mediation pathways (vascular/inflammatory/uremic); pooled multi-trial adjudicated analyses for precision.

Modality: Systematic review and meta-analysis of cognitive screening instruments (MoCA, MMSE, M-ACE, 3MS etc.) in CKD/kidney failure vs neuropsychological battery gold standard
Method_Architecture: Bivariate random-effects DTA meta-analysis (pooled sensitivity/specificity, DOR, HSROC); QUADAS-2
Best_Metric: MoCA cutoff 24: pooled sensitivity 0.94 (0.81-0.98), specificity 0.63 (0.35-0.85); MMSE sens 0.48 / spec 0.95
Dataset: 10 studies (Brazil, China, France, Germany, South Korea, UK, USA; 2012-2020) in CKD/kidney failure (dialysis/transplant)
Key_Novelty: First DTA meta-analysis of MCI/dementia screening in CKD/kidney failure - recommends MoCA cutoff 24
Primary_Limitation: Small number of studies (10) with high heterogeneity; no kidney transplantation or haemodiafiltration populations; selective reporting of optimal cutoffs may inflate performance; gold standards varied; publication bias not formally assessed.
Open_Problems: Performance in transplant and haemodiafiltration populations; pre-specified (non-optimal) cutoffs; head-to-head instrument comparisons; external validation of MoCA-24 in prospective CKD cohorts.

Modality: Resting-state EEG coherence (16-channel 10-20, 200Hz); whole-brain (120 pairs) and 8-class regional coherence across theta/alpha/beta/gamma; MMSE/HDS-R/FAB
Method_Architecture: Wavelet time-frequency decomposition (EEGLAB/MATLAB); Spearman correlations
Best_Metric: Alpha-range whole-brain coherence vs MMSE r=0.761; FPL r=0.719 vs FPR r=0.529; UPDRS total r=-0.577
Dataset: Proprietary Nara Medical University cohort (Japan); 20 PD-MCI + 10 MCI without Parkinsonism
Key_Novelty: First report linking alpha EEG coherence to cognition in PD-MCI with left>right frontoparietal dissociation - decreased brain efficiency/synchronization
Primary_Limitation: Very small sample (20 PD-MCI) without healthy controls; cross-sectional and correlational; no multiple-comparison correction; on-medication recordings; left/right 'compensatory' interpretation speculative; single-centre Japanese cohort.
Open_Problems: Whether alpha-coherence decrease is PD-MCI-specific vs other MCI etiologies; whether it predicts PD-dementia conversion; source-space/graph connectivity corroboration; longitudinal EEG with conversion endpoints.

Modality: Population survey (CHARLS 2018); TICS-10-based MCI (AACD, >1 SD below 5-year age-group mean); nocturnal sleep duration, nap duration, sleep quality
Method_Architecture: Restricted cubic spline (3 knots) dose-response models; stratified logistic regression with interaction tests
Best_Metric: OR 1.88 long sleep + poor sleep quality vs 1.33 good quality; OR 0.72 short sleepers with 30-60 min naps; lowest MCI odds at 6-8h sleep + 30-60 min naps
Dataset: CHARLS (China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study) wave 4/2018
Key_Novelty: First CHARLS dose-response study of joint sleep-quality x duration x napping interactions on MCI - 6-8h sleep + 30-60 min naps associated with lowest MCI odds
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference (reverse causality possible); self-reported sleep (no actigraphy/PSG); TICS-10 screening-based MCI definition rather than clinical diagnosis; long-sleep/very-long-nap cells small; residual confounding (depression, medications, APOE).
Open_Problems: Longitudinal designs with objective sleep measures; clinically adjudicated MCI; mediation via amyloid clearance/inflammation/vascular pathways; whether tailored sleep interventions reduce MCI incidence.

Modality: Clinical cohort (VMCI-Tuscany); MCI+SVD (moderate-severe WMH); MoCA demographically adjusted, Delta-MoCA; transition to major NCD (DSM-5)
Method_Architecture: Multivariate logistic regression (basal MoCA + age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, stroke history, WMH, lacunar infarcts); t-tests/chi-square
Best_Metric: OR 1.09 (95% CI 1.00-1.19, p=0.049) per MoCA point for MCI-to-major-NCD transition; Delta-MoCA -2.6 converters vs -0.7 stable
Dataset: VMCI-Tuscany Study (multicenter, Tuscany Italy; Florence/Pisa/Siena)
Key_Novelty: First MoCA longitudinal-change data in MCI+SVD - 32% converted to major NCD over 24 months; MoCA decline -2.6 points separates converters from stable (-0.7)
Primary_Limitation: Moderate sample (138) with borderline-significant effects (p=0.051 baseline difference; p=0.049 OR); 2-year follow-up short for conversion dynamics; practice/attrition effects not quantified; single-country Italian cohort; no individual-level classification utility established.
Open_Problems: Reliable-change-index analyses for clinically meaningful MoCA decline; mixed-effects trajectory models; larger multicentre VCI cohorts with longer follow-up; whether MoCA change monitoring improves clinical detection of progression.

Modality: Population surveys (CHARLS wave 4->5 development; HRS wave 14->15 external validation); TICS-based MCI (AACD); 16 sociodemographic/health/psychological predictors
Method_Architecture: LASSO feature selection; five ML models (LR, NN, XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest); SMOTE; random forest imputation; SHAP
Best_Metric: AUROC 0.722-0.782 (LightGBM best across discrimination, calibration, clinical utility); Brier/DCA reported
Dataset: CHARLS (China, n=2,142 COPD) development; HRS (US) external validation
Key_Novelty: First externally validated LightGBM MCI-risk model for COPD across CHARLS+HRS (AUROC 0.78) with SHAP feature profile (sex, residence, IADL, education, social activity, marital status, Internet use, depression)
Primary_Limitation: MCI defined by screening criterion (AACD, TICS), not clinical adjudication; self-reported COPD without spirometry; moderate AUROC (0.72-0.78) limits individual-level accuracy; external validation shares self-report/screening methodology; survey variables only; SMOTE may distort calibration.
Open_Problems: Whether survey-based model generalises to clinically diagnosed MCI; incremental value of spirometry/biomarkers/oxygenation predictors; prospective validation; calibration-focused evaluation; COPD-severity subgroup analyses.

Modality: Multicenter cross-sectional (Chinese Veteran Clinical Research platform, 277 communities/18 cities); satellite-based PM2.5/PM10 exposure; MCI/dementia via neuropsychological testing + clinical diagnosis
Method_Architecture: Logistic regression (crude + fully adjusted); stratified effect-modification analysis with interaction p-values
Dataset: Chinese Veteran Clinical Research (CVCR) platform (277 communities, 18 Chinese cities; 2009-2011)
Key_Novelty: First high-exposure Chinese PM2.5-dementia/MCI multicenter study (veterans, 18 cities) - OR 1.52 per 10 ug/m3 PM2.5 for MCI, strongest with low education
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; male-veteran-only sample limits generalisability (women excluded); satellite-modelled exposure (not personal monitoring) risks non-differential misclassification; 3-year exposure window may miss relevant longer-term exposure; no biomarker confirmation of outcomes.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal designs with incident dementia/MCI; personal/higher-resolution exposure monitoring; longer exposure windows and cumulative metrics; inclusion of women and general-population samples; mediation via inflammation/amyloid pathways.

Modality: Primary care RCT (Hong Kong, Lek Yuen Health Centre); HK-MoCA 19-25 MCI; three arms: CPR (cognitive training + Tai Chi + nurse-led RFM) vs RFM alone vs health advice
Method_Architecture: Three-arm open-label blinded-endpoint RCT; computer-generated 1:1:1 randomisation; linear mixed model with Bonferroni correction; modified ITT
Best_Metric: ADAS-Cog Z score at 15 months: CPR vs health advice beta=-0.04 (-0.34 to 0.26); RFM vs health advice beta=-0.14 (-0.44 to 0.15); no significant between-group differences
Dataset: Proprietary trial dataset (456 MCI older adults, Hong Kong primary care; ChiCTR1900026857)
Key_Novelty: Largest Asian RCT of nurse-led RFM + multi-component CPR for primary care MCI - null ADAS-Cog result at 15 months, cautioning against unproven interventions
Primary_Limitation: Open-label design (participants unblinded despite blinded endpoints); 3-month active intervention phase may be insufficient; ADAS-Cog may be insensitive in high-functioning primary care MCI; modified-ITT excludes 33 without follow-up; screening-based MCI definition (HK-MoCA 19-25).
Open_Problems: Higher-intensity/longer-duration interventions; sham/attention-matched control; 2-3 year follow-up with incident dementia outcomes; subgroup analyses by risk profile (hypertension, depression); process evaluations of fidelity.

Modality: Resting-state fMRI (ICA-based DMN identification); pure-tone audiometry (normal n=60 / HL n=34) and speech-reception thresholds; MCI older adults
Method_Architecture: ICA (DMN component); ANOVA with covariate control (normal vs HL); linear regression (speech-reception threshold x DMN connectivity)
Best_Metric: Decreased DMN-caudate and DMN-thalamus connectivity in MCI with pure-tone HL vs normal hearing; no DMN difference by speech-reception threshold
Dataset: Proprietary Montreal cohort (Concordia University / CCNA), Canada
Key_Novelty: First MCI-cohort link of pure-tone HL to reduced DMN-caudate/thalamus connectivity - candidate neural pathway for HL-dementia risk
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional with modest sample (94; 34 HL) precluding causal inference; no audiometric severity gradation; speech-reception null may reflect variance/power; multiple regional comparisons without explicit correction; hearing-aid use and MCI aetiology not examined as moderators.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal fMRI+audiometry designs testing whether HL-related DMN disconnection mediates dementia conversion; graded audiometry and hearing-aid use; source-space/graph connectivity; hearing-intervention trials with connectivity endpoints.

Modality: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (Toyama, Japan); MCI/mild AD (DSM-5); diosgenin-rich yam extract 18 mg/day vs placebo for 24 weeks; MMSE-J, ADAS-Cog, VFT; plasma NfL, GFAP, Ab42/40
Method_Architecture: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial; Simoa plasma biomarker assays; group comparisons and biomarker-cognition correlations
Best_Metric: Yam extract improved ADAS-Cog Praxis and reduced plasma NfL (12-24 weeks); MCI subgroup improved ADAS-Cog total/Memory and NfL; MMSE-J improvement related to Ab42/40 increase
Dataset: Proprietary trial dataset (Toyama University Hospital, Japan; jRCTs041200036)
Key_Novelty: First RCT of diosgenin-rich yam extract in MCI/mild AD - modest cognitive gain with plasma NfL reduction suggesting axonal protection
Primary_Limitation: Small sample (43 randomised) limiting precision; combined MCI+mild AD primary analysis complicates subgroup interpretation; modest effects; MMSE-J primary endpoint did not show simple between-group difference; axonal-repair mechanism inferred from NfL rather than demonstrated; single-centre with 24-week follow-up.
Open_Problems: Larger multicentre RCTs with MCI-only pre-specified primary endpoint; longer follow-up with serial cognition; direct neuroimaging outcomes (tractography, functional connectivity) to test axonal repair; additive effects with cholinesterase inhibitors; conversion endpoints.

Modality: Population survey (2016-17 Chilean National Health Survey); MCI via MMSE + Pfeffer Functional Activities Questionnaire (dementia excluded); PA via GPAQ
Method_Architecture: Survey-weighted logistic regression; overall + sex-stratified models
Dataset: 2016-17 Chilean National Health Survey (ENS), adults 60+
Key_Novelty: First Chilean population-level PA-MCI association using national survey + GPAQ; stronger effect in men (OR 2.44 vs n.s. women)
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional - direction unclear; screen-based MCI (MMSE/Pfeffer) without clinical adjudication; self-reported PA; female stratum non-significant; residual confounding.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal PA-MCI cohorts with objective PA (accelerometry); sex-stratified dose-response; pooled Latin American analyses; causal methods.

Modality: Structural MRI (T1-w) hippocampal subfield volumetry (FreeSurfer); ACE-III cognition
Method_Architecture: FreeSurfer automated segmentation; GLM group comparisons + partial correlations (age, sex, TIV covariates)
Best_Metric: Left presubiculum-memory r=0.460 (p=0.024); bilateral subfield reductions (tail, subiculum, CA1, CA3, molecular layer) in MCI
Dataset: CBR-TLSA (Tata Longitudinal Study of Ageing), Bangalore, India
Key_Novelty: First Indian-cohort hippocampal subfield-memory correlation; left subicular/dentate (presubiculum, parasubiculum, GC-ML-DG) pattern in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small sample (27 MCI); cross-sectional; no AD-biomarker confirmation; multiple subfield comparisons; FreeSurfer segmentation accuracy limits.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal subfield volumetry for conversion; biomarker (CSF/PET) stratification; multiple-comparison correction; multi-pipeline validation.

Modality: Systematic review: advanced activities of daily living (AADL) assessment vs cognitive assessment as MCI predictor in 60+
Method_Architecture: Systematic review across PubMed/Embase/Scopus/CINAHL/Web of Science/Cochrane; narrative synthesis
Best_Metric: 6 studies: AADL instruments optimal correlation with cognition + good HC-vs-MCI discrimination (p<0.01); no pooled metric
Dataset: 11 studies (8 cross-sectional, 3 longitudinal) from 6 databases
Key_Novelty: First synthesis comparing AADL vs cognitive assessment as MCI predictor in adults 60+; functional instruments complement but do not replace cognitive tests
Primary_Limitation: Narrative synthesis without meta-analysis; only 11 studies; named instruments (De Vriendt AADL, BIA, IADL-X) not usable as independent diagnostics; heterogeneity of instruments/criteria.
Open_Problems: Meta-analytic pooling of harmonised AADL psychometrics; more longitudinal predictive-validity studies; head-to-head vs cognitive-only against biomarker-confirmed MCI.

Modality: Clinical cohort (T2DM patients, Kano Nigeria); MoCA cognition; fasting plasma insulin (ELISA)
Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional case-control; correlations + logistic regression (MCI predictors)
Best_Metric: MCI prevalence 88.5% (diabetics) vs 50% (controls); plasma insulin 16.24±13.5 vs 7.59±2.9 uIU/ml
Dataset: Murtala Mohammed Specialist Hospital diabetic clinics, Kano, Nigeria
Key_Novelty: First characterisation of MCI prevalence + hyperinsulinaemia in African advanced T2DM; multi-domain MoCA deficits (executive, naming, attention, abstraction, delayed recall)
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional; small single-centre sample; 50% control MCI rate suggests MoCA cut-off/education validity issues; fasting insulin only (no HOMA-IR).
Open_Problems: Longitudinal hyperinsulinaemia-MCI studies with HOMA-IR; normed MoCA for SSA populations; multi-site replication; mechanistic biomarkers.

Modality: Cognitive training intervention (6 wk, 96 h) with 1-year follow-up; MoCA; APOE genotyping (rs429358/rs7412); serum biomarkers (Luminex)
Method_Architecture: Pre/post observational; Friedman test; ANOVA + Tukey by genotype
Best_Metric: MoCA improved post-training (chi2=9.26, p=0.002); e4/e4 pre-training lower MoCA and VEGF (F=8.12, p=0.006)/FGF-2 (F=7.32, p=0.008); genotype biomarker differences eliminated after training
Dataset: N.A. Alekseev Psychiatric Clinic No. 1 Memory Clinic, Moscow (conference abstract)
Key_Novelty: APOE genotype modulates cognitive-training outcome and VEGF/FGF-2 biomarker response in MCI; e4/e4 growth-factor gap eliminated by training
Primary_Limitation: Conference abstract (no full methods/data); no control group; rs7412 grouping conflates alleles; single site; long uncharacterised follow-up; multiple testing.
Open_Problems: Randomised sham-controlled genotype-stratified trials; full haplotype analysis; multi-timepoint biomarkers; replication in larger cohorts.

Modality: Systematic review: fMRI effective connectivity (directional) in AD/MCI
Method_Architecture: Systematic review (PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar); narrative synthesis of EC methods (MVAR, generative models)
Best_Metric: Hub-centre disconnection + altered inter-network interactions across 39 studies; no pooled metric
Dataset: 39 fMRI EC studies in AD/MCI (PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar)
Key_Novelty: Consolidates directional (effective) connectivity hub-disconnection pattern in AD/MCI; maps MVAR/generative-model methodological landscape
Primary_Limitation: Narrative-only synthesis without meta-analysis; three databases only; heterogeneous EC methods, tasks, criteria; no risk-of-bias assessment.
Open_Problems: Registered PRISMA protocol with broader database coverage; meta-analysis of aligned EC metrics; method-standardisation; separate MCI vs AD syntheses.

Modality: ICT-based tele-neuropsychological assessment; MoCA + Clock Drawing Test + autonomy measures
Method_Architecture: Correlational analysis (no ML)
Best_Metric: Moderate autonomy-cognition correlation (MoCA, CDT); significant in some variables; no AUC
Dataset: Mexican adults 60+ from geriatric day centres (CETYS Universidad)
Key_Novelty: First ICT tele-neuropsychological autonomy-cognition assessment in Mexican older adults; CDT may detect MCI indicators missed by MoCA
Primary_Limitation: Small convenience sample; no clinical MCI gold standard; tele modality unvalidated vs in-person; correlation-only; no multiple-comparison correction.
Open_Problems: Tele-vs-in-person validation against clinical MCI reference; ROC-based sensitivity/specificity; longitudinal follow-up; digital-literacy controls.

Modality: Qualitative lived-experience study; 34 in-depth interviews (3 Spanish hospitals, 2023); COREQ
Method_Architecture: Thematic analysis (qualitative)
Best_Metric: Five themes: diagnosis impact, daily challenges, care guidelines/support, social-emotional support, fear/uncertainty; no numeric metric
Dataset: Three Spanish hospitals (2023); MCI diagnosed during COVID-19 pandemic
Key_Novelty: First qualitative capture of MCI-diagnosis experience during the COVID-19 pandemic; complements caregiver-perspective literature
Primary_Limitation: Single-country three-hospital sample; retrospective self-report; no longitudinal outcomes; researcher-dependent thematic analysis; pandemic context limits generalisability.
Open_Problems: Multi-country replication; longitudinal designs linking experience to coping/progression; triangulation with caregiver/clinician perspectives.
Journal: Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics Plus 1:100010 (2024)

Method_Architecture: Linear and logistic regression (no ML classifier)
Best_Metric: Adjusted OR for MCI per unit TSH (males 0.80, 95% CI 0.70-0.92)
Dataset: ADNI multiethnic cohort (MCI + HC, TSH < 10, GDS < 5)
Key_Novelty: Sex-specific (male-driven) TSH-cognition association in large multiethnic ADNI sample
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional; normal-range TSH only; no longitudinal outcomes
Open_Problems: Longitudinal TSH-cognition studies; sex-aware screening thresholds; interaction with APOE and thyroid medication
Journal: Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics Plus 2:100195 (2025)

Method_Architecture: Multivariable logistic regression (no ML classifier)
Best_Metric: Adjusted OR (ADNPH vs ADMCI; e.g., males tobacco OR 1.818)
Dataset: Prisma Health-Upstate EHR (Feb 2016-Aug 2021): ADMCI n=33,064; ADNPH n=671
Key_Novelty: First large EHR contrast of NPH-associated AD vs MCI with sex-stratified sociodemographic/psychotropic profiles
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective EHR; confounding by indication; small NPH subgroup (n=671)
Open_Problems: Causal inference on psychotropics; imaging-adjudicated NPH; multi-site replication; prospective outcomes
Journal: Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics Plus 2:100202 (2025)

Method_Architecture: Systematic review (narrative synthesis; no ML)
Best_Metric: Qualitative: CAP deficit in 23/29 studies; no pooled metric
Dataset: 29 articles (2014-2024) from PubMed/Medline, Cochrane, Scopus, Google Scholar
Key_Novelty: Audit showing CAP tests are absent from leading MCI diagnostic guidelines despite consistent deficit evidence
Primary_Limitation: No meta-analysis; heterogeneous CAP tests and MCI criteria
Open_Problems: Meta-analysis of standardised CAP tests (GDT, DDT, SIN, Digits Backward); normative thresholds; guideline integration
Journal: Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics Plus 2:100231 (2025)

Method_Architecture: Cluster randomised trial protocol (no ML)
Best_Metric: not reported (trial in progress)
Dataset: Community-dwelling adults 60-75 with MCI, 20 wards, Tiruvalla taluk, Kerala, India
Key_Novelty: First culturally adapted multi-domain cluster-RCT protocol for MCI in a Kerala (low/middle-income) community setting
Primary_Limitation: Protocol stage; 20-cluster design may underpower cluster-level effects
Open_Problems: Effectiveness in LMIC setting; adherence over 2 years; scalability; biomarker endpoints
Journal: Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics Plus 3:100239 (2026)

Modality: Psychiatric risk factors (depression and related) in MCI-to-AD progression
Method_Architecture: Systematic review (narrative synthesis; no ML)
Best_Metric: Qualitative: 17 papers; depression supported as risk factor cross-species; no pooled metric
Dataset: 17 longitudinal human studies (MCI-to-AD) + targeted rodent literature
Key_Novelty: Cross-species (human + rodent) synthesis identifying depression as the key psychiatric MCI-to-AD risk factor
Primary_Limitation: Sparse non-depression psychiatric evidence; no meta-analysis
Open_Problems: Causal role of depression vs shared prodrome; SSRI prevention trials; transdiagnostic sleep/stress factors
Journal: Am J Geriatr Psychiatry: Open Science, Education, and Practice 8:17-32 (2025)

Modality: Multimodal diagnostic adjudication (serial neuropsychology expert panel + chart review + in-person neuro exam)
Method_Architecture: Multimodal consensus adjudication (no ML classifier)
Best_Metric: Incident diagnosis counts: 63 MCI (11.3%), 4 dementia (0.7%)
Dataset: SAGES cohort: 560 community-dwelling adults aged 70+, serial neuropsych up to 72 months post-surgery
Key_Novelty: Quantified multimodal adjudication (panel + chart + nested exam) for incident MCI/dementia in a large cohort without biomarker access
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective diagnosis; only 4 dementia events
Open_Problems: Validation vs biomarker gold standard; external replication; inter-rater reliability; prospective confirmation
Journal: Am J Geriatr Psychiatry: Open Science, Education, and Practice 9:8-18 (2026)

Modality: Non-pharmacological interventions: social, cognitive, and physical stimulation (behavioural/lifestyle)
Method_Architecture: Narrative review (no ML)
Best_Metric: Qualitative: consistent cognitive/functional benefits across modalities; no pooled metric
Dataset: Narrative synthesis of RCTs, meta-analyses, longitudinal studies (PubMed, Scopus, 2013-2024)
Key_Novelty: Integrated cross-domain synthesis linking social/cognitive/physical stimulation to EE-BDNF mechanisms, with multimodal synergy as central thesis
Primary_Limitation: Narrative selection; heterogeneous interventions; short follow-ups
Open_Problems: Optimal dose/duration/component combination; personalisation; large biomarker-anchored RCTs; dementia-conversion effects

Modality: Diabetes management in MCI: glycemic targets (HbA1c) and glucose-lowering medication outcomes (clinical/epidemiological)
Method_Architecture: Scoping review (narrative synthesis; no ML)
Best_Metric: Qualitative: 32 studies; no pooled metric
Dataset: 32 studies (guidelines, RCTs, observational) from PubMed, Embase, Cochrane (2000-2024)
Key_Novelty: First scoping synthesis integrating glycemic-target guidance with medication-class evidence specifically after MCI onset
Primary_Limitation: No meta-analysis; evidence for intensified control observational in small cohorts
Open_Problems: Mechanism of medication protection (glycemic vs neurotrophic); optimal HbA1c range in MCI; large RCTs with MCI-no-diabetes controls

Modality: Electrophysiology (gamma oscillations, EEG/MEG) + neurochemistry (GABA MRS) + neuromodulation (tACS/TMS/sensory)
Method_Architecture: Narrative review (no ML)
Best_Metric: Qualitative: 127 studies; modest cognitive benefits of 40 Hz interventions; no pooled metric
Dataset: 127 studies (2005-2025) from PubMed: animal models + human MRS/EEG/MEG/postmortem + intervention trials
Key_Novelty: Integrated GABA-gamma bidirectional cascade synthesis with full intervention landscape (GABA pharmacology, cell therapy, 40 Hz modalities) and MRS-GABA biomarker framing
Primary_Limitation: Narrative synthesis; small heterogeneous human trials; inconsistent biomarker outcomes
Open_Problems: Large sham-controlled phase III trials; harmonised oscillatory metrics; ApoE and stage stratification; home-based delivery

Modality: Clinical intervention: Kampo medicine (RO-8) with cognitive (HDS-R) and renal (eGFR) outcomes
Method_Architecture: Retrospective cohort with before/after statistics (no ML)
Best_Metric: 90.9% (70/77) cognitive improvement rate; HDS-R 19.90 to 25.05 (p<0.0001)
Dataset: Single Japanese clinic (2008-2023): AD (n=32) and MCI (n=51) RO-8 group vs control (n=17)
Key_Novelty: First documentation that RO-8 Kampo combination restores cognition in 90.9% of AD/MCI patients while preserving eGFR in CKD
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective single-centre non-randomised design; small control; speculative M1-to-M2 mechanism
Open_Problems: Prospective RCT confirmation; component-wise analysis; M1/M2 macrophage and cytokine mechanism; liver-function monitoring

Modality: Digital/Behavioural: bilingual (English/Cantonese) mobile MMSE self-evaluation app (eMMSE) with senior-friendly UI and record tracking
Method_Architecture: Mobile application design with usability evaluation (no ML)
Best_Metric: Not reported (no diagnostic accuracy metrics; qualitative usability findings)
Dataset: Hong Kong user sample (survey + 8-user focus group); no clinical cohort
Key_Novelty: First MMSE-based bilingual (English/Cantonese) mobile self-evaluation app for MCI with senior-friendly UI and longitudinal record tracking
Primary_Limitation: No diagnostic validation; performance confounded by education and computer literacy; small qualitative evaluation
Open_Problems: Diagnostic accuracy of self-administered digital MMSE; education/literacy bias mitigation; screen-size-robust pentagon drawing; comparison with MoCA/SLUMS
Journal: Chapter 9 in 'Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytics for Smart Healthcare', Elsevier (2021)

Modality: Clinical/Population: epidemiological review of AD prevalence, incidence, mortality and progression (2014-2021, NA/Europe/Asia)
Method_Architecture: Narrative literature review (no ML)
Best_Metric: Not applicable (review); 40-75% AD aetiology among MCI; lifetime risk 41.9% women / 33.6% men
Dataset: PubMed-indexed epidemiological literature 2014-2021 (North America, Europe, Asia)
Key_Novelty: Consolidates 2014-2021 AD epidemiology and quantifies MCI-to-AD aetiology (40-75%) and lifetime risks stratified by Abeta/neurodegeneration status
Primary_Limitation: Narrative non-systematic review; heterogeneous source populations; no pooled estimates; regional scope limited
Open_Problems: Preclinical-AD-to-MCI progression estimates; standardised AD-aetiology estimates among MCI; biomarker harmonisation; LMIC data

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological + functional (BADL/IADL/QoL/frailty) assessment in older cardiac-surgery candidates
Method_Architecture: Prospective cohort with relative-risk analysis (no ML)
Best_Metric: RR 3.5 for cognitive decline in MCI vs non-MCI at follow-up; IADL worsening in women with MCI (significant)
Dataset: Single-centre cohort of 48 older cardiac-surgery candidates (Spain)
Key_Novelty: First prospective demonstration in cardiac-surgery candidates that baseline MCI predicts post-operative cognitive decline (RR 3.5) and domain-specific functional/QoL loss without increasing resource use
Primary_Limitation: Small single-centre cohort without biomarker-confirmed MCI aetiology
Open_Problems: Prehabilitation/perioperative interventions on MCI trajectory; role of delirium; long-term cognitive outcomes; multicentre replication

Modality: Behavioural/Digital: immersive virtual reality (IVR) cognitive intervention - Chinese Virtual Supermarket (CVSM)
Method_Architecture: IVR serious-game intervention with pre/post neuropsychological assessment (no ML)
Best_Metric: Significant improvement in all cognitive measures (P<.001); perceived stress P=.048 (MD) / P=.03 (MCI)
Dataset: Single-centre Chinese cohort (Fujian): 18 MCI + 13 mild dementia (Aug 2020 - Jan 2021)
Key_Novelty: First pilot evaluation of a fully immersive virtual-supermarket (CVSM) IVR intervention in both MCI and mild dementia showing cognitive gains and perceived-stress reduction
Primary_Limitation: Uncontrolled pretest-posttest pilot; small sample; no follow-up; practice effects uncontrolled
Open_Problems: Long-term durability of IVR cognitive gains; optimal dose/frequency; differential response MCI vs dementia; RCT confirmation

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological assessment methodology (reliable change statistics, SEest vs SEpred)
Method_Architecture: Statistical methodology (regression-based reliable change; no ML)
Best_Metric: Correlation of SRB z-scores between SE metrics r=1.0 (p<.001); SE values 3.697 vs 3.719 (HVLT-R)
Dataset: Developmental sample n=167 (normal/MCI, 1-week retest) + independent MCI validation sample n=143 (University of Utah)
Key_Novelty: Empirically demonstrates SEest and SEpred yield near-identical values and equivalent SRB reliable-change z-scores in a clinical sample
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre, 1-week retest horizon only; equivalence untested across longer intervals and all measures
Open_Problems: SE equivalence across longer retest intervals and diverse batteries; optimal SE for extreme baseline scores; multi-site replication

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological assessment methodology (1-week reliable change, SRB validation)
Method_Architecture: Statistical methodology (SRB reliable change; no ML)
Best_Metric: Significant 1-week improvements (pairwise t-tests); observed follow-up below SRB prediction
Dataset: Independent community-dwelling amnestic MCI sample, 1-week retest (University of Utah)
Sample_N_Approx: Community-dwelling amnestic MCI sample (n in full text; same programme as P-922/P-924)
Key_Novelty: Externally validates Duff's 1-week SRB equations in amnestic MCI and shows incrementally smaller practice benefit with increasing MCI severity/domain burden
Primary_Limitation: Short (1-week) retest horizon; single-centre amnestic MCI sample
Open_Problems: SRB performance over longer intervals in MCI; prognostic value of small practice effects for conversion; non-amnestic MCI

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological assessment (RBANS) one-year reliable-change validation
Method_Architecture: Statistical methodology (SRB reliable change; no ML)
Best_Metric: z-scores significantly below zero for all 5 RBANS Indexes + Total Scale in clinic sample (ds |0.79-2.76|); 47% decline on Immediate/Delayed Memory
Dataset: Two independent amnestic MCI samples: community n=64 and clinic n=58 (University of Utah); reference development sample n=129
Key_Novelty: First external validation of Hammers et al.'s (2020) RBANS SRB equations in amnestic MCI and first community-vs-clinic comparison of one-year reliable change
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre, predominantly White, amnestic-only samples; SRB extremes susceptible to regression to the mean
Open_Problems: SRB performance over longer horizons; relation of SRB-defined decline to AD biomarkers/conversion; more diverse samples

Modality: Clinical/Population: functional (iADL) + neuropsychological longitudinal assessment with growth-curve modelling
Method_Architecture: Mixed-model growth curves + logistic regression with ROC (classical statistics; A1-type regression)
Best_Metric: AUC 0.94 (95% CI lower bound 0.87) for dementia conversion the year before diagnosis
Dataset: Memory-clinic cohort (Montreal): 121 MCI (47 progressors, 16 decliners, 58 stable), up to 5-year follow-up
Key_Novelty: First characterization of quadratic complex-iADL decline trajectories in MCI progressors and a simple cognitive+iADL model achieving AUC 0.94 for one-year conversion prediction
Primary_Limitation: Self-reported iADL with anosognosia risk; no biomarkers; no external validation; decliners group small
Open_Problems: Performance-based iADL measures; biomarker validation; independent-cohort replication; finer-grained detection of early decline

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological assessment (NTBV) with reliable change index methodology
Method_Architecture: Statistical methodology (reliable change index; no ML)
Best_Metric: Deterioration rates by group: AD converters up to 54.2% (TMT B); MCI up to 29.1%
Dataset: Vienna Conversion to Dementia study: 358 memory-clinic patients (HC 46, SCD 42, MCI 270, AD 48), 2008-2018
Key_Novelty: Stage-dependent individual deterioration rates (SCD<MCI<AD) quantified with RCI in a single memory-clinic cohort, including MCI-to-HC reversion and practice-effect-driven improvements
Primary_Limitation: Missing short-NTBV data for low-MMSE patients; mood/training confounds unmeasured
Open_Problems: Separating true improvement from practice effects; RCI sensitivity at SCD stage; mood covariates; biomarker-stratified groups

Modality: Clinical/Population: UK consensus guideline (diagnosis, neuroimaging, CSF/blood biomarkers, cognitive testing, follow-up)
Method_Architecture: Multi-stakeholder consensus guideline (no ML)
Best_Metric: Not applicable (guideline); cites 5-15% annual MCI-to-dementia progression; ~50% stable at 5 years; ADNI 16%
Dataset: UK consensus (Nov 2019, Manchester): synthesises COSMIC, AAN, IDEAS, NICE, CSF meta-analyses and blood-biomarker evidence
Key_Novelty: First UK national consensus roadmap for MCI diagnosis and management addressing the NICE guidance gap with actionable standards for biomarkers, imaging, follow-up, and research participation
Primary_Limitation: Consensus-based without systematic review; UK/NHS-specific; infrastructure and cost barriers unresolved
Open_Problems: NICE guideline development; health-economic modelling of biomarker pathways; age-specific biomarker norms; international harmonisation

Modality: Behavioural/Digital: on-road driving performance with cognitive + non-cognitive risk-factor predictors
Method_Architecture: Classical statistical prediction models (multiple linear + logistic hierarchical regression; A1-type)
Best_Metric: Accuracy 88.3% for prospective minor at-fault accident occurrence; 81.2% for fitness to drive; driving skills R2adj=0.30
Dataset: German community cohort of older drivers with and without MCI (EvKB Bielefeld); standardized on-road route + 12-month telephone follow-up
Key_Novelty: Shows non-cognitive risk factors (cervical spine mobility, avoidance behaviour, mileage) significantly improve driving-outcome prediction beyond cognitive tests in older and MCI drivers
Primary_Limitation: Small MCI subgroup (n=12); self-reported accident outcomes; no external validation; cross-sectional for driving skills
Open_Problems: Larger MCI samples; objective accident records; longer follow-up; external validation; additional non-cognitive domains

Modality: Clinical/Population: cognitive outcomes (MMSE/CDR) + amyloid PET in ChEI-treated MCI over 1 year
Method_Architecture: Classical statistical regression (linear + logistic with propensity matching; A1-type)
Best_Metric: OR 0.606 (95% CI 0.381-0.873) for baseline MMSE predicting CDR-1 progression; ChEI use OR 1.120 (p=0.892)
Dataset: Memory clinic cohort, Seoul National University Bundang Hospital: 111 MCI (CDR 0.5, 73 ChEI users / 38 non-users), 1-year follow-up, amyloid PET
Key_Novelty: First study examining ChEI effect on 1-year cognitive change in MCI stratified by amyloid PET status, showing no ChEI benefit regardless of amyloid burden
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective design with confounding by indication; small matched subsample (25+25); single centre; short 1-year horizon
Open_Problems: Prospective randomized designs; longer follow-up; standardized PET timing; CSF/MRI biomarkers; dose and adherence

Modality: Clinical/Population: integrative review of sleep-MCI association and sleep interventions
Method_Architecture: Integrative/narrative review (no computational model)
Best_Metric: RR ~1.39 for sleep disturbance -> MCI risk (lowest sleep-efficiency quartile ~1.53); interventions improved sleep
Dataset: 24 studies from 4 databases (sleep-MCI association, sleep quality, brain anatomy, interventions)
Key_Novelty: Integrative synthesis linking sleep disturbance to MCI risk and demonstrating effectiveness of sleep interventions (physical activity, CBT-based SWTW, acoustic stimulation) in MCI/AD
Primary_Limitation: Heterogeneous studies without meta-analytic pooling; narrative synthesis only; potential publication bias
Open_Problems: Meta-analysis of interventions; harmonised sleep measures; longitudinal studies with cognitive endpoints; objective sleep measures

Modality: Clinical/Population: visuo-constructive neuropsychological testing (VVT 3.0) across HC/SCD/MCI/AD
Method_Architecture: ROC analysis + multinomial logistic regression (classical statistics; A1-type)
Best_Metric: AUC 0.783 (95% CI 0.747-0.819) for AD vs non-AD at cut-off 70 (sens 0.78, spec 0.64); multinomial subgroup classification poor
Dataset: Memory-clinic sample (Vienna): 671 participants (HC 78, SCD 77, MCI 288, AD 228)
Key_Novelty: Establishes VVT 3.0 AD-detection cut-off (70, AUC 0.783) while demonstrating its inability to classify across SCD/MCI/AD subgroups
Primary_Limitation: Cannot classify across diagnostic subgroups; cross-sectional; AD group age-confounded (74 vs 56-68y)
Open_Problems: Longitudinal designs; combination with memory measures; age/education-adjusted norms; external validation

Modality: Clinical/Population: longitudinal MCI status transitions (stability/progression/reversion) with health predictors
Method_Architecture: Multinomial logistic regression (classical statistics; A1-type)
Best_Metric: OR 3.13 (CVD predicting MCI stability); OR 1.37 (depression predicting reversion); 74% stayed healthy, 12% progressed, 7% reverted
Dataset: Lothian Birth Cohort 1936 (Scotland): 292 with two MCI assessments at ages 76 and 82 (567 at T1)
Key_Novelty: Quantifies MCI transition fluidity (7% reversion, 12% progression) in LBC1936 and identifies depression as a reversion predictor and CVD as an MCI-stability predictor
Primary_Limitation: Substantial attrition between waves; small transition subgroups (n=20-36); cohort-derived MCI without clinical adjudication; no biomarkers
Open_Problems: Larger samples with repeated assessments; biomarker integration; longer follow-up; attrition handling

Modality: Peripheral/Indirect: ocular biomarkers (PVEP, FERG, OCT m-RNFL) linked to hippocampal MRI volume
Method_Architecture: Classical statistics (ANOVA, correlation, hierarchical regression; A1-type)
Best_Metric: m-RNFL group discrimination (P<0.001, eta2p=0.393); P100 amplitude associated with hippocampal volume after adjustment; m-RNFL+hippocampus associated with ADAS-cog
Dataset: Memory clinic cohort, Ruijin Hospital Shanghai: 59 (19 NC, 23 MCI, 17 AD); PVEP/FERG/OCT + 3T MRI
Key_Novelty: Links functional (P100 amplitude) and structural (m-RNFL) ocular changes to hippocampal volume in MCI/early AD, supporting non-invasive ocular biomarkers of AD neurodegeneration
Primary_Limitation: Small single-centre sample; cross-sectional; no longitudinal conversion data; strict ocular exclusion criteria
Open_Problems: Multicentre longitudinal studies; conversion outcomes; automated OCT segmentation; combination with fluid biomarkers

Modality: Clinical/Population: longitudinal cognitive/functional outcomes with MRI, FDG-PET, CSF biomarkers by smoking status
Method_Architecture: Linear mixed models (classical statistics; A1-type)
Best_Metric: FAQ change estimate 0.13 (p=0.03); EVR change estimate -0.02 (p=0.006); no associations for MMSE/RAVLT/HpVR/FDG/CSF
Dataset: ADNI: 870 MCI subjects (618 non-smokers, 252 smokers), up to 13-year follow-up
Key_Novelty: First longitudinal study showing smoking history predicts faster functional (FAQ) decline and entorhinal cortex atrophy in MCI, with no CSF amyloid/tau effect
Primary_Limitation: Observational; low statistical power for FDG/CSF outcomes due to missing data; ADNI sample homogeneity; combined former/active smokers
Open_Problems: Interventional designs; longer FDG/CSF follow-up; stratified active vs former smokers; diverse populations

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological memory assessment (pFCSRT+IR learning vs retention) for incident-MCI prediction
Method_Architecture: Cox proportional hazards models (classical statistics; A1-type)
Best_Metric: ~20% hazard reduction per SD increase in FR or DFR (independent predictors of incident MCI)
Dataset: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA): 1422 cognitively normal participants, 187 incident MCI, median 8.1-year follow-up
Key_Novelty: Shows learning (FR) alone matches retention (DFR) for incident-MCI prediction, challenging the convention of preferring retention and supporting burden-reduced protocols
Primary_Limitation: Highly educated sample (16.7y education); single test version; consensus-based MCI diagnosis; attrition over follow-up
Open_Problems: Replication in diverse samples; word-list versions; longer retention intervals; trajectory modelling
Journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society 28:292-299 (2022)

Modality: Clinical/Population + Neuroimaging: metamemory/awareness assessment (FOK, MARS) with FDG-PET and structural MRI
Method_Architecture: Classical statistics (ANOVA, correlations, small-volume-correction imaging; A1-type)
Best_Metric: Chance-level episodic FOK accuracy (Hannann coefficient) in converters; higher MARS anosognosia in converters; left inferior prefrontal gray-matter correlate
Dataset: Memory-clinic cohort (Liege, Belgium): 44 aMCI (23 converters, 21 non-converters) + 28 controls, 4-year follow-up, FDG-PET + MRI
Key_Novelty: Shows anosognosia for memory specifically characterises aMCI patients who progress to AD within 4 years, with left inferior prefrontal gray-matter correlates
Primary_Limitation: Small groups; memory-clinic referral bias; no biomarker confirmation of AD pathology; awareness limited to memory domain
Open_Problems: Larger samples; amyloid/tau confirmation; longitudinal awareness tracking; broader task batteries

Modality: Clinical/Population: multi-cohort harmonisation and progression analysis for historical-control (PGSA) trial design
Method_Architecture: Meta-analysis and survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, proportional hazards; A1-type)
Best_Metric: Progression-rate contrast: ~10% (InDDEx trial) vs >30% (other four samples) MCI-to-dementia at 4 years; no verbal-fluency decline in trial sample
Dataset: Five MCI databases: ADNI (395), NACC (4328), InDDEx trial (831), CNG Germany (726), BS-MC Switzerland (1558)
Key_Novelty: Demonstrates via five international MCI datasets that progression heterogeneity (trial ~10% vs cohort >30%) undermines historical-control (PGSA) validity without criteria harmonisation
Primary_Limitation: Heterogeneous historical datasets with different eras/criteria; drug-trial selection effects; no harmonised biomarkers; convenience samples
Open_Problems: Standardised MCI criteria and neuropsychological batteries; harmonised instruments; registry-based collection; PGSA validation on harmonised data

Modality: Behavioural/Digital: conversational speech timing (temporal/acoustic speech features)
Method_Architecture: Linear mixed-effect models + Cartesian genetic programming classifiers (classical statistics + evolutionary computation)
Best_Metric: Multi-class classification accuracy 82.47-84.17% (AD-HC 74%, MCI-HC 63%)
Dataset: Single-centre cohort (Trinity College Dublin / St James's Hospital, Ireland): 20 MCI, 20 mild-to-moderate AD, 40 HC
Key_Novelty: First attempt to examine conversational speech-timing discrimination while investigating its cognitive and structural (brain-volume) underpinnings
Primary_Limitation: Small exploratory sample; moderate pairwise accuracies; no external validation or conversion outcome
Open_Problems: Larger samples; longitudinal conversion outcomes; automated extraction without caregiver; feature fusion with lexical measures

Modality: Clinical/Population: self-reported lifestyle/health risk-factor screening index
Method_Architecture: Stepwise multivariable logistic regression with weighted risk scoring (classical statistics; A1-type)
Best_Metric: AUC 0.73 (95% CI 0.70-0.75) for incident MCI-or-dementia; 45% increased odds per point; validation AUC 0.74
Dataset: Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Study: SLAS-1 (N=1601 development), SLAS-2 (N=3051 validation), NIC community field project (N=437 screened / 194 enrolled)
Key_Novelty: First externally validated MCI-specific risk index with a deployed self-administered field version in a community intervention trial
Primary_Limitation: Modest discrimination (AUC 0.73-0.74) and low PPV; Singapore-only Asian population
Open_Problems: Validation in other ethnic groups; biomarkers; cost-effectiveness; PPV improvement
Journal: Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 8(3):335-344 (2021)

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological cognitive stress testing (LASSI-L semantic interference)
Method_Architecture: ROC analysis with Youden cut-points + chi-square (classical statistics; A1-type)
Best_Metric: AUC 0.905 (95% CI 0.836-0.974) CN vs aMCI-to-dementia on Cued B1 PIE; 83.3% of aMCI progressors classified at PIE cut-point 44%
Dataset: University of Miami / Mount Sinai Medical Center memory-clinic cohort: 116 (51 stable CN, 25 PreMCI reverted, 22 PreMCI->MCI, 18 aMCI->dementia), ~26-month follow-up
Key_Novelty: First longitudinal demonstration that LASSI-L semantic intrusion errors (PIE) predict progression in PreMCI and aMCI
Primary_Limitation: Small subgroups; no neuroimaging correlate; single centre; 26-month horizon
Open_Problems: Amyloid/atrophy correlation; replication; larger samples with extended follow-up

Modality: Clinical/Population: longitudinal cognitive/functional progression trajectories (CDR-SB, FAQ)
Method_Architecture: Growth mixture models + multinomial logistic regression (latent trajectory modelling; A8-type)
Best_Metric: 77% CDR-SB-FAQ class concordance; fast-progression predictors: age>=86 OR 5.26, APOE4 OR 1.94, baseline CDR-SB OR 2.46
Dataset: NACC Uniform Data Set, 26 US Alzheimer's Disease Centers (09/2005-02/2019): 830 incident MCI (515 with FAQ)
Key_Novelty: First large multi-centre latent-class characterisation of both cognitive (CDR-SB) and functional (FAQ) MCI progression with concordance assessment
Primary_Limitation: No biomarker confirmation; NACC referral/volunteer sample; statistical (not clinical) class definitions
Open_Problems: Biomarker-anchored subtypes; external replication; harmonised instruments

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological review (visuospatial working memory, metamemory, visuomotor control)
Method_Architecture: Systematic narrative review (no computational model)
Best_Metric: Qualitative: VSWM and metamemory deficits significant predictors of MCI-to-AD conversion (no pooled effect sizes)
Dataset: 48 studies from systematic search (May 2021): 42 cross-sectional, 6 longitudinal
Key_Novelty: First systematic synthesis framing VSWM, memory-awareness and visuomotor control as an imaging-free neuropsychological window on posteromedial-parietal conversion risk
Primary_Limitation: Only 6 longitudinal studies; visuomotor-conversion relationship unstudied; no meta-analysis
Open_Problems: Longitudinal visuomotor studies; task standardisation; direct PMC neuropsychology vs FDG-PET comparison

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological assessment with PCA dimensionality reduction
Method_Architecture: Principal component analysis + ANOVA with post-hoc comparisons (classical statistics; A1-type)
Best_Metric: Memory component F=4.383 (p=0.016, eta2p=0.087); visuoconstruction component F=5.395 (p=0.006, eta2p=0.105)
Dataset: Single-centre cohort, Arequipa, Peru: 94 community-dwelling older adults (33 normal, 35 SCD, 26 MCI)
Key_Novelty: First PCA-based neuropsychological profiling separating SCD and MCI on memory and visuoconstruction components in a Peruvian (LMIC) cohort
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional, small sample, no conversion follow-up, data-driven factor structure
Open_Problems: Longitudinal validation; factor-structure replication; external cohorts; blood biomarkers

Modality: Clinical/Population: systematic review of bipolar disorder vs MCI/dementia cognition
Method_Architecture: Systematic review / narrative synthesis (no computational model)
Best_Metric: Qualitative: euthymic BD cognitive impairment equal/more severe than MCI (no pooled effect sizes)
Dataset: 5 studies from systematic search (2 BD-vs-MCI, 3 BD-vs-dementia); PROSPERO CRD42020150412
Key_Novelty: First systematic review directly comparing cognitive impairment in bipolar disorder, MCI and dementia
Primary_Limitation: Only 5 eligible studies; narrative synthesis without meta-analysis; heterogeneous mood states
Open_Problems: More direct BD-MCI comparisons; longitudinal BD-to-dementia designs; mood-state and medication control

Modality: Clinical/Population: two-stage screening with trajectory templates and MRI add-on value
Method_Architecture: K-means trajectory clustering + logistic/Cox-type prognosis models (classical statistics + unsupervised clustering; A1-type)
Best_Metric: Optimism-corrected concordance index 0.830 (ADAS-13 longitudinal model); NRI 0.246 (95% CI 0.021-0.848)
Dataset: ADNI-1 (N=85 trajectory development) + ADNI GO/2 (N=374 evaluation); 3-year follow-up
Key_Novelty: First two-stage screening frame quantifying the incremental value of MRI specifically in trajectory-defined high-risk MCI
Primary_Limitation: ADNI-only validation; IDI confidence interval includes zero; change-rate predictors require 1-year revisit
Open_Problems: External validation; additional biomarkers; longer horizons; cost-effectiveness of staged strategy

Modality: Clinical/Population: clinical-data prediction of amyloid PET positivity
Method_Architecture: Multivariate logistic regression (classical statistics; A1-type)
Best_Metric: AUC 0.845 (AD subgroup), 0.775 (all subjects), 0.735 (MCI)
Dataset: Single memory clinic, Seoul St. Mary's Hospital (Catholic University of Korea), 2016-2019: 410 patients with MCI or AD + amyloid PET + APOE genotyping
Key_Novelty: Subgroup-specific (all/MCI/AD) clinical-data models for amyloid-PET positivity using only routine memory-clinic variables
Primary_Limitation: Moderate MCI AUC (0.735); single centre; no external validation; retrospective
Open_Problems: External validation; blood biomarkers (plasma p-tau, NfL); longitudinal amyloid confirmation

Modality: Clinical/Population: neuropsychological composite scoring and unsupervised subtyping
Method_Architecture: Confirmatory factor analysis + PAM clustering + random forest classifiers (A1-type with ML component)
Best_Metric: AUC 0.76 (60-month progression, composite scores) vs 0.69 (standard tests); Cohen's d=1.59
Dataset: ADNI: learning set 40% CU (n=268) + 40% MCI (n=272); evaluation 60% MCI (n=408); four MCI subgroups (159/129/88/32)
Key_Novelty: CFA-derived domain composite scores plus unsupervised clustering characterise four MCI subgroups and outperform standard test totals in progression prediction
Primary_Limitation: ADNI-only; no external validation; data-driven subgroup structure; requires detailed subscores
Open_Problems: External validation; subgroup-outcome mapping; fluid biomarkers; harmonised subscore collection
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring 13:e12237 (2021)

Modality: Clinical/Population: longitudinal PD cohort (BDI, ESS, PDQ-39, five-domain neuropsych battery)
Method_Architecture: Linear mixed models (LMM; A8-type statistical modelling)
Best_Metric: LMM group-by-time: BDI p=0.042, PDQ-39 p=0.035, TMT-A p=0.047, Stroop p=0.037 (PD-SCC vs PD-NC)
Dataset: Huashan Hospital (Fudan University, Shanghai) PD cohort 2010-2020: 383 PD (189 NC, 59 SCC, 135 MCI)
Key_Novelty: First complete motor/nonmotor/QoL progression profile of PD-SCC showing faster depression and QoL decline
Primary_Limitation: Single centre; single-question SCC definition; no external validation
Open_Problems: PD-SCC to PDD conversion; mechanisms of early attention/executive decline
Journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology 8(10):2096-2104 (2021)

Method_Architecture: Multinomial and binomial logistic regression; forward stepwise selection (A1-type)
Best_Metric: Nagelkerke pseudo-R2=0.51 (EFT+RAVLT model); AD-vs-MCI EFT OR 0.89 (0.83-0.96)
Dataset: University Medical Center Groningen memory clinic (Parelsnoer Initiative): 143 patients + 60 HC
Key_Novelty: First direct quantification of emotion recognition added value over episodic memory across AD/MCI/MDD/NI
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional; single centre; no biomarker-confirmed diagnoses
Open_Problems: Emotion-recognition decline trajectory; specificity across dementia subtypes

Method_Architecture: Multistate life tables (A8-type statistical modelling)
Best_Metric: MCI total life expectancy 21.4y (95% CI 19.0-23.6) at age 60; 2.9y lived with dementia
Dataset: Rotterdam Study (population-based cohort, Netherlands) 2002-2014: 648 MCI + 6410 non-MCI aged 60+
Key_Novelty: First population-based MCI life-expectancy estimates distinguishing years with/without dementia by sex, education, subtype
Primary_Limitation: No dementia-subtype data; single population
Open_Problems: Dementia-subtype-specific expectancy; longer follow-up
Journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society 70:481-489 (2022)

Method_Architecture: PRISMA systematic review; random-effects dose-response meta-analysis (A1-type synthesis)
Best_Metric: MD adherence lowers MCI risk RR 0.91 (0.85-0.97) and AD risk RR 0.89 (0.84-0.93) per point
Dataset: Systematic review PubMed/Cochrane/Scopus: 22 studies reviewed, 11 in meta-analysis (12,458 participants)
Key_Novelty: Updated dose-response meta-analysis quantifying MD-adherence benefit for both MCI and AD risk per unit increase
Primary_Limitation: Observational included studies; moderate AD heterogeneity; varying MD scoring
Open_Problems: Causal mechanisms; interaction with APOE; interventional RCT evidence

Method_Architecture: HOG feature extraction; SVM and ELM classifiers (A1-type)
Best_Metric: SVM original-image AUC 0.87 (MCI group, validation); AUCs 0.85/0.87/0.86 normal/MCI/dementia
Dataset: Seventh Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University: 86 subjects (38 normal, 26 MCI, 22 dementia), 332 fundus images
Key_Novelty: Fundus vascular HOG features with SVM/ELM for MCI recognition; original images beat segmentation for SVM
Primary_Limitation: Small sample; single centre; no external validation
Open_Problems: Generalisability; longitudinal prediction; deep-learning architectures

Modality: Clinical/Population: randomized-trial blood-pressure intervention with cognitive outcomes
Method_Architecture: Multistate survival models; competing-risk accounting (A8-type)
Best_Metric: Intensive BP reduces MCI risk HR 0.81 (0.69-0.94); amnestic 0.78 (0.66-0.92); multidomain 0.78 (0.65-0.93)
Dataset: SPRINT trial (NCT01206062), multi-centre US: 9361 hypertensive adults (4678 intensive, 4683 standard)
Key_Novelty: Subtype-specific amnestic/multidomain MCI reduction from intensive BP control with progression-risk quantification
Primary_Limitation: Secondary analysis; exclusions (diabetes, stroke) limit generalisability
Open_Problems: Long-term dementia prevention; biomarker-confirmed MCI; external replication
Journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society 70(5):1384-1393 (2022)

Method_Architecture: Cox proportional hazards and modified Poisson regression (A1-type classical statistics)
Best_Metric: Incident MCI 56 per 1000 person-years; 12.9% progressed to dementia, 47.9% reverted
Dataset: WHICAP (Washington Heights-Inwood Columbia Aging Project, Northern Manhattan): 2903 cognitively normal baseline
Key_Novelty: Separates predictors of incident MCI from predictors of subsequent course in a diverse multiethnic cohort
Primary_Limitation: Algorithmic MCI diagnosis; single urban community
Open_Problems: Biological drivers of reversion; biomarker confirmation; longer uniform follow-up

Method_Architecture: Latent class analysis + actuarial Jak/Bondi criteria (A8-type statistical modelling)
Best_Metric: Diagnostic agreement kappa consensus-LCA 0.80, actuarial-consensus 0.68, actuarial-LCA 0.70; MCI rates 44/53/41%
Dataset: Penn Memory Center / UPenn ADRC: 354 older adults (68% White, 29% Black)
Key_Novelty: First consensus vs actuarial vs LCA MCI diagnostic comparison in racially diverse sample showing method-by-race effects
Primary_Limitation: Single centre; no biomarker confirmation
Open_Problems: Cross-cultural diagnostic fairness; community/population-based validation

Method_Architecture: Qualitative thematic analysis (no computational model)
Best_Metric: not reported (qualitative: 15/19 use MCI term; ACE-III used by all; neuroimaging minimally useful)
Dataset: Semi-structured interviews with 19 old age psychiatrists at five Scottish sites (Nov 2020-Jan 2021)
Key_Novelty: First systematic clinician-perspective study of MCI assessment and risk-disclosure practice in Scottish memory services
Primary_Limitation: Small qualitative sample; single country; self-reported practice
Open_Problems: How disclosure variability affects patient outcomes; guideline development

Modality: Clinical/Population: longitudinal cohort with cognitive-reserve indicators
Method_Architecture: Multistate Markov modelling with competing risks (A8-type)
Best_Metric: 30.3% MCI->NC reversion (83.9% never demented); education >2x RR; grammatical complexity RR ratio 5.78 (1.56-21.42)
Dataset: Nun Study (School Sisters of Notre Dame, US): 619 participants aged 75+, up to 12 annual assessments
Key_Novelty: Joint modelling of MCI reversion vs progression vs death showing cognitive-reserve indicators strongly favour reversion
Primary_Limitation: Homogeneous cohort (female religious sisters); small written-language subsamples
Open_Problems: Mechanisms linking written-language skills to resilience; replication in diverse cohorts

Modality: Clinical/Population: population cohort (Rotterdam Study) with structural MRI correlates
Method_Architecture: Epidemiological multinomial + subdistribution hazard regression (A8-type)
Best_Metric: 5-y cumulative dementia 13.3% (MCI) vs 7.0% (MCRS) vs 2.3% (unaffected); MCI HR 6.95 (3.78-12.75); MCRS HR 3.55 (1.91-6.60)
Dataset: Rotterdam Study (Netherlands): 3025 dementia-free participants aged 60+, 5th wave 2009-2015
Key_Novelty: First single-population comparison of MCRS vs MCI showing gait-defined MCRS carries independent dementia risk and neurodegenerative imaging correlates with a distinct risk-factor profile
Primary_Limitation: Single European population; MCRS/MCI overlap (2.0%) not modelled in outcome analyses
Open_Problems: Mechanism of BMI-MCRS association; whether MCRS and MCI share pathology; validation in non-European populations

Modality: Clinical/Population: community cohort with autopsy neuropathology
Method_Architecture: Epidemiological Cox/logistic regression (A8-type)
Best_Metric: Lowest PF HR 1.95 (1.43-2.66) for MCI; HR 1.55 (1.03-2.33) MCI-to-dementia; AD pathology OR 1.32; vascular pathology OR 3.05
Dataset: Rush Memory and Aging Project (Chicago, US): 1312 dementia-free community participants, up to 21y follow-up, 540 autopsies
Key_Novelty: First study linking composite pulmonary function to MCI-to-dementia progression and to both AD and vascular neuropathology at autopsy
Primary_Limitation: Observational; baseline-only PF; autopsy subset potentially non-representative
Open_Problems: Causality and mechanism (hypoxia vs shared ageing); whether PF-improving interventions preserve cognition

Modality: Clinical/Population: health-economic and QoL burden review
Method_Architecture: Narrative literature review (A8-type)
Best_Metric: MCI carries greater cost burden and worse QoL than normal cognition; informal care a key cost driver; progression-delaying therapy modelled to yield savings
Dataset: PubMed-indexed literature 2014-2021 (North America, Europe, Asia); no primary data
Key_Novelty: First 2014-2021 three-region synthesis covering both humanistic and economic burden of AD including MCI due to AD
Primary_Limitation: Narrative review without systematic pooling; heterogeneous QoL/cost methods; industry sponsorship
Open_Problems: MCI-specific cost estimates; standardised QoL instruments; real-world MCI cost data

Method_Architecture: Causal-adjustment survival analysis (marginal structural Cox + IPW) (A8-type)
Best_Metric: Hearing impairment HR 2.58 (1.73-3.84) for MCI; hearing aid use HR 0.47 (0.29-0.74) vs non-use; aided users vs normal hearing HR 0.86 (ns)
Dataset: National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC, US): 4358 cognitively healthy referral-cohort participants
Key_Novelty: First large NACC study with causal-adjustment (IPW marginal structural Cox) showing hearing aid use eliminates the hearing-loss MCI risk gap
Primary_Limitation: Observational self-reported hearing; referral cohort; no RCT allocation
Open_Problems: Mechanism (cognitive load, sensory deprivation); dose-response of hearing aid use; RCT evidence
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia: Translational Research & Clinical Interventions 8:e12248 (2022)

Method_Architecture: Birth-cohort logistic regression with IQ-discrepancy analysis (A8-type)
Best_Metric: Test-score-only MCI criteria lack temporal stability; IQ-discrepancy did not improve prediction; non-amnestic MCI predicted dementia in ABC21 only
Dataset: Aberdeen 1921 and 1936 Birth Cohorts (Scotland): two community-recruited cohorts with childhood IQ records, phenotyped 1997-2017
Key_Novelty: First use of childhood IQ records to show test-score-only MCI criteria lack temporal stability and IQ-discrepancy adds no dementia prediction
Primary_Limitation: Cohort-specific (Scottish birth cohorts); modest dementia events; no biomarker confirmation
Open_Problems: What underlies subjective age-related cognitive decline if tests do not capture it; MCI criteria revision

Method_Architecture: PRISMA scoping review (A8-type)
Best_Metric: Questionnaires 12,586 participants/131 studies vs PSG 3492/88 vs actigraphy 3359/38; 37.6% of outcome parameters reported once
Dataset: 188 included studies (17,139 participants) from CINAHL, Embase, Medline, Psychinfo, BNI to March 2021
Key_Novelty: First scoping review mapping sleep measurement and outcome-reporting practice in MCI/early dementia, motivating a core outcome set
Primary_Limitation: Scoping design without quantitative pooling; outcome heterogeneity across studies
Open_Problems: Standardised core sleep outcome set; more PSG/actigraphy and non-PSG EEG; circadian/micro-architectural parameters

Method_Architecture: Retrospective cohort logistic regression (A8-type)
Best_Metric: 1-year conversion 18.4%; vitamin D deficiency OR 3.13 (1.04-9.44); first MMSE OR 0.83 (0.73-0.93); first MoCA OR 0.58 (0.45-0.76)
Dataset: Ramathibodi Hospital, Mahidol University (Bangkok, Thailand): 250 MCI patients aged 50+, 2014-2016
Key_Novelty: First Thai hospital-based 1-year MCI-to-dementia conversion estimate (18.4%) with vitamin D deficiency as a novel predictor
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective single-centre; 1-year follow-up; vitamin D subset only
Open_Problems: Vitamin D-MCI conversion causality; larger multi-centre samples; longer follow-up
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring 8:e12272 (2022)

Method_Architecture: PRISMA systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (A8-type)
Best_Metric: Apathy pooled HR 1.54 (95% CI 1.29-1.84) for MCI-to-dementia across 11 studies/9504 individuals; significant AD subgroup
Dataset: 11 longitudinal studies, 9504 MCI individuals (Medline, Embase, Cochrane, Epistemonikos, PsychINFO, CINAHL 2000-2021)
Key_Novelty: Updated meta-analysis confirming apathy predicts MCI-to-dementia conversion (HR 1.54) with significant AD-subgroup effect
Primary_Limitation: Unadjusted pooled HRs; heterogeneous apathy instruments; possible publication bias
Open_Problems: Apathy treatment effects on conversion; apathy vs depression separation; harmonised apathy definitions
Journal: Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry and Neurology 36(1):3-17 (2023)

Method_Architecture: Saccade-paradigm behavioural analysis (A8-type)
Best_Metric: MCI: increased inhibition errors and uncorrected errors in PS/AS and Go/No-go; no classification AUC reported
Dataset: Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine / GARD cohort (South Korea): 79 MCI + 170 age-matched HC
Key_Novelty: First systematic PS/AS + Go/No-go characterisation showing MCI patients fail to self-correct saccadic inhibition errors, mirroring AD
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional; no conversion outcome; no classification AUC
Open_Problems: Whether saccade deficits predict conversion; longitudinal validation; multi-site standardisation

Modality: Clinical/Population: SPRINT MIND post hoc imaging analysis
Method_Architecture: Longitudinal imaging logistic regression (A8-type)
Best_Metric: WMH-progression Z OR 1.51 (1.12-2.04); >=1.4 mL threshold OR 2.89 (1.23-6.81); event rate 12.8% vs 4.7% (p=0.002)
Dataset: SPRINT MIND trial (US): 433 participants with baseline and 48-month MRI
Key_Novelty: First test of WMH progression (not static burden) as an independent risk factor for incident probable dementia/MCI
Primary_Limitation: Post hoc trial subset; 33 dementia/MCI events; single follow-up MRI
Open_Problems: Whether reducing WMH progression lowers dementia incidence; mediation of BP-lowering effect through WMH progression

Method_Architecture: Interventional RCT with ERP (A8-type behavioural/neurophysiological)
Best_Metric: Flanker P3 amplitude and accuracy improvement; MoCA improvement (p<0.05)
Dataset: Tainan Hospital, Taiwan: 24 MCI elderly (12/12 RCT)
Key_Novelty: First randomised trial of a magic-performance cognitive training program in MCI, with ERP (P3) outcomes
Primary_Limitation: Small single-centre sample (n=24); no follow-up; no functional/AD endpoint
