Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional; mediation inferred not causal; single-centre; plasma measures without neuronal confirmation.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal confirmation; mechanistic validation of CDR1as-alpha-Syn regulation; non-diabetic replication.

Modality: 16S rRNA oral microbiome profiling with CSF inflammatory mediators and MCI diagnostic markers
Method_Architecture: 16S rRNA sequencing of oral microbiome; differential abundance analysis; blood and CSF inflammatory marker measurement; association analyses with MCI markers
Best_Metric: Not applicable as classifier (differential abundance and association statistics)
Dataset: Own cohort: 68 older adults (Emory University / Columbia University)
Key_Novelty: Oral microbiome (Pasteurellaceae, Lautropia mirabilis) and CSF inflammation jointly linked to MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small cross-sectional sample; 16S resolution; CSF subset; no longitudinal outcome.
Open_Problems: Larger cohorts; longitudinal follow-up; shotgun metagenomics; periodontal-treatment intervention studies.

Modality: Serum PARP-1, 8-OHdG, NOS2, Abeta1-42, p-tau biomarkers with EVOO dietary intervention and in silico docking
Method_Architecture: MICOIL clinical trial (NCT03362996); 50 ml EVOO daily for 1 year; ELISA of serum oxidative-stress and AD-hallmark biomarkers; group comparisons; molecular docking of EVOO constituents on PARP-1/NOS-2
Best_Metric: Not applicable as classifier (group-level biomarker restoration)
Dataset: MICOIL clinical trial (NCT03362996; Greek Alzheimer's Association / AHEPA Hospital, Thessaloniki)
Key_Novelty: One-year EVOO restores PARP-1/8-OHdG/NOS2 and AD hallmarks to normal in MCI (MICOIL)
Primary_Limitation: Open-label (no placebo oil); small MCI subgroups; biomarker-only endpoints; single-centre Greek cohort.
Open_Problems: Placebo-controlled design; cognitive endpoint correlation; longer follow-up; mechanistic validation of PARP-1/NOS-2 inhibition.

Method_Architecture: Retrospective single-centre memory-clinic cohort; Kaplan-Meier survival + log-rank; factor analysis (PCA) of NTBV subscales; multivariate backward-stepwise binary logistic regression for 5-year mortality; Spearman correlations
Best_Metric: Odds ratio for 5-year mortality (lg10 homocysteine OR 11.20, 95% CI 2.03-61.86; categorical OR 1.84, 95% CI 1.08-3.11)
Dataset: Memory Outpatient Clinic, Medical University of Vienna, Austria (retrospective cohort)
Key_Novelty: Homocysteine independently predicts five-year mortality in SCD/MCI/AD memory-clinic cohort
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective single-centre; no cognitively normal control group; heterogeneous 15-year data collection; listwise case exclusion in models.
Open_Problems: Whether homocysteine is causal (neurotoxic) or only a marker; larger prospective multi-centre studies; standardised screening and vitamin B12/folate substitution trials.

Method_Architecture: Community survey of NW-China elderly; plasma exosome isolation and characterisation (WB Alix/CD9/TSG101, TEM); qPCR of candidate miRNAs; ROC curve analysis with sensitivity/specificity; group comparisons
Dataset: Community cohort, northwestern China (Gansu Province) - own cohort
Sample_N_Approx: 275 community elderly screened; miRNA/ROC cohort 72 (24 MCI, 24 age-matched HC, 24 younger HC)
Key_Novelty: Exosomal miR-483-5p/502-5p are non-invasive plasma MCI biomarkers (AUC 0.901/0.872)
Primary_Limitation: Small ROC cohort (n=72); cross-sectional; no amnestic/non-amnestic MCI distinction; single-region sampling.
Open_Problems: Validation in larger multi-centre cohorts; aMCI/naMCI stratification; mechanistic studies of exosomal miRNA trafficking and brain aging.

Modality: Questionnaire survey of MCI symptom awareness and knowledge needs (self-report)
Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional survey; custom-designed 3-section questionnaire (15 MCI/non-MCI symptom cases, attitudes, knowledge sources/needs); descriptive statistics; content validity CVI 0.92, structural validity, Cronbach alpha 0.78
Best_Metric: MCI symptom awareness score 7.45 +/- 3.58; correct case identification 55.1%
Dataset: Geriatrics Outpatient Department, tertiary-level general hospital, Beijing, China (own survey)
Key_Novelty: First outpatient-clinic survey of MCI symptom awareness and knowledge needs in Beijing older adults
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre outpatient setting; limited stigma items; self-report recall; case-based identification may not reflect real-world recognition.
Open_Problems: Multi-setting surveys (community, rural); more nuanced stigma instruments; linkage of awareness to screening uptake and intervention design.

Modality: Serum metabolomics/lipidomics (LC-MS/MS) plus MoCA cognitive assessment
Method_Architecture: Prospective observational cohort (NCT05347459); T2D patients on metformin monotherapy vs metformin+DPP-4i/SGLT2i vs healthy volunteers; MoCA at baseline and 6 months; untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics/lipidomics with MSEA pathway enrichment; total antioxidant capacity; ANOVA/Tukey comparisons
Best_Metric: MoCA group comparisons (combination therapy comparable to healthy volunteers; metformin monotherapy lower; no within-group change)
Dataset: Alexandria University Main Hospital (AUMH), Egypt - prospective observational cohort (NCT05347459)
Sample_N_Approx: 141 (111 T2D patients on metformin +/- DPP-4i/SGLT2i; 30 healthy volunteers)
Key_Novelty: DPP-4i/SGLT2i protect T2D cognition via oxidative-stress metabolism, not glycemia
Primary_Limitation: Observational (no randomization); drug agent and dose uncontrolled; 6-month horizon; no GLP-1 arm; follow-up attrition.
Open_Problems: Randomized trials; dose/agent-specific effects; longer horizons; mechanistic validation of purine/glutathione/sphingolipid pathways in cognition.

Modality: Nanocarrier drug delivery review (extracellular vesicles, carbon nanotubes)
Method_Architecture: Narrative review of EV and CNT nanocarriers: BBB transport mechanisms, engineering strategies, preclinical applications, dual diagnostic/therapeutic potential in MCI
Best_Metric: Not applicable as classifier (narrative review; no quantitative comparison)
Dataset: Not applicable (narrative review)
Key_Novelty: EVs and carbon nanotubes as dual diagnostic/therapeutic BBB nanocarriers for MCI
Primary_Limitation: Narrative (non-systematic) review; largely preclinical evidence; CNT toxicity and EV scalability unestablished; no clinical MCI data.
Open_Problems: Standardized EV production and cargo loading; CNT biocompatibility/toxicity; early clinical feasibility trials; integration with MCI biomarker-based patient selection.

Method_Architecture: Community cohort; baseline fecal 16s-rDNA high-throughput sequencing; 2-year follow-up; GDS-based progression classification; differential abundance (11 flora) and multivariate regression of Ruminococcaceae/Megamonas with clinical and cognitive factors
Best_Metric: Independent regression associations (Ruminococcaceae decrease with P-tau181 B -1.895 p=0.003; Megamonas increase with diabetes B 2.271 p=0.026)
Dataset: Local community, Shanghai Pudong New Area, China (own cohort)
Sample_N_Approx: 87 MCI (30 progressive, 57 unprogressive) of 1013 screened; 2-year follow-up
Key_Novelty: Ruminococcaceae decrease and Megamonas increase predict rapid 2-year MCI progression
Primary_Limitation: Single baseline stool sample; single-centre; modest sample; no in-vivo mechanistic experiments.
Open_Problems: Serial gut-flora sampling; multi-centre replication; animal/mechanistic studies of butyrate-HDAC-Treg and metabolic pathways; integration with serum biomarkers.

Modality: UCH-L1 protein oxidative/nitrosative modification in brain (review)
Method_Architecture: Invited narrative review of ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L-1: UPS protein quality control; protein carbonyls, 3-nitrotyrosine, HNE modifications; lower UCH-L1 levels and function in AD/MCI brain; therapeutic targeting
Best_Metric: Not applicable as classifier (narrative review of molecular mechanisms)
Dataset: Not applicable (narrative review)
Key_Novelty: UCH-L1 oxidative/nitrosative damage drives neuronal death in AD and MCI brain
Primary_Limitation: Single-author narrative review; largely the author own laboratory findings; no systematic search or quantitative synthesis.
Open_Problems: UCH-L1 as pharmacological target; validation in MCI brain tissue; intervention studies modulating oxidative/nitrosative stress; biomarkers of UPS dysfunction.

Modality: Mouse hippocampal transcriptomics and ERs/NF-kB/AQP1 pathway assays
Method_Architecture: Ovariectomized APP/PS1 female mice as menopausal low-estrogen MCI model; Tiaogeng decoction (TGD) gavage 12 weeks at 0.08/0.16/0.32 g/ml; Morris water maze; RNA-seq + scRNA-seq; ERs/NF-kB/AQP1 pathway validation by WB/RT-qPCR; ELISA for E2, P-tau181, Abeta42, IL-1beta, IL-18
Best_Metric: MWM spatial-memory improvement and pathway-marker changes (high-dose TGD most significant)
Dataset: Own animal experiment: APP/PS1 double-transgenic female mice (Beijing Huafukang), SHUTCM Animal Center
Sample_N_Approx: 180 APP/PS1 female mice (60 dose-screening n=10/group; 120 verification n=30/group) + 10 KM mice
Key_Novelty: Tiaogeng decoction rescues menopausal MCI via ERs/NF-kB/AQP1 signaling (APP/PS1)
Primary_Limitation: Mouse model (not human); ovariectomy approximates menopause; dose-response may not translate; single fixed decoction composition.
Open_Problems: Translation to human menopausal MCI trials; active constituent identification; ER-pathway confirmation in human tissue; combination with standard therapies.

Modality: Plasma cardiometabolic and inflammatory markers (kMCT RCT secondary)
Method_Architecture: Secondary analysis of 6-month double-blind RCT: 30 g/day ketogenic medium-chain triglycerides (kMCT) vs calorie-matched placebo (high-oleic acid) in MCI; fasting plasma before and 2 h after last drink; mixed-model ANOVA with time-by-group interactions
Best_Metric: Time-by-group interactions (ketones p=0.001; 8:0/10:0 acids p=0.001; IL-8 p=0.002; kMCT increases 48%/3800%/4900%/147%)
Dataset: Research Center on Aging, CIUSSS de l Estrie - CHUS, Sherbrooke, Canada (secondary analysis of kMCT RCT)
Key_Novelty: Six-month kMCT minimally alters cardiometabolic markers in MCI, supporting supplementation safety
Primary_Limitation: Secondary outcomes; acute vs chronic drink effects not separable; no food logs; medication confounders; IL-8 increase significance unknown.
Open_Problems: Longer-term trials with dietary control; clarify IL-8 and ketone effects on cognitive benefit; cardiovascular outcome studies in MCI.
Journal: Prostaglandins, Leukotrienes and Essential Fatty Acids 169: 102236, 2021 (Elsevier)

Method_Architecture: Plasmonic asymmetric nanobridge (PAN) single-nanoparticle biosensor; DNA-directed Au crystallization synthesis; FDTD EM simulation; multiplexed LSPR peak-shift detection of pT231/pT181/pS396 (LOD 85.9-143.8 aM); SVM (polynomial kernel degree 3, one-vs-one) with 60/40 train/test split
Best_Metric: SVM classification accuracy 94.47%; ROC AUCs (pT231 0.9659 MCI-HC, 0.9063 MCI-AD; pT181 0.9682 AD-HC)
Dataset: Own clinical cohort: Korea University Anam Hospital / Inha University Hospital, Korea (20 AD / 16 MCI / 11 HC)
Key_Novelty: Asymmetric-nanobridge biosensor with SVM classifies HC/MCI/AD from plasma p-tau at 94.47%
Primary_Limitation: Small single-centre cohort (n=47); SVM split internal only, no external validation; complex fabrication.
Open_Problems: Larger multi-centre cohorts; external SVM validation; longitudinal MCI-to-AD conversion prediction; simplified PAN synthesis for clinical routine.

Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional serum ELISA for spermidine (MyBiosource kit); non-parametric group comparisons adjusted for autopsy status; Pearson correlations with MMSE/CDR/CDR-SOB, neuroimaging volumes, and iron-related proteins (hepcidin, ferritin, transferrin) and Abeta40/42 in a 24-subject subgroup
Best_Metric: Spermidine group difference (MCI vs control 266.9 vs 112.3 ng/ml, p=0.01) and correlations (MMSE r=-0.705 p=0.003; CDR r=0.751 p=0.002; CDR-SOB r=0.704 p=0.007 in pure AD)
Dataset: Oregon Alzheimer's Disease Center Bio-repository (autopsy-anchored; 28/76 neuropathology)
Key_Novelty: First serum polyamine (spermidine) biomarker study in MCI/AD, elevated MCI levels linked to iron
Primary_Limitation: Pilot cross-sectional design; small MCI group (n=12); high inter-individual variability; no multiple-testing correction.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal cohorts; mass-spectrometry corroboration; measurement of SAMDC/ODC/SSAT1 enzyme activity; prospective conversion prediction.

Method_Architecture: ADNI-1 targeted serum metabolomics (Absolute IDQ p180, UPLC/MS-MS); ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis with LSD for group differences; ROC/AUC with bootstrap for diagnosis; Cox proportional hazards (median split; adjusted for gender/age/education) for CN-to-MCI/AD and MCI-to-AD progression; Spearman correlations with CSF Abeta42/T-tau/P-tau and MMSE/ADAS-Cog
Best_Metric: Cox HR for MCI-to-AD progression at low Glu (cutoff 94.2 uM); serum Glu ROC not significant (no diagnostic value)
Dataset: ADNI-1 (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative; 57 US/Canada centres)
Key_Novelty: First large ADNI-1 test: serum glutamate predicts MCI-to-AD progression despite no diagnostic value
Primary_Limitation: Baseline single-cohort (ADNI-1) analysis; no external validation; inconsistent CSF-correlation directions; no cognitive-function correlation.
Open_Problems: External cohorts; repeated longitudinal Glu; combination with other metabolic biomarkers; mechanistic studies of Glu-glutamine cycle in AD.

Method_Architecture: Serum 1H NMR (CPMG, water suppression) metabolomics; 130 deconvoluted signals to 48 representative peaks; PLS-DA with VIP-based variable selection (>0.8); 66/33 discovery/validation split; venetian-blind cross-validation; 200-iteration permutation tests; univariate t-test/Mann-Whitney; ANOVA with Scheffe for MCI subsets; MetaboAnalyst pathway enrichment (global test)
Best_Metric: PLS-DA AUC (AD vs HC 0.9816 sens 93.75% spec 94.18%; AD vs MCI 0.9281 100%/82.35%; HC vs MCI failed AUC ~0.56)
Dataset: Vallecas Project cohort + CIEN Foundation, Madrid, Spain (AD neuropathologically confirmed in 43/51)
Key_Novelty: Neuropathology-anchored NMR serum metabolomics separates AD from HC/MCI, finds progression pathways
Primary_Limitation: HC vs MCI model not predictive (AUC ~0.56); small MCI subgroups (9-14); no external validation.
Open_Problems: Larger MCI cohorts; external validation; longitudinal sampling; standardised metabolite reporting; NMR+MS combination.

Method_Architecture: BALTAZAR MCI subgroup; INNO-BIA (Luminex) plasma assay: free amyloid from undiluted plasma, total after 1/3 denaturing dilution; 3-year follow-up with 6-monthly visits; adjudicated MCI-to-dementia conversion (NIA-AA); logistic and Cox proportional hazards (adjusted age/sex/education/APOE4); quartile and threshold analyses; CSF and MRI subsets
Best_Metric: Cox HR for conversion at highest free-ratio quartile (0.36, 95% CI 0.15-0.87, p=0.022); total ratio HR 0.37 (0.16-0.89, p=0.027)
Dataset: BALTAZAR study (multicentre French cohort; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01315639)
Key_Novelty: First head-to-head: free plasma Abeta42/40 predicts MCI-to-dementia conversion like total ratio
Primary_Limitation: Subgroup selection (106/541); below-detection-limit exclusions (11 samples); modest conversion event count.
Open_Problems: Larger cohorts; standardised free-amyloid assays; external validation; longer follow-up; combination with other biomarkers.

Modality: Free water diffusion MRI + gut microbiota 16S rRNA
Method_Architecture: 3-T multi-shell DWI free water imaging (bi-tensor model, Dipy) with TBSS/GBSS; 16S rRNA (V1-V2) fecal microbiome sequencing (MiSeq); ROI analysis (JHU ICBM-DTI-81 and Desikan-Killiany atlases); correlations of FW with neuropsychological scores (MMSE/MoCA/ADAS-Cog/CDR) and gut microbiota relative abundance
Best_Metric: Correlations of FW with cognition and butyrate-producer abundances (negative FW-butyrate associations; NC/MCI/AD decreasing trend)
Dataset: Own single-centre cohort (Juntendo University Urayasu Hospital, Japan)
Key_Novelty: First human link of gray-matter free water to decreased gut butyrate producers across NC/MCI/AD
Primary_Limitation: Small cross-sectional sample (n=56); causality not established; 16S genus-level resolution; FW is indirect neuroinflammation marker.
Open_Problems: Larger cohorts; longitudinal FW and microbiome; metagenomics/butyrate measurement; SCFA or prebiotic intervention studies.

Method_Architecture: Untargeted serum metabolomics (Metabolon platform, four UPLC-MS/MS methods; ~3300 standards; 1136 metabolites); random forest classification; PCA; generalized linear models relating metabolites to MMSE/MoCA; male vs female MCI vs control comparisons; cultured aged-mouse astrocyte assays for 1-arachidonoyl glycerol (SphK2 phosphorylation, TRPV1 antagonist, G-quadruplex/chromatin)
Best_Metric: Sex-differential metabolite findings (1-palmitoleoyl glycerol/1-AG higher in female MCI; dicarboxylic FAs lower); no classification accuracy reported
Dataset: Own cohort (UTHealth McGovern Medical School, Houston, USA)
Key_Novelty: First sex-stratified serum metabolomics in MCI: female lipid signature via TRPV1/SphK2 in astrocytes
Primary_Limitation: Small cross-sectional cohort (n=80); functional validation in aged-mouse, not human, astrocytes; HRT in 4 female MCI patients.
Open_Problems: Larger cohorts; longitudinal metabolomics; human tissue validation; functional studies of 1-AG/SphK2 in human cells.

Modality: T1 MRI GMV normative modeling + DTI free water + transcriptomics (PD-MCI)
Method_Architecture: Quantile regression normative modeling of GMV (z5/z50/z95 deviation maps; HCP-MMP1.0 360 regions); K-means clustering (Calinski-Harabasz/silhouette; 10-fold CV ARI 0.6875, 1000 permutations); free water imaging (ANCOVA); 11-test five-domain neuropsychological battery; cognitive network density; AHBA imaging transcriptomics with PLS regression and GO enrichment; PPMI external validation (n=115)
Best_Metric: Cluster stability ARI 0.6875; network density 0.95 vs 0.90; subtype group differences (p<0.05)
Dataset: Discovery: Affiliated Brain Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (Nanjing, China); Validation: PPMI (n=115)
Key_Novelty: First normative subtyping of drug-naive PD-MCI with free water + transcriptomics, PPMI-validated
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre discovery; atlas-based (not patient) transcriptomics; cross-sectional; no longitudinal outcome.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal subtype tracking; multi-centre discovery; patient-level transcriptomics; functional validation; subtype-guided treatment trials.

Method_Architecture: EMCOA cohort cross-sectional study; UPLC-MS/MS quantitation of 22 free serum oxysterols (picolinic acid derivatisation); genotyping of 27 SNPs in 6 oxysterol-related genes (MassARRAY/KASP); FFQ dietary assessment; ROC analysis (demographics Model 1, +diet Model 2, +biomarkers); logistic regression with FDR; linear regressions with clinical characteristics
Best_Metric: Combined five-oxysterol panel AUC 0.834 (95% CI 0.804-0.866; sens 81.0%, spec 71.7%); CYP46A1 rs8019753 T carriers OR 0.525 (FDR p=0.003)
Dataset: EMCOA cohort (ChiCTR-OOC-17011882; Beijing Chaoyang / Jincheng / Linyi sites, China)
Key_Novelty: First five-free-oxysterol serum panel with genetics and diet achieving AUC 0.834 for MCI diagnosis
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional; no external validation; only rs8019753 survived FDR in SNP analyses; free-oxysterol assay technically demanding.
Open_Problems: Longitudinal progression prediction; external validation; standardised oxysterol assays; mechanistic studies of 27-OHC in MCI.

Method_Architecture: NA
Best_Metric: NA
Dataset: NA
Key_Novelty: Editorial: Plasma SASP markers (MPO/MMP7) as new MCI risk link and senolytic-trial readouts
Primary_Limitation: Opinion commentary without methodology; not usable as empirical evidence
Open_Problems: SASP-based MCI biomarkers and senolytic-trial monitoring; senotype-specific signatures
Journal: The Journal of Nutrition, Health and Aging 29: 100561, 2025 (Elsevier Masson SAS / SERDI)

Method_Architecture: Case-control; plasma IgG N-glycan UPLC (24 peaks, 17 derived traits); 8-cytokine ELISA (IL-1b, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-a, BDNF, VEGF); multifactorial logistic regression with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR; partial/typical correlation; stepwise logistic regression; ROC/AUC
Best_Metric: Combined IgG N-glycan (GP7,GP14,GP18) + cytokine model AUC 0.939 (95% CI 0.910-0.967)
Dataset: Taian Central Hospital and Taian Hospital of Transportation, Shandong, China (cerebrovascular stenosis cohort)
Key_Novelty: First IgG N-glycan plus cytokine panel (AUC 0.939) for MCI screening in cerebrovascular stenosis
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional, single-centre cohort with no external validation; sociodemographic group differences.
Open_Problems: External multicentre validation; longitudinal progression prediction; mechanistic studies of IgG N-glycan agalactosylation/hypo-sialylation in MCI.

Modality: Blood-based biomarkers (plasma Abeta42, Abeta oligomer, tau)
Method_Architecture: Systematic review + HSROC meta-analysis; seven databases searched; QUADAS-2 appraisal; DOR/sensitivity/specificity pooling; subgroup/meta-regression; Deeks' funnel-plot test
Best_Metric: Plasma tau DOR 52.1 (sens 90%, spec 87%) for AD detection
Dataset: 17 pooled studies (n=2,083) from systematic search of seven databases
Key_Novelty: First HSROC meta-analysis of blood biomarkers (AUC/DOR pooling) for both AD and aMCI detection
Primary_Limitation: Few constituent studies per biomarker; heterogeneous assays/reference standards; limited aMCI evidence.
Open_Problems: More aMCI primary diagnostic-accuracy studies; blood assay standardisation; prospective validation vs CSF/PET gold standards.

Modality: CSF and peripheral blood biomarkers (NfL, GFAP, T-tau, HFABP, NSE, UCHL1, S100B)
Method_Architecture: PRISMA-guided systematic review + random-effects meta-analysis; SMD pooling (DerSimonian-Laird); I2/Cochran Q; meta-regression (age/MMSE/female/APOE4); subgroup by compartment/assay; trim-and-fill
Best_Metric: CSF NfL SMD 0.69 (95% CI 0.56-0.83) for MCI vs controls
Dataset: 107 pooled studies (meta-analysis) + 10 qualitative, from Medline/PsychINFO/Embase/Cochrane search
Key_Novelty: First pooled synthesis of neuronal-injury and astroglial fluid biomarkers across CSF and blood
Primary_Limitation: High heterogeneity; several biomarkers lacked datasets for quantitative pooling.
Open_Problems: Standardised assays/MCI criteria; longitudinal biomarker trajectories; larger blood datasets for HFABP/NSE/UCHL1/S100B.

Method_Architecture: Narrative mechanistic review; postmortem AD brain, B-lymphocyte and fibroblast expression; novel miR-455-3p transgenic (protective) and knockout (detrimental) mouse models; pathway linkage (APP, TGF-beta, NRF2, mitochondria, synaptogenesis)
Best_Metric: Not reported (narrative review; no pooled accuracy metric)
Dataset: Not applicable (narrative review; Reddy-lab tissue/cell, postmortem and transgenic/knockout mouse data)
Key_Novelty: miR-455-3p as peripheral biomarker and therapeutic target; novel transgenic mice support this role
Primary_Limitation: Narrative review dependent on in-house evidence; no large independent human-cohort diagnostic validation.
Open_Problems: Independent multicentre circulating miR-455-3p measurement with ROC evaluation; large-cohort validation; therapeutic mimic studies; assay harmonisation.

Method_Architecture: Targeted UPLC-TQMS metabolomics/lipidomics of serum; univariate/multivariate differential-metabolite analysis; pathway enrichment; random forest, SVM, Boruta classifiers validated by gradient boosting, logistic regression, RF; independent external validation cohort
Best_Metric: 10-metabolite AD and 13-metabolite MCI panels discriminate from CN with high accuracy (external cohort 2 validated)
Dataset: Second Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University cohort 1 + independent cohort 2 (Chinese)
Sample_N_Approx: 120 (cohort 1: 22 AD + 19 MCI + 19 CN; cohort 2: 20 AD + 20 MCI + 20 CN)
Key_Novelty: Externally validated serum metabolomic/lipidomic panels (10 AD, 13 MCI) for AD/MCI discrimination
Primary_Limitation: Small cohorts (n=120); targeted panel; limited phenotyping in validation cohort.
Open_Problems: Larger multicentre cohorts; longitudinal progression prediction; expansion of targeted metabolic panel; pre-analytical standardisation.

Modality: VDR gene single-nucleotide polymorphisms (ApaI, BsmI, FokI, TaqI)
Method_Architecture: Systematic review + meta-analysis; pooled ORs under allelic/dominant/recessive/homozygous/heterozygous models; Newcastle-Ottawa quality assessment; Egger's publication-bias test; Caucasian subgroup analysis
Best_Metric: BsmI dominant model OR 2.04 (95% CI 1.32-3.16) for MCI susceptibility
Dataset: 10 pooled case-control studies (n=3,573) from PubMed/Embase/Cochrane/CNKI
Key_Novelty: First meta-analysis linking VDR BsmI to MCI risk; confirms TaqI-AD association
Primary_Limitation: Population heterogeneity and case-control design; no gene-gene/gene-environment interaction control.
Open_Problems: Studies incorporating gene-gene and gene-environment interactions; standardised phenotypes; prospective confirmation; functional VDR variant studies.
Journal: Advances in Nutrition 12(6): 2255-2264, 2021 (Oxford / Am Soc for Nutrition)

Modality: CSF Abeta/tau biomarkers, amyloid & FDG-PET, brain MRI, APOE genetics
Method_Architecture: Biomarker categorisation (A+/A- amyloid, N+/N- neurodegeneration); CSF Abeta1-42/tau/p-tau; PIB + FDG-PET; MRI; APOE genotyping; prospective MCI-to-dementia follow-up with progression-rate comparison
Best_Metric: 45% of A+ vs 20% of A- MCI progressed to dementia at 30 months
Dataset: FLENI memory clinic (Instituto de Investigaciones Neurologicas Raul Carrea), Buenos Aires, Argentina (incl Argentinian ADNI cohort participants + FLENI database)
Key_Novelty: Biomarker-based MCI prognostication in a Latin American memory clinic (A+/A- gradient)
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre, moderate sample; biomarker cut-off dependent; short follow-up.
Open_Problems: Larger multicentre Latin American cohorts; standardised cut-offs; longer follow-up; CSF vs PET biomarker comparison; plasma biomarker incorporation.

Modality: AD-risk gene SNPs (SORL1, PVRL2, CR1, TOMM40, APOE, PICALM, GWAS 14q, CLU, BIN1); neuropsychological cognition
Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional exploratory descriptive study; Neuronorma neuropsychological battery (language, memory); SNP genotyping of nine AD-risk loci/isoforms; nonparametric statistics with confidence intervals
Best_Metric: Group differences in Neuronorma language/memory performance across BIN1/CLU/CR1 carrier status (no pooled AUC)
Dataset: Universidad Nacional de Colombia / Hospital Universitario Nacional cohort (Bogota, Colombia)
Sample_N_Approx: 54 genotyped (20 healthy controls, 34 MCI) from 261 recruited
Key_Novelty: First link between AD-risk gene polymorphisms (BIN1/CLU/CR1) and cognition in MCI in Colombia
Primary_Limitation: Small exploratory sample; no multiple-comparison correction; cross-sectional design.
Open_Problems: Larger definitive samples; multiple-comparison correction; longitudinal follow-up; gene-gene and gene-environment interactions.

Modality: Structural MRI hippocampal volumetry; PRS-AD and APOE genetics (isoform SNPs rs429358/rs7412 + CSF pQTLs)
Method_Architecture: Longitudinal 5-year mixed-effects models of hippocampal volume; disease-stratified (CU Abeta-, MCI A+, AD A+); sex-stratified analyses; APOE-region exclusion sensitivity analyses
Best_Metric: AD genetic risk (primarily APOE CSF pQTLs) accelerates MCI hippocampal-atrophy (stage-specific); excluding APOE region negates effect
Dataset: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI)
Key_Novelty: Longitudinal 5-year ADNI study: AD genetic risk (APOE CSF pQTLs) accelerates MCI hippocampal atrophy
Primary_Limitation: ADNI-dependency; APOE-region-localised effect limits broader polygenicity inference; no external replication.
Open_Problems: External replication in independent longitudinal cohorts; dissect isoform-vs-pQTL contribution; integrate plasma ApoE; longer follow-up across MCI-to-AD transition.

Modality: CSF and plasma Abeta40/Abeta42/p-tau181/t-tau biomarkers (Lumipulse G assays)
Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional diagnostic-accuracy study; fully-automated Lumipulse G (LUMIPULSE G600II, CLEIA) assays; logistic regression (age/sex); Spearman CSF-plasma correlations; ROC/AUC with Youden-index cut-offs and PPV/NPV
Best_Metric: Plasma Abeta42/p-tau181 ratio AUC 0.895 (95% CI 0.800-0.989; sens 95.1%, spec 82.8%)
Dataset: Memory Clinic, Fondazione Policlinico Universitario A. Gemelli IRCCS, Rome, Italy (local aMCI cohort)
Key_Novelty: Fully-automated Lumipulse G plasma assays (Abeta42/p-tau181 AUC 0.895) for A+/A- aMCI discrimination
Primary_Limitation: Small single-site cohort; no p-tau217 or longitudinal progression data.
Open_Problems: Multicentric validation in larger cohorts; addition of p-tau217; longitudinal follow-up; use-adaptive/multi-risk thresholds; combination with cognitive tests and APOE genotyping.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 11(4): 1073-1078, 2024 (Springer)

Modality: Soluble p-tau and Abeta42 biochemistry (rat hippocampus/CSF); DYRK1A inhibition
Method_Architecture: DYRK1A inhibitor Leucettine L41; NanoBRET; ELISA; Western blot; Morris water maze; open-field; ANOVA
Best_Metric: Not applicable as classifier (MWM 120h probe target-quadrant preference; p=0.003)
Dataset: Own animal experiment (AAV-AD rat model; INSERM/CEA MIRCen, Universite Paris-Saclay)
Sample_N_Approx: 35 Wistar rats (10 vehicle controls, 12 vehicle AAV-AD, 13 L41-treated)
Key_Novelty: DYRK1A inhibitor L41 lowers p-tau, prevents MCI onset in AAV-AD rats despite unchanged Abeta42
Primary_Limitation: Animal model with partial P-tau reduction; no human in-vivo soluble-P-tau measurement method.
Open_Problems: Longer-term follow-up; combined Abeta42+P-tau reduction; in-vivo soluble-P-tau quantification; AI-driven predementia biomarker discovery.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 9(3): 480-490, 2022 (Serdi)

Modality: SNP genotyping + gene-expression microarrays (peripheral blood, ADNI)
Method_Architecture: SNF similarity-network fusion; spectral clustering; label propagation; Kaplan-Meier; VBM; limma enrichment
Best_Metric: MCI-to-AD conversion log-rank p=4.58e-3 (ADNI-1); p=2.26e-4 (ADNI-GO/2)
Dataset: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI-1 discovery; ADNI-GO/2 verification)
Key_Novelty: SNF blood-omics (SNP+expression) defines two MCI subtypes with different AD conversion risk
Primary_Limitation: Small discovery cohort; peripheral-blood omics as brain proxy; no non-ADNI external validation.
Open_Problems: Integration of methylation/miRNA; larger multicentre validation; prospective label-propagation classifier; functional validation of immune-pathway hypotheses.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 8(2): 224-233, 2021 (Serdi and Springer Nature)

Modality: Plasma p-tau217 (ALZPath), GFAP, NfL (Simoa); MRI volumetry; clinical scales
Method_Architecture: ANCOVA group comparisons; multiple linear regression; binary logistic regression
Best_Metric: Plasma p-tau217 OR 10.37 (95% CI 3.00-35.02, p<.001) for MCI-to-dementia progression
Dataset: 1Florida Alzheimer's Disease Research Center (UF / UM / Mt. Sinai Miami)
Sample_N_Approx: 378 cross-sectional (76 CNAD-, 198 MCIAD-, 104 MCIAD+); 207 MCI longitudinal
Key_Novelty: p-tau217 stratifies AD vs non-AD MCI; OR 10.37 progression; recruitment-source bias highlighted
Primary_Limitation: Observational; no CSF/PET AD confirmation; 3-year follow-up; recruitment-source confounding.
Open_Problems: Standardised p-tau217 cut-offs; non-AD biomarker panels; CSF/PET reference standards; longer follow-up; community-based recruitment.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 12: 100011, 2025 (Elsevier Masson / SERDI)

Modality: Pseudocontinuous ASL MRI cerebral perfusion; PiB-PET amyloid
Method_Architecture: Spatial covariance (SSM/PCA) ADRP; pcASL CBF; ROC analysis
Best_Metric: Left precuneus relative rCBF AUC 0.85 (95% CI 0.75-0.95) for MCI-AD vs non-AD MCI; AUC 0.80 vs CUC
Dataset: Tianjin Medical University General Hospital, Tianjin, China (local MCI + CU cohort, PiB-PET classified)
Key_Novelty: ASL left precuneus rCBF (AUC 0.80-0.85) identifies AD-etiology MCI via amyloid-PiB stratification
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre moderate sample; relative CBF; PiB- MCI etiologically heterogeneous.
Open_Problems: Multi-centre validation; longitudinal progression prediction; combination with plasma biomarkers; standardised ASL/absolute quantification.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 12: 100031, 2025 (Elsevier Masson / SERDI)

Method_Architecture: Consensus methodology: pre-meeting online survey + in-person meeting; qualitative/quantitative synthesis
Best_Metric: Not applicable (consensus recommendations; no quantitative accuracy metric)
Dataset: SEACURE consortium expert survey and consensus (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam)
Sample_N_Approx: Not reported in source (expert consensus of SEACURE members from 6 SEA countries)
Key_Novelty: First SEACURE multi-country consensus roadmap for MCI diagnosis/management across Southeast Asia
Primary_Limitation: Expert-consensus opinion without empirical SEA prevalence data or implementation validation.
Open_Problems: SEA MCI epidemiology; harmonised biomarker access; country-validated cognitive tests; digitized diagnostics; implementation research.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 12: 100110, 2025 (Elsevier Masson / SERDI)

Modality: Narrative review of published AAPN country-level AD data
Method_Architecture: Narrative literature synthesis; country-by-country comparison of prevalence/diagnostics/treatment/guidelines
Best_Metric: Not applicable (narrative review; no quantitative accuracy metric)
Dataset: Published literature across AAPN countries (Australia, New Zealand, Korea, Japan, China, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, Pacific)
Sample_N_Approx: Not reported in source (narrative review of published country-level literature)
Key_Novelty: Narrative review of early-AD prevalence, diagnostics and treatment across Asia/Australasia/Pacific
Primary_Limitation: Narrative non-systematic review with sparse, non-comparable AAPN country-level data and industry authorship.
Open_Problems: Systematic country-level early-AD data; biomarker/specialist capacity; guideline updates incl. amyloid-targeting therapies; Pacific-nation equity.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 12: 100362, 2025 (Elsevier Masson / SERDI)

Modality: Plasma Abeta42/Abeta40 by ABtest-MS; amyloid-PET; MRI volumes
Method_Architecture: ABtest-MS antibody-free IP-MS; Cox proportional-hazards; linear mixed-effects models
Best_Metric: Low Abeta42/40 HR 3.25 (95% CI 1.17-9.01) for conversion to MCI due to AD; HR 2.84 for Abeta-PET+
Dataset: Fundacio ACE Healthy Brain Initiative (FACEHBI), Barcelona, Spain (AMYPAD consortium data)
Sample_N_Approx: 200 individuals with subjective cognitive decline (SCD), 5-year follow-up
Key_Novelty: ABtest-MS plasma Abeta42/40 predicts 5-yr atrophy and SCD-to-MCI conversion (HR 3.25)
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre moderate cohort; weak cognitive-decline associations; MS assay complexity.
Open_Problems: Multi-centre validation in larger SCD cohorts; integration with p-tau217/GFAP/NfL; longer follow-up; harmonised MS protocols; cutoff validation.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease (in press, 2025), article 100465 (Elsevier Masson / SERDI)

Modality: Plasma NfL/pTau217; MRI gray-matter atrophy; ADAS-cog/ADL clinical endpoints
Method_Architecture: Phase 3 randomized modified delayed-start RCT; ADAS-cog11/13 and ADCS-ADL23; plasma NfL/pTau217; MRI atrophy
Best_Metric: MCI ADAS-cog13 early- vs delayed-start HMTM 16 mg/day at 78 wk (p=0.0291) and 104 wk (p=0.0308); NfL reduction p=0.0291
Dataset: Phase 3 trial TRx-237-039 (82 centres: Canada, EU, UK, USA)
Sample_N_Approx: 598 amyloid-PET-positive participants (263 MCI due to AD; 335 mild to moderate dementia due to AD)
Key_Novelty: Phase 3 HMTM arrests NfL/atrophy progression; MCI ADAS-cog13 separation at 78/104 wks
Primary_Limitation: Co-primary endpoints missed at 52 weeks; MCI benefit late-emerging and subgroup-based.
Open_Problems: Confirmation in replication study; tau-positive enrichment; earlier primary time points; longer-term outcomes; comparison with amyloid antibodies.
Journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease 13: 100480, 2026 (Elsevier Masson / SERDI)

Method_Architecture: Cox proportional-hazards models; plasma LCFA quantification; 48-month follow-up
Best_Metric: Fully-adjusted HR 1.3-2.2 (P=0.0005-0.003) for MCI-to-AD by C14:0/C16:0/C18:0
Dataset: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI-1, 63 sites across USA and Canada)
Sample_N_Approx: 618 AD-free ADNI-1 participants (226 CN, 392 MCI), 48-month follow-up
Key_Novelty: Saturated LCFAs predict MCI-to-AD conversion (HR 1.3-2.2) in ADNI; C20:0 null; no CN-to-MCI effect
Primary_Limitation: Observational single-measurement design; ADNI cohort enrichment; C20:0 null unexplained.
Open_Problems: Prospective validation; repeated LCFA measurements; dietary/metabolic interventions; mechanistic LCFA-neuroinflammation studies; gene-environment interactions.

Modality: Urinary PAH metabolites (GC-MS); matched case-control clinical epidemiology
Method_Architecture: Matched case-control (4:1 frequency matching); GC-MS urinary PAH quantification; conditional logistic regression
Best_Metric: Per log-unit urinary 1-OHP OR 1.15 (aMCI)/1.16 (AD); 2-NAP OR 1.11 (aMCI)/1.13 (AD)
Dataset: Samsung Medical Center cases + EPINEF community-based matched controls, Seoul, Korea (2014-2019)
Key_Novelty: Urinary PAH metabolites (1-OHP, 2-NAP) raise aMCI/AD risk in matched case-control (OR 1.11-1.16)
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional case-control; recent-exposure urinary markers; residual confounding; single Korean site.
Open_Problems: Prospective cohorts with repeated PAH measurement; APOE and other confounders; multi-centre validation; mechanistic PAH-AD studies; source apportionment.
Journal: Heliyon 10(15): e35614, 2024 (Elsevier / Cell Press, open access)

Modality: Peripheral blood multiomics (miRNA, transcriptome, proteome, metabolome)
Method_Architecture: Multiomics profiling + DataRobot AI (XGBoost) classifier; composite hsa-miR-4455/let-7b-3p ratio index; OPLS-DA.
Best_Metric: AUC 0.971 (hsa-miR-4455/hsa-let-7b-3p ratio); sensitivity 0.8, specificity 1.0
Dataset: IHPP community checkup (Hirosaki) + JPSC-AD validation, Japan
Sample_N_Approx: 74 (25 aMCI + 25 HC discovery; 12 aMCI + 12 HC validation)
Key_Novelty: Peripheral-blood multiomics+AI: hsa-miR-4455/let-7b-3p ratio discriminates aMCI (AUC 0.971)
Primary_Limitation: Small discovery cohort (n=50); only miRNA biomarkers independently validated; low miRNA detection sensitivity in the validation microarray.
Open_Problems: Open: validation in large cohorts; causality of GCN1/ISR changes; clinical cut-off standardisation. Applications: community-based aMCI screening with blood miRNA panels. Methodologies: multiomics integration, DataRobot AI feature ranking, composite ratio indices. Achievable: high-specificity early screening and hypothesis-driven biomarker follow-up.
Journal: Current Research in Translational Medicine 71 (2023) 103367 (Elsevier Masson SAS, open access)

Modality: Dental examination + MCI screening (community checkup cohort)
Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional cohort; MCI screening test (CDR-validated); PPD-based periodontitis staging; multivariate logistic regression.
Best_Metric: Adjusted OR 4.024 (95% CI 1.768-9.161, p<0.001) severe periodontitis vs MCI
Dataset: J-SHIPP dental health checkup, Ehime University Hospital, Japan
Key_Novelty: Severe periodontitis (PPD>6mm) independently linked to MCI (OR 4.024) in community dental checkup
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional design cannot establish causality; high selection bias of anti-aging checkup participants; single Japanese centre.
Open_Problems: Open: causality and treatment effects; mechanism via systemic inflammation. Applications: dental checkup screening for MCI risk; oral-health interventions. Methodologies: PPD-based periodontitis staging, MCI screening, multivariable logistic regression. Achievable: identifying high-risk older adults through routine dental examinations.
Journal: The Journal of Aging Research & Lifestyle 13:108-112, 2024 (SERDI, open access)

Method_Architecture: Longitudinal tau-PET SUVR change; FRS/BMI moderation; hierarchical linear regression with sex/APOE-e4 interactions.
Best_Metric: Sex effect on tau change: Braak34 right beta 0.218 (p=.029), left 0.213 (p=.016); Braak56 right 0.192 (p=.016)
Dataset: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), multi-site US/Canada
Key_Novelty: Vascular risk (FRS) fails to explain female-biased tau in Abeta+ MCI; BMI-tau link male-specific
Primary_Limitation: Small ADNI-only sample (n=52); two tau-PET timepoints; several sex effects only trending after FRS adjustment.
Open_Problems: Open: drivers of female-biased tau accumulation; mechanisms of male-specific BMI effect. Applications: sex-stratified dementia risk assessment; vascular risk management targets. Methodologies: longitudinal tau-PET SUVR composites, FRS/BMI moderation modelling. Achievable: identifying sex-specific modifiable factors for AD risk stratification.
Journal: The Journal of Aging Research & Lifestyle 14 (2025) 100001 (Elsevier Masson SAS / SERDI, open access)

Method_Architecture: mtDNA bisulfite methylation sequencing; Random Forest classifier with cognitive and risk-factor features; independent test set.
Best_Metric: AUC-ROC 0.903; test accuracy 83.2% (95% CI 75.2-89.4%); sensitivity 95.1%, specificity 70.7%
Dataset: Seven international cohorts (Knight ADRC, AIBL, HUB, HCB, CITA, HSCSP, HGH)
Sample_N_Approx: 600 (P group n=307 MCI-to-ADD, plus stable MCI and CN groups)
Key_Novelty: Blood mtDNA methylation predicts MCI-to-ADD progression, beta-amyloid-independent (AUC 0.903)
Primary_Limitation: Clinical-progression endpoint without universal biomarker confirmation; specificity 70.7%; external replication in large prospective cohorts still required.
Open_Problems: Open: replication in diverse cohorts; mechanistic link between mtDNA methylation and neuronal dysfunction. Applications: blood-based prognosis for MCI patients in memory clinics and trials. Methodologies: mtDNA bisulfite sequencing, Random Forest modelling, independent-set testing. Achievable: early identification of MCI patients likely to progress to ADD.

Modality: Blood DNA methylation epigenetic clocks + cognition transitions
Method_Architecture: Epigenetic clocks from DNA methylation; Cox proportional hazards for NC/MCI/dementia transitions; race interaction analysis.
Best_Metric: HR 1.56 (1.15-2.11) GrimAge NC-to-MCI; HR 1.62 (1.09-2.40) Horvath skin&blood MCI-to-dementia; Non-White HRs up to 4.33
Dataset: US Health and Retirement Study (HRS), 2016-2020
Key_Novelty: Epigenetic age acceleration predicts cognitive transitions only in Non-Whites (HR up to 4.33)
Primary_Limitation: Short follow-up with few dementia events (n=42); telephone-based cognitive assessment; heterogeneous Non-White grouping.
Open_Problems: Open: mechanisms of racial differences; generalizability beyond HRS. Applications: risk stratification for cognitive decline using epigenetic clocks; targeted prevention in minority populations. Methodologies: DNA-methylation epigenetic clocks, Cox transition modelling, interaction analysis. Achievable: equity-informed biological aging screening.
Journal: Global Transitions 8: 1-9, 2026 (published online 2025; KeAi/Elsevier, open access)

Method_Architecture: NA (non-research erratum; two reference-list corrections to P-493).
Best_Metric: NA
Dataset: NA (correction to Biomarkers in Neuropsychiatry 9 (2023) 100069, corpus P-493)
Sample_N_Approx: Not reported in source (erratum; no participants)
Key_Novelty: Erratum: correction of two reference-list citations in P-493 (Gaugler 2020 addition; Xu et al. year 2018->2020)
Primary_Limitation: Correction notice without methodology; not usable as empirical evidence
Open_Problems: None - parent review (P-493) content unchanged; erratum only corrects its reference list

Method_Architecture: PRISMA systematic review; random-effects meta-analysis (Hedges' g); meta-regression on age, sex, MMSE.
Best_Metric: Hedges' g: serum/plasma IL1beta, IL6, IL8, IL18, CRP, hsCRP raised in AD; CSF YKL40, MCP-1 raised in AD; MMSE-cytokine meta-regression
Dataset: 106 case-control studies (pooled)
Key_Novelty: Cognition, sex and age drive inflammation-marker heterogeneity across MCI and AD (meta-regression)
Primary_Limitation: Case-control pooling cannot establish causality; biospecimen/assay heterogeneity; study-level meta-regression.
Open_Problems: Open: causal direction; central vs peripheral inflammation contributions; menopause-related sex effects. Applications: inflammation-targeted cognitive-risk stratification; monitoring in lifestyle interventions. Methodologies: random-effects meta-analysis with meta-regression, Hedges' g. Achievable: consensus on which inflammatory markers track cognition.
Journal: Brain, Behavior, & Immunity - Health 40: 100819, 2024 (Elsevier, open access)

Method_Architecture: Paired plasma-CSF SOMAscan proteomics; hierarchical clustering; Cox proportional hazards with Bonferroni correction.
Best_Metric: Cox HR 1.936/SD sIL6RA (p=0.0018, Bonferroni-robust); SMOC1 HR 1.3 (p=0.002)
Dataset: ACE Alzheimer Center Barcelona (paired plasma-CSF, SOMAscan)
Key_Novelty: sIL6RA predicts MCI-to-dementia conversion independent of amyloid/tau (6/63 mediators correlate)
Primary_Limitation: Single-centre ACE cohort; moderate effect sizes; external multi-centre replication still required.
Open_Problems: Open: external replication; mechanism of sIL6RA action; therapeutic implications. Applications: blood-based progression risk stratification in MCI. Methodologies: SOMAscan proteomics, hierarchical clustering, Cox survival analysis with Bonferroni correction. Achievable: routine monitoring of sIL6RA/SMOC1 for MCI prognosis.
Journal: Brain, Behavior, & Immunity - Health 42: 100899, 2024 (Elsevier, open access)

Modality: Plasma immune biomarker panel (TTB training intervention)
Method_Architecture: Randomized TTB physical+cognitive training; plasma immune biomarker panel (Proquantum/ELLA); pre/post group comparisons.
Best_Metric: Group biomarker change: IL-6, IL-17A, TNF-alpha, CCL11 down post-TTB; IL-10/TGF-beta/IL-4/BDNF maintained in training vs decline in control
Dataset: Train the Brain (TTB) study, Pisa, Italy (CDCD/AOUP recruitment)
Key_Novelty: TTB training reverses an MCI inflammatory fingerprint; IL-10 an efficacy biomarker
Primary_Limitation: Moderate sample with COVID-19-related attrition; exploratory biomarker panel; single-centre Italian cohort.
Open_Problems: Open: durability of biomarker changes; causal link to cognitive benefit. Applications: blood-based monitoring of multidomain intervention response; personalised lifestyle prescription. Methodologies: multiplex plasma biomarker panels (Proquantum/ELLA). Achievable: identifying training responders via immune profiling.
Journal: Brain, Behavior, & Immunity - Health 48: 101062, 2025 (Elsevier, open access)

Modality: Serum AD hallmarks + inflammatory markers (VR training)
Method_Architecture: Randomized VRADA VR dual training (12 weeks); serum ELISA for IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, Abeta42/40, total tau, p181-tau; between-group comparisons.
Best_Metric: Between-group at follow-up: IL-1beta lower, Abeta42/Abeta40 higher, total tau/p181-tau/p181-tau-Abeta42 lower in VRADA vs Control
Dataset: Alzheimer Hellas Day Care Centre 'Saint Helen', Thessaloniki, Greece (2020-2022)
Key_Novelty: 3-month VRADA VR dual training improves serum Abeta42/Abeta40 and lowers tau/IL-1beta vs control in MCI
Primary_Limitation: Small sample (n=29); short follow-up; no cognitive endpoint; between-group effects without robust within-group changes.
Open_Problems: Open: replication with larger samples; mechanism linking VR exercise to amyloid/tau modulation; durability of effects. Applications: scalable non-pharmacological MCI intervention in day-care centres. Methodologies: VR cycling with cognitive dual tasks, serum ELISA biomarker panels. Achievable: accessible VR-based lifestyle intervention for MCI.

Modality: CSF bacterial proteins FliC/DING + COX-1/2, Abeta42, tau
Method_Architecture: Indirect ELISA for FliC, DING, COX-1, COX-2, Abeta42, total tau in CSF; correlation and multilinear regression.
Best_Metric: CSF FliC and DING increased in AD vs controls; FliC elevated in MCI vs controls; correlations with tau and COX-1/2
Dataset: AHEPA University General Hospital CSF biobank (GAADRD), Thessaloniki, Greece
Key_Novelty: First CSF FliC/DING evaluation linking microbiome to COX and AD-hallmark markers
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional exploratory study with semi-quantitative ELISA; no external or longitudinal validation.
Open_Problems: Open: causative vs correlative role of bacterial proteins; which microbiota contribute; external validation. Applications: CSF (and potentially blood) microbiome-inflammation staging. Methodologies: indirect ELISA, multilinear regression. Achievable: microbial-involvement staging along the MCI-AD continuum.

Modality: Remote video-call multidomain lifestyle intervention; NTB cognition
Method_Architecture: Multicentre single-masked RCT; 12-month remotely-delivered personalised multidomain intervention; ITT analysis of 24-month NTB.
Best_Metric: Adjusted mean difference 0.06 (95% CI -0.001 to 0.128) in 24-month NTB; p=0.055
Dataset: APPLE-Tree trial, 11 sites in England (ISRCTN17325135)
Sample_N_Approx: 746 randomised (374 intervention, 372 control); 635 (85%) in primary analysis
Key_Novelty: First multicentre RCT of a low-intensity remote multidomain prevention programme
Primary_Limitation: Primary cognitive endpoint not statistically significant (p=0.055); 15% missing primary-outcome data.
Open_Problems: Open: differential effects by SCD vs MCI and risk profile; durability beyond 24 months. Applications: scalable dementia-prevention services. Methodologies: remote video-call behavioural intervention, NTB battery. Achievable: wide-scale low-intensity prevention.
Journal: The Lancet Healthy Longevity 6: 100777, 2025 (Elsevier, open access)

Modality: UWF retinal and choroidal vasculature imaging
Method_Architecture: UWF fundus imaging (Optos SLO); automated VAMPIRE-UWF 2.0 analysis of vessel width/choroidal density; group comparisons MCI vs controls.
Best_Metric: Retinal artery/vein width gradients less negative (P<0.001; P=0.027); smaller width intercepts (P<0.001; P=0.017); higher choroidal density (P=0.025)
Dataset: Eye Multimodal Imaging in Neurodegenerative Disease Study (EMINDS), Duke University
Sample_N_Approx: 131 eyes of 82 MCI patients and 230 eyes of 133 cognitively normal participants
Key_Novelty: Largest UWF retinal/choroidal MCI study: thinner vessels, higher choroidal density
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional single-centre design without diagnostic accuracy metrics or AD-biomarker confirmation.
Open_Problems: Open: whether parameters predict MCI-to-AD progression; pathological basis of choroidal density increase. Applications: ophthalmic screening adjuncts. Methodologies: UWF imaging with automated vessel/choroidal analysis. Achievable: non-invasive retinal biomarker panels.

Method_Architecture: Conference symposium perspective (IBRO 2023) on the AbO hypothesis; no experimental data.
Best_Metric: Not reported (conference perspective abstract; no classification/performance metric)
Dataset: Not applicable (conference perspective abstract; no study cohort)
Sample_N_Approx: Not reported in source (no study population)
Key_Novelty: Oligomer-selective antibody and imaging landscape for AD diagnosis/therapy at IBRO 2023
Primary_Limitation: Conference perspective with no primary data or sample; preclinical evidence only; financial-interest disclosure.
Open_Problems: Open: which AbO species are most pathogenic; whether targeting them changes clinical course. Applications: immunotherapy and diagnostic imaging probes. Methodologies: AbO-selective antibodies, scFv/AAV expression, MRI/PET probes. Achievable: oligomer-targeted early diagnostics/therapies.
Journal: IBRO Neuroscience Reports 15 (2023) supplement (IBRO 2023 Congress); Elsevier

Modality: Serum inflammatory cytokines and AD hallmarks; PE +/- cognitive training
Method_Architecture: 3-arm PE / PE+cognitive / control intervention (32 sessions, 45 min, 2-3x/week, 3 months); serum ELISA IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha, Abeta42/40, t-tau, p-tau181 at baseline and 3 months.
Best_Metric: PE and Mixed reduced IL-1beta, IL-6, p-tau181; PE-only raised Abeta42 and Abeta42/40 and lowered p-tau181/Abeta42; Mixed-only lowered TNF-alpha, Abeta40, t-tau
Dataset: Alzheimer Hellas Day Care Centre 'Saint Helen', Thessaloniki, Greece (2020-2021)
Sample_N_Approx: 74 MCI patients (Control, PE, PE+cognitive-training Mixed groups)
Key_Novelty: PE+cognitive training lowers p-tau181 and inflammation; PE alone raises Abeta42/40 in MCI serum
Primary_Limitation: Uneven group allocation and small per-group samples; no cognitive endpoint or multiple-comparison control.
Open_Problems: Open: durability and cognitive translation of biomarker changes; optimal dose/combination. Applications: community exercise-based dementia prevention. Methodologies: serum ELISA biomarker panels with intervention designs. Achievable: biomarker-guided non-pharmacological MCI management.

Method_Architecture: Cross-sectional study; PCA of occupational exposure factors (PC1/PC2); NLRP3 SNP genotyping (rs10754558, rs10925027, rs3806265, rs4612666); logistic regression with interaction terms.
Dataset: Aluminum electrolysis production factory, Guangxi, China
Key_Novelty: First NLRP3 gene x occupational-exposure interaction study for MCI odds in aluminum workers
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional single-factory design with PCA-based exposure; no external replication.
Open_Problems: Open: causal NLRP3-inflammasome pathway; replication in other cohorts. Applications: occupational MCI screening and exposure reduction. Methodologies: PCA exposure modelling, SNP genotyping, logistic regression with interactions. Achievable: genotype-informed occupational risk stratification.
Journal: Hygiene and Environmental Health Advances 16: 100144, 2025 (Elsevier, open access)

Modality: Multimodal - genomics, metagenomics, metabolomics, MRI, EEG
Method_Architecture: Multimodal profiling (genomics/metagenomics/metabolomics/MRI/EEG); random forest classifiers (80/20 stratified split, SMOTE, GridSearchCV, RFE) for SCD/MCI/AD vs HC.
Best_Metric: Random forest AUCs: 0.78 (SCD vs HC), 0.84 (MCI vs HC), 0.98 (AD vs HC)
Dataset: Own multimodal cohort (BGI Genomics / Shenzhen People's Hospital, China)
Key_Novelty: Integrated multi-omics-MRI-EEG stage map of SCD-to-MCI-to-AD; EEG early marker
Primary_Limitation: Cross-sectional single-centre staging without external validation of the ML classifiers.
Open_Problems: Open: causality of gut-brain axis dysregulation; external generalisability of classifiers. Applications: EEG-based early screening; multimodal staging panels. Methodologies: multi-omics integration, random forest with SMOTE/RFE. Achievable: objective early-screening support in memory clinics.
Journal: Alzheimer's & Dementia 21: e70182, 2025 (Wiley / Alzheimer's Association, open access)

Method_Architecture: Serum exosome isolation (ultracentrifugation); small RNA sequencing; differential expression; target prediction; GO/KEGG enrichment; ROC-AUC per miRNA across NC/MCI/AD.
Best_Metric: ROC AUC >0.9 (miR-210-3p, miR-151-3p) for NC/MCI/AD discrimination; further miRNAs AUC >0.8.
Dataset: Shanghai Mental Health Center / Changning District Mental Health Center cohort, China (2022-2024)
Key_Novelty: Stage-specific plasma exosomal miRNA signatures across NC-MCI-AD; miR-210-3p/miR-151-3p AUC>0.9
Primary_Limitation: Very small single-centre cohort (n=29) without external or longitudinal validation of the miRNA panel.
Open_Problems: Open: causal role of exosomal miRNAs in AD progression; cross-population stability. Applications: blood-based early AD/MCI screening and monitoring. Methodologies: small RNA-seq, exosome isolation, ROC biomarker evaluation. Achievable: liquid-biopsy miRNA panels for memory-clinic triage.
Journal: RSC Advances 15: 23670-23680, 2025 (Royal Society of Chemistry, open access)

Modality: CSF O-glycoproteome and endogenous peptidome; LC-MS/MS
Method_Architecture: Universal boronic acid enrichment; high-pH fractionation; EThcD LC-MS/MS; Byonic searching; three-step database search; pooled-group glycoform comparison (control/MCI/AD).
Best_Metric: 308 O-glycopeptides from 110 O-glycoproteins in healthy CSF (largest reported CSF O-glycoproteome); descriptive trends (decreasing fucosylation, increasing peptide O-glycosylation).
Dataset: Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center (ADRC) CSF biobank, USA
Sample_N_Approx: 48 (16 healthy controls, 16 MCI, 16 AD; pooled per group)
Key_Novelty: Largest unbiased CSF O-glycoproteome dataset; first CSF peptide O-glycosylation profile in MCI/AD
Primary_Limitation: Discovery design with pooled per-group CSF samples and no per-subject quantitative statistics or validation.
Open_Problems: Open: functional role of fucosylation in AD. Applications: CSF glycopeptide biomarker panels; peptidomics diagnostics. Methodologies: boronic acid enrichment, EThcD glycoproteomics. Achievable: deeper CSF glycoproteome coverage for biomarker discovery.

Modality: Plasma p-Tau181/Abeta42-40 (Simoa); rs-fMRI DMN FC; cortical thickness
Method_Architecture: Simoa plasma biomarker measurement; resting-state fMRI DMN functional connectivity; cortical thickness analysis; logistic regression with backward selection; Hosmer-Lemeshow calibration; ROC-AUC.
Best_Metric: Combined clinical+plasma+imaging model AUC 0.987 (95% CI 0.903-1.000) for PD-MCI vs PD-NC.
Dataset: Own single-centre cohort: early drug-naive PD patients, Nanjing (China)
Key_Novelty: Integrated clinical+plasma (Simoa)+DMN-FC+cortical-thickness PD-MCI diagnostic model, AUC 0.987
Primary_Limitation: Small single-centre sample without external validation; backward-selection model risks overfitting.
Open_Problems: Open: external generalisability and longitudinal predictive value. Applications: PD-MCI screening and stratification. Methodologies: Simoa plasma assays, resting-state FC, cortical thickness, logistic regression. Achievable: integrated biomarker panels for early PD cognitive screening.

Method_Architecture: Prospective cohort follow-up (33 months); Cox multivariate regression; dichotomised prognostic score (age, MMSE, aMCI); ROC-AUC; NPV/PPV.
Best_Metric: Score 0-3: conversion 6% (score 0) to 72% (score 3); ROC AUC 0.72 (95% CI 0.66-0.75); MMSE HR 0.84, aMCI HR 2.35, age HR 1.05.
Dataset: University of Ferrara memory clinic cohort (Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria S. Anna), Italy
Key_Novelty: Simple 0-3 clinical score (age, MMSE, aMCI) stratifies MCI-to-dementia risk from 6% to 72%
Primary_Limitation: Derivation cohort only, without external validation; modest discrimination (AUC 0.72) and no biomarker augmentation.
Open_Problems: Open: external validation and biomarker augmentation. Applications: primary-care risk stratification for dementia in MCI. Methodologies: Cox regression, simple prognostic scoring, ROC. Achievable: low-cost dementia-risk triage in memory clinics.

Method_Architecture: Voxel-based morphometry; SVM classification (SVMst structure-only; SVMcog +MMSE); ADNI half training/half validation; external test on AIBL, Japanese ADNI, MIDIAD, OASIS; radiologist comparison.
Best_Metric: AD diagnostic accuracy 90.5% (SVMst) vs radiologists 57.5-70%; MCI progression prediction 83-85% (SVMst/SVMcog 83-85%); external test accuracy 92.5-100%.
Dataset: ADNI (train/validation) + external AIBL, Japanese ADNI, MIDIAD, OASIS
Key_Novelty: VBM+SVM BAAD outperforms expert radiologists for AD diagnosis; validated on 4 external datasets
Primary_Limitation: ADNI-centred training with moderate MCI progression prediction accuracy (83-85%); no fluid-biomarker integration.
Open_Problems: Open: generalisability to community MRI and diverse populations. Applications: clinical decision support for AD diagnosis and MCI triage. Methodologies: VBM, SVM, radiologist comparison. Achievable: routine imaging-based AD/MCI screening support.
Journal: Frontiers in Neurology 11: 576029, 2021 (Frontiers Media, open access)

Method_Architecture: Narrative review of pharmacologic, non-pharmacologic and surgical treatments for PD-MCI/PDD; evidence grading; no primary data.
Best_Metric: No effective treatment for PD-MCI; rivastigmine only recommended PDD therapy; exercise shows growing support; most repurposed/novel therapies insufficiently evidenced.
Dataset: Not applicable (narrative review)
Key_Novelty: Evidence-graded PD-MCI/PDD treatment map; only rivastigmine recommended, no effective PD-MCI therapy
Primary_Limitation: Narrative (non-systematic) review without quantitative evidence synthesis or risk-of-bias assessment.
Open_Problems: Open: disease-modifying therapy; biomarkers for trial enrichment. Applications: clinical treatment decisions for PD cognitive impairment. Methodologies: pharmacologic, non-pharmacologic, surgical interventions. Achievable: evidence-based PD-MCI/PDD treatment guidance.

Method_Architecture: ASL perfusion MRI; regional CBF group comparisons; stepwise logistic regression with leave-one-out cross-validation; Cox survival models; partial volume correction.
Best_Metric: Stepwise logistic model predicting MCI-to-AD conversion with 93% accuracy (2-3 year follow-up; 83-92% at 4-7 years); baseline PCC/BSMF rCBF predicted 3MSE.
Dataset: Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS) Cognition Study cohort, USA (2002-2013)
Key_Novelty: First longitudinal ASL study of NC-MCI-AD with baseline-rCBF conversion prediction (93%)
Primary_Limitation: Small sample with prediction effects not robust to FWE correction; no amyloid/tau biomarker integration.
Open_Problems: Open: external replication and FWE-stable endpoints. Applications: non-invasive screening of MCI-to-AD risk. Methodologies: ASL rCBF, logistic/Cox prediction, PVC. Achievable: perfusion-based conversion risk assessment in memory clinics.

Modality: CSF amyloid-beta/tau (AT(N)); MRI hippocampal volume, cortical thickness
Method_Architecture: CSF amyloid/tau assays; MRI hippocampal volumetry and cortical thickness; AT(N) classification; cross-sectional and longitudinal cognitive/imaging comparisons (mixed-effects models).
Best_Metric: Group comparison: mismatch A+T-(N+) MCI milder, slower-declining than prodromal AD; MTL-restricted cortical thinning; slower MTL volume loss.
Dataset: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI)
Sample_N_Approx: 401 MCI AT(N)-classified (176 analysed: 44 mismatch, 84 prodromal AD, 48 neurodegeneration-only) + 161 A- CN
Key_Novelty: Longitudinal AT(N): A+T-(N+) mismatch MCI is non-AD-like, milder, slower than prodromal AD
Primary_Limitation: Biomarker-only AT(N) with no histopathologic confirmation of non-AD pathology; modest mismatch subgroup.
Open_Problems: Open: identifying the specific non-AD pathologies driving mismatch MCI. Applications: trial enrichment stratification; prognostic counselling. Methodologies: AT(N) CSF/MRI classification, longitudinal mixed models. Achievable: biomarker-guided MCI subtyping in clinical research.

Method_Architecture: Untargeted plasma metabolomics; LASSO/SVM/random forest feature selection; random forest classification with fivefold cross-validation; ROC analysis.
Best_Metric: RF fivefold-CV accuracy 80.3% (P-MCI vs S-MCI); 73.5% three-group accuracy; eight-metabolite index AUC 0.96; indole-3-propionic acid predictor.
Dataset: Taipei Veterans General Hospital cohort, Taiwan (own single-centre data)
Sample_N_Approx: 48 MCI patients (19 P-MCI, 29 S-MCI) plus AD comparison group
Key_Novelty: ML-derived 20-metabolite plasma signature; indole-3-propionic acid predicts MCI-to-AD conversion
Primary_Limitation: Small single-centre cohort without external validation; gut-microbiota role inferred from metabolites, not directly measured.
Open_Problems: Open: confirmation of gut-microbiota mediation and multi-centre generalisability. Applications: MCI-to-AD risk stratification; metabolomics-based monitoring. Methodologies: untargeted metabolomics, LASSO/SVM/RF feature selection, fivefold CV. Achievable: plasma metabolite panels for AD conversion risk in clinics.
Journal: International Journal of Molecular Sciences 22(20): 10903, 2021 (MDPI, open access)

Modality: PRS from blood GWAS genotypes (ADNI European-ancestry subset)
Method_Architecture: PLINK QC + PRS computation, Cox regression, APOE e4 interaction analysis
Best_Metric: HR 1.468 (95% CI 1.335-1.615) for PRS+APOE on MCI-to-dementia conversion
Dataset: ADNI
Key_Novelty: APOE e4-stratified PRS conversion prediction: stronger genetic signal in e4 non-carriers
Primary_Limitation: ADNI-only with no external replication cohort; European ancestry restriction limits generalisability; modest PRS effect in e4 carriers.
Open_Problems: External replication in diverse non-European cohorts; standardisation of PRS construction (GWAS weights, APOE handling) across studies.

Modality: Neuron-derived exosomal proteomics from peripheral blood (TMT)
Method_Architecture: TMT-based quantitative proteomics, fuzzy c-means clustering, differential expression
Best_Metric: Descriptive: 360 exosomal proteins; C7/ZYX candidate markers
Dataset: Shenzhen cohort (China)
Key_Novelty: C7 and ZYX proposed as novel neuron-derived exosomal protein markers of NC-MCI-AD progression
Primary_Limitation: Very small single-centre discovery cohort (n=15) with no independent validation or quantitative assay-level confirmation.
Open_Problems: Independent validation in larger cohorts; candidate-based assay confirmation (ELISA/Simoa) of C7 and ZYX; correlation with CSF and neuroimaging markers.
Journal: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 13: 696944, 2021 (Frontiers Media, open access)

Modality: PRS from blood GWAS genotypes (40 non-APOE SNPs); CSF/PET/MRI readouts
Method_Architecture: PRS construction, survival/proportional-hazards regression, longitudinal cognition, mediation analysis
Best_Metric: beta 0.182 (SE 0.061, p=0.003) ADNI; replicated beta 0.094 (SE 0.037, p=0.009) NACC
Dataset: ADNI (767 MCI) + NACC (1373 MCI)
Key_Novelty: 40-SNP non-APOE PRS: MCI-to-AD survival + biomarker changes; NACC replication; Abeta42 mediation
Primary_Limitation: Modest effect sizes; European-ancestry discovery/replication cohorts; non-APOE SNP panel only.
Open_Problems: APOE-aware scoring, diverse population validation, integration of PRS with fluid/imaging biomarkers into a combined risk tool.

Modality: Olfactory identification test x hippocampal volumetry (MRI), meta-analysis
Method_Architecture: Systematic search + NOS quality scoring, pooled correlation (r) with moderator analysis
Best_Metric: Pooled r = 0.3392 (95% CI 0.2335-0.4370) olfactory-test x hippocampal-volume
Dataset: Pooled literature (7 studies, n=902)
Key_Novelty: First pooled r 0.34: olfactory-test x hippocampal-volume correlation stronger in AD/MCI than NC
Primary_Limitation: Only 7 studies; small pooled n; correlation magnitude modest; no publication-bias analysis reported.
Open_Problems: Standardised olfactory protocols and volumetric pipelines; longitudinal studies; combining olfactory tests with other non-invasive markers in diagnostic models.
Journal: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 13: 755160, 2021 (Frontiers Media, open access)

Method_Architecture: Structured review with qualitative-quantitative synthesis (3 databases, 1990-2021)
Best_Metric: Directional: CSF YKL-40 higher in AD vs controls/MCI-AD/stable MCI; higher in MCI-AD vs stable MCI
Dataset: Literature review (PubMed/Web of Science/Cochrane 1990-2021)
Key_Novelty: CSF YKL-40 as neuroinflammation marker for AD-vs-MCI differential diagnosis and MCI-to-AD prognosis
Primary_Limitation: Narrative review without formal meta-analysis; heterogeneous assays; YKL-40 lacks AD specificity.
Open_Problems: Formal meta-analysis with harmonised assays; combination with amyloid/tau markers; longitudinal validation of MCI-to-AD predictive value.

Method_Architecture: Systematic review; miRNA-expression synthesis across 30 studies, target-gene mapping
Best_Metric: Qualitative candidate set: 5 peripheral-fluid miRNA profiles across 30 studies
Dataset: Literature (30 articles on MCI peripheral-fluid miRNAs)
Key_Novelty: 30 studies / 5 peripheral-fluid miRNA profiles -> candidate early-MCI biomarker landscape
Primary_Limitation: No quantitative pooling; heterogeneous platforms and normalisation; candidates not yet validated in independent cohorts.
Open_Problems: Consensus normalisation and reporting standards; independent replication cohorts; functional validation of miRNA-target relationships.
Journal: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 13: 807764, 2022 (Frontiers Media, open access)

Modality: Structural MRI regional radiomics similarity networks (R2SN)
Method_Architecture: Regional radiomics, individual similarity networks, NMF clustering, gene-enrichment analysis
Best_Metric: 3-year progression: 61.54% (A-CI) vs 21.77% (N-CI)
Dataset: ADNI
Key_Novelty: R2SN+NMF MCI subtyping: A-CI 61.5% vs N-CI 21.8% 3-year progression, distinct gene enrichment
Primary_Limitation: ADNI-only without external validation; anchor-group dependent clustering; no CSF/biomarker integration.
Open_Problems: External cohort validation of the two R2SN subtypes; integration with CSF/tau biomarkers; longitudinal design across longer horizons.

Modality: Clinical/demographic (age, APOE e4, MMSE, CDR; tabular)
Method_Architecture: Multivariable Cox proportional hazards, sex-stratified risk scoring, ROC cutoff, external validation
Best_Metric: C-statistics 0.902 (F)/0.911 (M) ADNI; 0.950 (F)/0.965 (M) HABS external
Dataset: ADNI (derivation) + HABS (external validation)
Key_Novelty: Sex-specific CN-to-MCI risk score (age, APOE e4, MMSE, CDR); external C-stat 0.95-0.97
Primary_Limitation: ADNI-derived with a single external cohort (HABS); no fluid/imaging biomarkers; population calibration needs further testing.
Open_Problems: Broader external cohorts; inclusion of fluid/imaging biomarkers to raise prediction beyond four clinical variables; calibration studies in real-world clinics.
Journal: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 13: 774804, 2022 (Frontiers Media, open access)

Modality: Neurofilament light chain in CSF and blood
Method_Architecture: Random-effects meta-analysis (SMD pooling), subgroup by sample type and assay
Best_Metric: CSF NfL SMD significant MCI-vs-controls; blood NfL not significant
Dataset: Pooled literature (7 studies; PubMed/Embase/WoS)
Key_Novelty: CSF NfL (not blood) differentiates MCI; ELISA yes, Simoa no - assay-stratified meta-analysis
Primary_Limitation: Only 7 studies; blood subgroup not significant; assay heterogeneity; no publication-bias analysis.
Open_Problems: More blood-NfL studies using sensitive assays with harmonised protocols; larger CSF-NfL datasets; longitudinal diagnosis/prognosis outcomes.

Modality: Serum cholesterol profile (TC, LDL-C, HDL-C) + PVRL2 rs6859 SNP
Method_Architecture: Prospective cohort, Cox regression (HR, FDR), gene x lipid interaction, categorical trend test
Best_Metric: Adjusted HR 2.75 (95% CI 1.32-5.76) rs6859 AG/AA vs GG on MCI-to-AD; LDL-C interaction HR 0.52 per mmol/L
Dataset: Shanghai Aging Study sub-cohort (China)
Key_Novelty: PVRL2 rs6859 x LDL-C: risk-allele carriers get 48% per-mmol/L LDL-C protection on MCI-to-AD
Primary_Limitation: Single Chinese cohort without replication; moderate sample and small genotype subgroups; observational design.
Open_Problems: Replication in independent cohorts; larger carrier subgroups; mechanistic studies of PVRL2 function; longer follow-up with repeated lipid measures.
Journal: Frontiers in Genetics 13: 823406, 2022 (Frontiers Media, open access)

Modality: Plasma p-tau217 (+NfL, GFAP, Abeta42/40), hippocampal volume, APOE genotype, mPACC cognitive composite
Method_Architecture: Multi-model logistic regression (AICc-based selection), DeLong AUC comparison, sensitivity analyses adding demographics
Best_Metric: AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.82-0.95) full model (p-tau217+hippocampus+mPACC+APOE); AUC 0.84 p-tau217 alone; parsimonious AUC 0.87
Dataset: Flutemetamol PET clinical trial cohort (NCT01028053; Lund/Skane, Sweden)
Key_Novelty: Plasma p-tau217 + mPACC cognition parsimoniously predict MCI-to-AD dementia (AUC 0.87-0.89)
Primary_Limitation: Single cohort without external replication; partial plasma panel (80/110); amnestic MCI only.
Open_Problems: External replication in independent cohorts; mass-spectrometry Abeta42/40; plasma-CSF p-tau concordance; non-amnestic MCI generalisation.
Journal: Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 14: 46, 2022 (BMC/Springer Nature, open access)

Modality: Blood-plasma gene expression (Affymetrix Human Genome U219 microarray, 49,386 probes)
Method_Architecture: Chi-square rank-based feature selection with 10-fold CV, random forest classification, intersection of StableMCI and Progression probes
Best_Metric: AUC 0.841 (10-CV)/0.775 (test); external StableMCI-1y 0.832, StableMCI-3y 0.765
Dataset: ADNI plasma gene-expression database
Key_Novelty: 31-probe (29-gene) plasma-gene RF classifier: stable-MCI CV AUC 0.841, test 0.775
Primary_Limitation: ADNI-only derivation without external multi-centre validation; unknown biological role of ~13 biomarker genes.
Open_Problems: Biological validation of unstudied genes; larger and more comprehensive datasets; advanced algorithms (XGBoost); external prospective validation.
Journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 19(8): 4839, 2022 (MDPI, open access)

Modality: Circulating blood miRNA triad (miR-181a-5p, miR-146a-5p, miR-148a-3p); commentary on Islam et al. 2021
Method_Architecture: Commentary synthesis: mouse ageing/APP-PS1 models, neuronal/microglial cell culture, blood miRNA measurement, in-vivo triad inhibition
Best_Metric: not reported
Dataset: Not applicable (commentary on Islam et al. 2021 EMBO Mol Med)
Key_Novelty: Commentary: blood miRNA triad (181a-5p/146a-5p/148a-3p) flags MCI/AD and is a candidate target
Primary_Limitation: No primary data; triad specificity across comorbid cancers/osteoarthritis/obesity unvalidated.
Open_Problems: Specificity across comorbidities; standardised elevation thresholds; safety of systemic inhibition; brain-specific delivery approaches.

Modality: Plasma p-tau217 (Janssen Simoa vs Lilly MSD); CSF Abeta42/40; amyloid-PET
Method_Architecture: Head-to-head assay comparison: ROC/DeLong AUC, Youden cut-points, Spearman correlations, Bland-Altman agreement, general linear and mixed-effects models
Best_Metric: AUC 0.88 (Janssen)/0.89 (Lilly) MCI-to-AD; 0.91 both assays MCI vs controls
Dataset: Swedish BioFINDER study (cohort 1) + Skane University Hospital Malmo Memory Clinic (cohort 2)
Sample_N_Approx: 199 (cohort 1: 52 - 27 CU + 25 MCI; cohort 2: 147 MCI follow-up avg 4.92 yrs)
Key_Novelty: Head-to-head: novel Simoa p-tau217+Janssen matches Lilly assay for Abeta detection and MCI-to-AD prognosis
Primary_Limitation: Both Swedish cohorts; moderate plasma cross-assay correlation (~0.70); small cohort 1; no tau-PET comparison.
Open_Problems: Cross-assay standardisation; matrix-interference/epitope analyses; larger multi-ethnic cohorts; tau-PET comparisons.
Journal: Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 14: 67, 2022 (BMC/Springer Nature, open access)

Modality: CSF NfL (plus CSF Abeta42/T-tau/P-tau ATN staging; PET amyloid)
Method_Architecture: Prospective AIBL cohort; ATN biomarker classification; ROC (Youden cut-off); Cox proportional hazards; Kaplan-Meier; mixed linear models for longitudinal cognition
Best_Metric: HR 4.77 (95% CI 1.31-17.29) CSF NfL >674 pg/mL on CH dementia onset; HR 1.60 continuous; AUC 0.79 preclinical AD screen
Dataset: Australian Imaging, Biomarkers and Lifestyle (AIBL) study, Australia
Sample_N_Approx: 186 (154 CH + 32 MCI); 124 CH for dementia-onset analysis
Key_Novelty: CSF NfL predicts CH dementia onset (HR 4.77) and stratifies MCI decline rate in AIBL
Primary_Limitation: Very small MCI sample (n=32); median dichotomisation; possible risk overestimation; no external replication.
Open_Problems: Larger cohorts with tertile/quartile stratification; CH-to-MCI and MCI-to-AD prediction; plasma NfL translation for clinical use.

Modality: Disease clusters, blood biochemistry (WBC, platelets, Na, TSH), cognitive status
Method_Architecture: Multicentre population cohort; hierarchical disease clustering; multivariable logistic regression (models A/B) with stepwise selection
Best_Metric: OR 4.0 (1.06-14.93) hypertension/bone-joint cluster PCH-to-MCI; OR 4.2 low WBC and OR 1.5 disease count MCI-to-dementia; OR 7.3 Na and OR 3.6 TSH for reversion
Dataset: Multicentre Italian population-based cohort (Brescia, Schio-Vicenza, Bologna, Fermo-Ascoli Piceno)
Key_Novelty: Hypertension/bone-joint cluster and low WBC predict MCI progression; Na/TSH predict MCI reversion
Primary_Limitation: Short 1-year follow-up; small subgroups; no dementia-type diagnosis; no FT3/FT4 measures.
Open_Problems: Longer observation; complete follow-up data; thyroid hormone (FT3/FT4) measurement; larger MCI subgroups; dementia-type outcomes.
Journal: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 14: 876359, 2022 (Frontiers Media, open access)

Modality: Blood genetics (EAA-related SNPs/PRS), CSF biomarkers, MRI volumes
Method_Architecture: GWAS genetic correlation/LDAK heritability; Cox single-locus survival with BFDP; LD clumping + survival LASSO; PRSICE-2 PRS; linear mixed models
Best_Metric: EEAA-PRS associated with shorter MCI-to-AD progression (p=.036 ADNI / p=.003 NACC); Harrell's C 0.641 without significant gain
Dataset: ADNI (767 MCI, discovery) + NACC (1373 MCI, replication)
Key_Novelty: EAA-related SNPs/PRS: EEAA-PRS replicates on MCI-to-AD progression; shared genetic architecture with AD
Primary_Limitation: No FDR-significant single SNP; European-ancestry cohorts; EAA PRS adds no significant predictive accuracy.
Open_Problems: Multi-ancestry validation; causal/mechanistic studies; integration with fluid/imaging biomarkers and other omics for prediction.
Journal: Journal of Gerontology: Biological Sciences 77(9): 1734-1742, 2022 (Oxford University Press)

Method_Architecture: Retrospective cohort; ANCOVA on regional SUVRs; time-dependent ROC with stepwise backward elimination; DeLong; ADNI replication
Best_Metric: AUC 0.762 left parietal SUVR; combined precuneus+parietal+composite AUC 0.763 conversion prediction
Dataset: Asan Medical Center (Seoul, Korea) cohort + ADNI UC Berkeley florbetaben subset
Sample_N_Approx: 103 amyloid-negative amnestic MCI (39 converters) + 48 ADNI (11 progressors)
Key_Novelty: Subthreshold regional FBB SUVR predicts dementia conversion in visually amyloid-negative aMCI
Primary_Limitation: Retrospective single-centre design; no tau/TDP-43/alpha-synuclein measures; possible selection bias; no follow-up PET.
Open_Problems: Follow-up PET threshold verification; combined-pathology models; post-mortem confirmation; prospective design with complete neuropsychological follow-up.
